items.statement: FY26 volume growth guidance 10-15% and EBITDA spread INR 4,600-5,000 per ton
items.quote: Now first half into financial year of '26, we are fairly confident that we will be able to meet our guidance, which we gave in the quarter 1 call, which was 10% to 15% volume growth and EBITDA spread of INR 4,600 to INR 5,000 per ton.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 volume target 9 lakh tons, Q4 FY26 target 9.2-9.5 lakh tons with EBITDA ~INR 5,000/ton
items.value: 9 lakh tons Q3; 9.2-9.5 lakh tons Q4; ~INR 5,000/ton EBITDA
items.quote: Now, I understand it in my language, the target of 9 lakh tons will be Q3, the target of 9.2-9.5 lakh tons will be Q4. In that, the EBITDA of around INR 5,000 is INR450-INR450, INR900 crores, and INR 800 crores has come, so INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA target INR 1,700 crores
items.quote: And almost INR 1700 crores EBITDA target that we have taken, we will definitely beat that.

items.statement: INR 1,500 crores capex for 7 million ton capacity expansion over 2-3 years, 100% funded from internal cash flows
items.quote: 100% will be funded from internal cash flows. If you look at our operating cash flow to EBITDA, that's like above 90%. So this will help us to fund 100% of capex, so.

items.statement: Current capacity 5 million tons, adding 7 million tons (6M India, 1M Middle East) over 2-3 years; Raipur 1.5M tons, Dubai expanding to 500k tons
items.quote: Right now, we are close to a capacity of 5 million tons; and in the last 2 or 3 years, we are going to build up the capacity of further 7 million tons. Out of 7 million tons, there is 1 million ton capacity in Middle East.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 70% overall; Raipur ~65-70%, Dubai ~80-85% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We are right now 5 million ton capacity. We are going to do this year 3.5 million tons, so 70% capacity utilization we are running.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA spread INR 5,200/ton, up INR 500/ton QoQ from brand premiumization, operating leverage, value-added mix
items.quote: So this is the breakup of INR500 per ton improvement in EBITDA.

items.statement: General category EBITDA spread doubled to INR 3,400/ton in last 2-3 quarters after Jan 2025 price hike of INR 2,000-3,000/ton
items.quote: Number one was the brand power of APL Apollo, which we are able to demonstrate in the EBITDA spreads of general category, which have almost doubled to INR3,400 per ton in last 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA spread target INR 6,000/ton blended over next 4-5 years
items.quote: And the next four, five years, definitely, the trajectory could be from INR5,000 to INR6,000 per ton.

items.statement: Steel price changes 100% passed through to NSR; GP/ton improvement driven by value-added mix not inventory gains
items.quote: Now for example, if you look at Q1 versus Q2, our NSR declined by INR5,000 per ton and the steel -- our raw material cost also came down by a similar level.

items.statement: Value-added mix improvement from Raipur and Dubai plants (EBITDA >INR 5,500-6,000/ton); new 1000x1000mm mill and capsule roofing products
items.quote: Second reason for margin expansion was the value-added mix improvement, which is mainly coming from our Dubai and Raipur plant, where the EBITDA per ton on -- for these plants is above INR5,500, INR6,000 per ton.

items.statement: SG Premium brand launched at ~10-15k tons/month to compete with secondary steel; EBITDA near breakeven on this brand
items.quote: Today, Apollo is higher than almost with all the other brands, INR3,000 minimum or maybe maximum INR 5,000 to INR 6,000 per ton. Apollo product is costly in the market.

items.statement: No demand boost seen yet; H1 FY26 weak due to monsoon, holidays, steel price decline; expect H2 better as monsoons over and channel empty
items.quote: Very frankly, I am saying that we are not seeing any boost up in demand. But due to our brand leverage, due to our size, due to our systems, we are sustainable.

items.statement: Steel prices downtrend ended in October; channel inventory empty so restocking demand expected from November
items.quote: Now in October it seems that the downward trend has ended. If it doesn't increase from November then it won't decrease either. So the channel is completely empty so the demand should pick up.

items.statement: 12% safeguard duty on HRC imports supports domestic prices; import parity at INR 52-53k/ton vs domestic INR 46k/ton
items.quote: Yes, 100% you are correct. Like right now, the HR coil for the month of October is close to INR46,000 per ton landed Ghazi abad or anywhere in the country, or if we do any import wit h the duties, it cost us to INR52,000 or INR 53,000 per

items.statement: Working capital days at 0 as of September 2025; ROCE >32% sustainable
items.quote: Lastly, on working capital front, our working capital days remain in single digit, in fact, 0 as at September 2025, which boosted our ROCE upward of 32%, 33%.

items.statement: No external debt for capex; 100% internal funding; focus on reducing payables to get supplier discounts
items.quote: First, our strategy is to remove the liabilities from the book and get some more discounts from the suppliers.

items.statement: Excess cash after capex and dividends to be used for higher dividends or buybacks; not kept as FDs
items.quote: The remaining money is a good problem to solve. We will increase dividends or buy back. We will do something. Keeping in company -- we will not make an FD.

items.statement: Dubai plant 8% of volume; opening warehouses in Liverpool and Antwerp to improve service and increase EBITDA spread by EUR 50/ton
items.quote: We are already supplying from Dubai. But if we open a warehouse there and make the service better, then we think that our EBITDA spread should increase by EUR50.

items.statement: Freight cost target reduction from INR 1,900/ton to INR 1,500/ton; salary cost target from INR 950/ton to INR 600/ton at 5M tons volume
items.quote: We are targeting to bring it to INR1,500 per ton. And number three on the front of our salary cost. We are targeting that today our salary is 5 million per ton. Minimum wages should increase. Nothing much will increase. So as soon as we achieve 5 million per ton then that cost will also increase a lot. Which is now running around INR950. My target is to bring down to INR600 per ton.

items.statement: Not focused on competitors; lowest cost producer globally; new capacity in new markets/products not competing with existing players
items.quote: We don't pay much attention to the competitor to be frank. We are working on our own strategy on how we have to do. We are going in a new area and we are not building up any capacity in our competitive items.

items.statement: Key risk is further GDP deterioration from current levels; no significant downside if demand stable
items.quote: Except further deterioration in GDP from existing levels.

items.statement: Pre-galvanized pipe volume 2 lakh tons/quarter (Coast Guard pipe category)
items.quote: 2 lakh ton is the sale of our quarter. Chetan Khandelwal: The product break-up that you will see in our presentation, the Coast Guard pipe in it, all that is pre

items.statement: Salary cost per ton to decrease from INR 950 to INR 600 as volume scales to 5M tons; minimum wage increases expected
items.quote: We are targeting that today our salary is 5 million per ton. Minimum wages should increase. Nothing much will increase. So as soon as we achieve 5 million per ton then that cost will also increase a lot. Which is now running around INR950. My target is to bring down to INR600 per ton.

items.statement: Long-term volume target 10 million tons; structural steel tube market 10% CAGR to 2030; conversion from secondary to primary steel key driver
items.quote: Most market is already there. But in India, there is the biggest problem there is a one secondary material is there, which is a very low quality material and it has a low cost. So, people are very much worried about the brand, about good material. So, as soon as the market is over, then 10 million tons will reach very easily.

items.statement: White space cost reduction target of ~95% by September 2026
items.quote: we remain committed to our target, which I had shared last time in the call that by September of next year we will reduce our white space cost by about 95%.

items.statement: White space reduced by over 20% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: I'm pleased to share with you that we have, in the last quarter alone, achieved a reduction of 20% plus of our white space in the last quarter.

items.statement: Express business turned gross margin positive for first time at 0.2% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: This is our first GM positive quarter with 0.2% gross margin as compared to minus 5.2% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: No new BTS warehouse space additions planned; future expansion via RTM model
items.quote: We have no plans to add in the near future any BTS space. However, if some client comes in and gives to us a back-to-back kind of a commitment, we will consider that. But broadly, expansion will happen is by RTM ready to move, where there are no long-term commitments to any landlord.

items.statement: Warehouse network fully built out; peak rental cost reached
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier in this call, we have completed most of our warehouse expansion. And so, therefore, the way I look at it is that lease cost. And therefore, the depreciation cost arising from Ind AS 116 is at its peak and fully built out in the current quarter financials.

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced from INR601 cr to INR73 cr after rights issue; INR187 cr retained for general corporate purposes
items.quote: As a result, we have reduced our consolidated debt obligation from INR601 crores at the end of quarter 1 to INR73 crores at the end of quarter 2. This will help us realize interest cost savings of INR40 crores to INR45 crores per annum.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR749 cr completed in August 2025; proceeds used for debt repayment
items.quote: let me share an update on the successful completion of our rights issue of INR749 crores in August 2025. The proceeds have been prudently utilized towards the repayment of debt, resulting in a stronger balance sheet.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin expanded to 10.1% in Q2 FY26 from 9.2% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated gross margin is at 10.1% in Q2 FY26 compared to 9.2% in Q2 FY25, driven by more favorable business mix, customer mix as well as volume leverage.

items.statement: Festive demand strong; grocery fulfilment center handled 8.2 lakh units in a single day
items.quote: For example, one of our grocery fulfilment center, I don't want to mahindra share the name of our customer. We handled 8.2 lakh units in a single day. This is our best ever, 8.2 lakh units in a single day from one site

items.statement: Key customer expansions from Cummins, Bosch, Amazon, Flipkart, Mahindra
items.quote: Also, repeat expansion projects from key customers such as Cummins, Bosch, Amazon, Flipkart, Mahindra, etcetera, reflect our robust customer partnership and strong execution capabilities.

items.statement: Express tonnage grew 7% YoY; yield improved by ~INR0.90 per kg year-to-date
items.quote: Our tonnage has improved 7% Y-o-Y and our share of Value-Added Services, which we call VAS has also improved.

items.statement: Last-mile pricing pressure persists; strategic customer mix decisions taken
items.quote: customer-driven pricing pressure continues to be a concern in last-mile delivery, and this has led to a few strategic decisions taken by us on our customer mix.

items.statement: Launched Alyte Prive premium B2C mobility service in Delhi NCR; expansion planned for Noida International Airport
items.quote: We have launched Prive service only in the region of Delhi NCR, and we have expansion plans now for Noida International Airport. There is a lot of growth that can be achieved in NCR, and we will keep the Prive focus on NCR for the whole of next year.

items.statement: INR50 cr equity infusion into MESPL to support journey to EBITDA positive
items.quote: Further, MLL is infusing additional equity capital of INR50 crores in MESPL to support in its journey to become EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Express PAT loss narrowed to INR20 cr from INR24 cr YoY; gross margin improvement flowing to PAT
items.quote: We have a PAT loss of INR20 crores in Q2 FY26 compared to INR24 crores in Q2 FY25. The improvement in gross margin is flowing down to PAT as well. We have improved gross margin by about INR5 crores, and you will see about INR4 crores improvement in the PAT.

items.statement: One-time PDD charge of INR4.8 cr for bankrupt 3PL customer
items.quote: During the quarter, we have recognized a onetime charge of INR4.8 crores under Provisions for Doubtful Debts or PDD arising from the bankruptcy filing of one of our 3PL customers.

items.statement: GST rate cuts positive for economy; e-way bill growth supports domestic resilience
items.quote: increasing domestic resilience, which is evident in the growth of e-way bills supported by GST cuts, very, very positive for overall economy

items.statement: Express market share maintained; focus on high-yield loads over volume
items.quote: No, we have not gained market share if that's what you mean. Achal: Yes. Hemant Sikka: I think there our improvement is on a very thought through strategy of improving our customer mix and that is helping us to improve our yield per kg

items.statement: Isha Dalal joined as new CFO with 15+ years experience across media, IB, PE, corporate finance
items.quote: I would like to extend a warm welcome to Ms. Isha Dalal as she joined us for her maiden earnings call in the capacity of Chief Financial Officer of Mahindra Logistics Limited. Ms. Isha has over 15 years of diverse experience spanning media, investment banking, private equity and corporate finance.

items.statement: PDD provision reflects prudent accounting for credit exposure on outstanding receivables
items.quote: This adjustment was undertaken as a prudent accounting measure to reflect potential credit exposure on our outstanding receivables.

items.statement: Freight forwarding volumes grew 9% YoY despite global headwinds
items.quote: Overall volumes grew by 9% Y-o-Y despite, as we all know, there are very strong global challenges, headwinds because of global tariffs and geopolitical challenges. Still, our cross-border business has done exceedingly well, growing by 9% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Depreciation of INR72 cr (mostly Ind AS 116 lease cost) at peak; expected to stay stable quarterly
items.quote: So the depreciation cost of the INR72 crores that we see in our consolidated P&L, actually, most of it belongs to the cost of the leases under Ind AS 116. And most of the year-on-year increase of the INR18 crores that you see also belongs to the impact of leases under Ind AS 116.

items.statement: Warehousing revenue up 20% YoY to INR333 cr driven by new sites and volume ramp-up
items.quote: Revenue from the warehousing segment stands at INR333 crores as compared to INR278 crores in Q2 FY25. That's up by approximately 20%, driven by the addition of new sites and the volume ramp-up in our existing sites.

items.statement: Infrastructure push and e-commerce/quick commerce expansion positive for coming quarters
items.quote: Further infrastructure push and rapid expansion of e-commerce and quick commerce have set a very positive tone for us in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Global tariff and geopolitical challenges create cross-border headwinds
items.quote: We continue to face headwinds like global uncertainty, cross-border price volatility and elevated input cost on the cross-border side.

items.statement: Operationalized 8 new projects across manufacturing and e-commerce; launched 3 lakh sq ft facility in Nashik
items.quote: Happy to share that we have operationalized 8 new projects across manufacturing and e-commerce and launched a 3 lakh square foot facility in Nashik.

items.statement: MD Dr. Prasada Raju resigned for personal priorities; will stay for transition through FY25
items.quote: Dr. Prasada Raju will be stepping down from his role as Managing Director of Cohance. Dr. Prasad a Raju has resigned from his position considering his personal priorities and to continue his learning journey. Prasad will remain associated with the company to orderly transition for an extended period ending this fiscal

items.statement: Board approved new org structure with three business CEOs reporting to Executive Chairman; platform COO joining shortly
items.quote: The board has approved a revised organizational structure, one that better reflects our multi- business portfolio and expanding global footprint and positions Cohance strongly on its path towards a $1 billion U.S. vision. This new structure is designed to bring greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability across our businesses.

items.statement: CFO Himanshu Agarwal appointed to board as director
items.quote: Additionally, I am pleased to share our CFO, Mr. Himanshu Agarwal will be joining the company's board as director, ensuring continuity and alignment across leadership and governance levels.

items.statement: Platform COO to join in next few weeks; based in Hyderabad with 30+ years experience
items.quote: We will also be welcoming a platform COO shortly, a seasoned industry leader who will be based out of Hyderabad. A techno- commercial professional with over three decades of experience, he brings a strong blend of operational excellence and on-the-ground project execution.

items.statement: Reaffirmed US$1 billion revenue vision by 2030 with significant CDMO contribution
items.quote: Our vision of a US$1 billion business by 2030 remains there. We are committed to reach there. And as part of that, we're bringing in more global leaders, more talent that can help us reach there faster and improve our chances of reaching there.

items.statement: RFP pipeline becoming more robust with strengthened BD team and commercial infrastructure
items.quote: Our RFP pipelines, which, you know, with the addition of a BD team and all these investments we've been making in commercial infrastructure is becoming more and more robust.

items.statement: Oligonucleotide unit at Nacharam completed equipment validation; on track for Q4 commissioning
items.quote: Surya, our oligonucleotide unit, has successfully completed equipment validation and remains on track for commissioning in Q4, marking another important milestone in expanding our advanced therapy capabilities.

items.statement: Nacharam FTF unit received OAI classification; appointing US and Indian consulting firms for remediation; business <1% of EBITDA
items.quote: OI classification of our Nacharam FTF unit, which we updated to the stock exchange last week, we are in the process of appointing a leading U.S. FTA consulting firm to also help us in addition to an Indian firm to guide us through the remediation process. We're working proactively with external experts to address observations and engage with the agency in the best possible manner. However, as we h

items.statement: R&D leadership transitioned internally with Dr. Somesh and Dr. Ashok; ADC and Oligo expansion adding R&D headcount
items.quote: have a new head of R&D for the CDMO business. We actually have two senior guys who joined us in the last one year. They've taken over as the head of R&D, Dr. Somesh and Dr. Ashok. Both were in the system and they are now running the R&D, including t he ADCPs for the business. On R&D part, we've also added the ADC segment with NJ Bio expansion. We have not seen, except for one or two changes at the

items.statement: Senior leadership stabilization expected; more talent added than lost; internal promotion pipeline emphasized
items.quote: I expect at the senior level we are reaching that phase of stabilization. Now, as we continue to expand, as we have just hired a Chief Operating Officer for the CDMO business who joined us about three weeks ago, as we continue to expand and as we continue, there might be changes and upgrades that you might see at different positions. But at the senior level, my hope is that we are reaching that po

items.statement: Aggressively pursuing inorganic opportunities with in-house M&A team; focus on niche tech capabilities for CDMO
items.quote: On your second question, in terms of the non -- the inorganic growth, we are aggressively committed. We actually have in -house M&A team of two people that is very experienced. We are aggressively looking at opportunities all the time, and as we are talking, there are some discussions going on. These are, again, focusing on our strategic direction that we said that we want to be a key CDMO player

items.statement: M&A funding primarily through internal resources; open to borrowing if needed; target cash positive at strategy period end
items.quote: Our plan is to fund everything with internal funding. If required, we can borrow money, but right now we're looking at everything with internal funding. Our idea is to remain cash positive and then just leverage our internal resources and the kind of opportunities in the capital structure we are looking at for equity structure aligns with our vision that should be just with internal funding and mi

items.statement: New hires may cause short-term cost overlap; running Lean Six Sigma cost optimization programs; committed to prior guidance
items.quote: there is cost involved with the new people that are coming in and there will be some overlap also, because when new people come in, old is there. So, sometimes there will be a timing difference and some of these things. However, we are also very cautious of cost and looking at every single opportunity to optimize cost. We have some internal programs that we are running on Lean Six Sigma. We have a

items.statement: Biosecure Act progress positive for India CDMO; companies pursuing China-free strategies regardless of legislation
items.quote: Listen, people are moving towards figuring out a China-free strategy. I think that trend, irrespective of biosecure, I think companies are trying. However, the pace at whi ch they move depends on company -to-company. Indian companies will definitely continue to benefit. Now, the Act, as you know, is still being reviewed and it's not fully passed, but it's a step in the right direction

items.statement: M&A targeting differentiated assets in ADC, oligonucleotide and other niche tech modalities; capability-focused not capacity-focused
items.quote: So, idea is to look for capabilities, not capacities. ADC, we have an East capability. We have a West capability. Oligo, we have an Eastern capability. You know, if we find something in the west, then Oligo will be happy, but we are looking at assets that are profitable, that bring unique capabilities to our portfolio. And they are all part of niche tax, s omething with niche capability

items.statement: FY26 credit growth guidance 14-15%, deposit growth 12-13%, CASA growth 12%
items.quote: In fact, this year, we hope to end up with 14% plus, 14% to 15% on the credit growth. And taking it further, also on the deposits, I said we will be aligned to the market, but I think we will be better than the market this quarter. I'm looking at 12% to 13% growth on the deposit and 12% on the CASA itself.

items.statement: FY27 profit growth guidance 20% plus/minus 3%
items.quote: FY '27, we have maintained will certainly be a breakout. I think it will be certainly in the round maybe 3% plus/minus 20%, right?

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilize at 3.85% plus going forward
items.quote: Like I said, when the deposit gets repriced, this will stabilize, and we expect this to be at least 3.85% plus going forward.

items.statement: ROA expected to be maintained at 1.85% going forward
items.quote: ROA continues to have a slight tick quarter-on-quarter, 1.81% in last quarter of last year to 1.82% to 1.85%. I think this is something that we hope will be maintained, 1.85% would be maintained going forward as well.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio committed to be maintained under 45% annually
items.quote: Cost-to-income ratio is at 43.81%. This has come down almost 5.5% from the previous quarter, and we are committed to maintaining it under 45% going into the next quarters.

items.statement: GNPA expected to remain in 1% range, credit cost 0.25-0.5% in FY27-28
items.quote: I still anticipate the GNPA to be in the 1% kind of range. And obviously, the credit cost would be well, well in the 0.25% to 0.5% range going into FY '27 and FY '28.

items.statement: IT budget INR250 crore for FY26 split INR125 crore capex and INR125 crore opex
items.quote: In fact, the planned investment in technology in the current year itself i s about INR250 crores, which was about INR151 crores last year

items.statement: IT modernization to continue into FY27 with similar investment levels
items.quote: No, no, no. the modernization will continue. It will. It will. We'll take a call. We'll see how things are moving. But technology is something that this bank is heavily investing in.

items.statement: Opened 22 branches in H1 FY26, plan 30-36 more in FY26, targeting >35% non-Tamil Nadu branches in 3 years
items.quote: 22 branches have been already opened in the first 6 months, and we hope to open another 30, 36 branches going forward in the current year.

items.statement: Non-Tamil Nadu branches to exceed 35% of total in next 3 years from current ~25%
items.quote: Our intention is over the next 3 years should bring down or take up the non-Tamil Nadu branches to beyond 35%.

items.statement: Advances grew 10.34% YoY, MSME grew 3.84% QoQ, RAM portfolio 94.59% of advances
items.quote: Advances momentum is aligned to the market, but the momentum is picking up. You will see that noticeable in the next 2 quarters quite substantially.

items.statement: NIM 3.83% in Q2, cost of deposits down 11 bps QoQ to 5.90%, yield on advances 9.97%
items.quote: Deposit quarter-on-quarter has moved down 11 basis 6.01% to 5.90%. Yes, and this will continue trending down as the deposit gets repriced into the new rate buckets. Cost of yield on advances at 9.97% and the net interest margin is at 3.83%.

items.statement: 66% of deposits in 1-2 year bucket repricing over next 2 quarters to offset potential 50 bps repo cut
items.quote: See, if you look at our deposit portfolio, substantially, we are in the 1- to 2-year market bucket, about 66% plus is in the 1 - to 2-year bucket. And that is now getting will be repriced going forward. The next 2 quarters going up to Apri l '26 is when this repricing will

items.statement: GNPA 1.01%, NNPA 0.26%, PCR 74.36% (95.30% with technical write-offs), slippage 5 bps, SMA 2.67%
items.quote: GNPA has shown a sharp reduction, 1.01%; net NPA at 0.26%. ROA has shown an uptick. In fact, it has been going up in the last 2, 3 quarters, and it is at 1.85%. ROE has also taken an upswing, it is 13.77%. And PCR, all this has happened without compromising on the PCR, which also has taken 132 basis points upswing with 70.36%.

items.statement: NPA collateral cover 111%, technical write-off pool ~INR2,000 crore, restructured book down to INR271 crore from INR443 crore YoY
items.quote: The other point that we would like to make here is the collateral cover of our NPA. We do have, as you have seen, INR474 crores of NPA, but it is covered to the extent of 111% by collateral.

items.statement: ECL transition requires INR210 crore additional provision (73 bps capital impact), to be funded from INR250 crore COVID contingency buffer
items.quote: We have done our calculations and we noticed that we would be requiring an additional INR210 crores of provision. This is coming in the form of additions in Stage 1 assets and Stage 2 assets. So INR210 crores provision is what we look at and that would have a 73 basis capital adequacy impact.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 30.96%, well above regulatory requirements
items.quote: On the capital adequacy, 30.96% is where we stand.

items.statement: 82-83% of staff shifted to CTC model from IBA, variable pay linked to operating profit and business growth
items.quote: About 82% of our employees today is on the CTC model. That is one major step that we took. I think going forward, we'll be getting the benefit of it. And apart from that, Now there is a variable component that we have offered them. That variable component, also now in an another major step in last month, we have aligned that to the operating profit and the business growth.

items.statement: Unsecured exposure 0.30% of advances with negligible NPA, US tariff impact only 1.05% of export credit (17.53% of that 1.05%)
items.quote: On the unsecured exposure, another concern for the market is our share of it in the total advances is 0.30% with practically negligible NPA in that. U.S. tariff impact, we have just mentioned that, yes, we do have a 1.05% impact on export credit, but only 17.53% of that is impacted by the U.S. tariff, of this 1.05%.

items.statement: CASA grew 9.30% YoY, share up 92 bps in H1 (58 bps in Q2), term deposits 13.50% YoY
items.quote: CASA is something we lost in the last year. But in the current year, the year-on-year growth is 9.30%, but 92 basis is what we have picked up. CASA share has gone up 92 basis in the last 2 quarters. In fact, in quarter 2 itself, it has gone up 58 basis.

items.statement: Gold price reversal risk on jewel loan growth, cushioned by customer base expansion in semi-urban/rural branches
items.quote: There will certainly, see, the gold growth is not just coming from the gold price alone. It is also coming from the fact that 47% of our branches are in the semi-urban and 21% are in the rural. So it is also coming from the expansion of the number of customers.

items.statement: ED show-cause notice under FEMA max penalty INR2 lakh, fully provided, no monetary impact expected
items.quote: When we look at the maximum penalty there is INR2 lakhs. INR2 lakhs, right? INR2 lakhs, and we have already provided for that.

items.statement: Loan Management System Phase 1 under UAT, going live bank-wide by November end, Phase 2-3 in next 2 quarters
items.quote: Loan management systems, the Phase 1 is on right now, is almost completed and is under UAT. Workflow automation out of the 8 projects, 3 have already been handed over.

items.statement: Digital engagement hub-based internet banking replacement going live January 2026, mobile banking revamp, website replacement, CDP next
items.quote: You will see that result in January of '26 when the entire Internet banking will be replaced. Wholesale will be replaced. The entire website is being replaced wholesale. The mobile banking is completely being revamped.

items.statement: NRI deposits up ~9%, Global NRI Center launched in Kochi during Onam, NRI numbers to be disclosed next quarter
items.quote: We have already set up the global NRI center, right? And we are also seeing an uptick I think that also went up about 9%, right? The NRI business NRI deposits are also beginning to show some growth.

items.statement: FY26 AUM growth guidance of 12-14% maintained; expect to meet guidance in H2 as write-offs normalize
items.quote: Largely, we do see we'll be able to meet the growth guidance what we have given.

items.statement: FY27 AUM growth expected at 20%+ combining retail finance and microfinance; microfinance growth in early teens
items.quote: It should be in the range of 20% plus combining retail finance and microfinance, but I think we should look at guidance by end of the year.

items.statement: FY26 credit cost deviation of 70-100 bps vs initial guidance due to delayed PAR improvement and ECL provisioning increase
items.quote: Hence, overall for FY'26, we may see credit cost deviation of 70 -100 bps as against our initial performance guidance.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost may range 4-4.5% including one-time ECL rate revision of 70-80 bps; ECL rates should remain range-bound post revision
items.quote: Hence, the overall credit cost may range in 4 -4.5% in FY'27, including the one-time ECL rate revision of 70-80 bps. Post this revision, the ECL rates should remain range bound.

items.statement: ROA target of 4-4.5% range maintained for FY27 despite higher credit cost, driven by PPOP improvement
items.quote: Amidst the evolving market environment, we continue to leverage our risk -based pricing strategy, low cost of borrowings, and efficient operating structure to protect our ROA within the 4–4.5% range

items.statement: Q2 FY26 write-off of Rs 683 crore including Rs 554.7 crore accelerated write-off of 180+ dpd non-paying accounts; additional credit cost of Rs 172 crore
items.quote: In Q2 FY'26 we undertook write-off of Rs. 683 crore, including an accelerated write-off of Rs. 554.7 crore related to 180+ dpd non -paying accounts, leading to an additional credit cost of Rs. 172 crore for the quarter.

items.statement: Accelerated write-off cycle largely complete; Q3/Q4 write-offs will be much lower
items.quote: We are largely done with the accelerated write -off cycle. There may be some portion of Karnataka book, which we have to see, but largely, we are done. So, you will not see these figures in third and fourth quarter.

items.statement: PAR 15+ accretion rate range-bound at 40-45 bps vs expected 25-30 bps due to heavy rains/floods; each month delay adds 15-20 bps credit cost
items.quote: The PAR 15+ accretion rate trajectory remained range -bound, due to the temporary impact of heavy rains / floods across operating geographies. Since the PAR accretion rate is 40 -45 bps as against 25-30 bps expected, every month of delay in PAR accretion improvement is resulting in an additional credit cost of 15 -20 bps.

items.statement: Deleveraging on track: borrowers with >3 lenders at 6.9% (Sep-25) vs 25.3% (Aug-24); >Rs 2L unsecured debt at 7.2% vs 19.1%
items.quote: The deleveraging trend is moving on the expected lines with GLP % of borrowers with > 3 lenders at 6.9% in Sep -25 vs. 25.3% in Aug -24. The GLP of borrowers with > Rs 2 Lakh unsecured indebtedness stood at 7.2% as of Sep-25 compared to 19.1% in Aug-24.

items.statement: Group loan pricing increased by 75 bps in last pricing review to offset elevated credit cost; pricing reviewed quarterly
items.quote: given all the points that we've discussed so far and the visibility that the credit cost is going to be elevated in the last pricing review committee, the company has increased the pricing for group loan by around 75 basis points.

items.statement: Weighted average borrowing cost expected to decline from 9.8% to ~9.5% in FY26 and ~9.3% in FY27; 65% floating rate linked to MCLR with gradual repricing
items.quote: maybe this year, our weighted average borrowing cost started at 9.8%, maybe we end the year somewhere at 9.5%. So nex t year, we start at 9.5% and maybe we may have an average borrowing cost of around 9.3

items.statement: Opened 150 branches in H1 FY26 (96 in Q2), total branches 2,209; launched retail finance from 150 additional branches in Q2, pipeline of 200 more in H2
items.quote: We continued to strengthen our last-mile reach as we opened 150 branches in H1 FY'26, including 96 in Q2 FY'26, taking the total branch count to 2,209.

items.statement: Healthy monsoons, strong agri output, strengthening rural ecosystem expected to drive robust demand in H2 FY26; Q3/Q4 typically strong quarters
items.quote: Healthy monsoons, strong agricultural output, and strengthening rural ecosystem trends are expected to drive robust on-ground demand in H2 FY26, resulting in stronger loan portfolio growth.

items.statement: Added ~4.4 lakh new borrowers in H1 FY26 (2.2 lakh in Q2); 39% new-to-credit in Q2; unique borrower share risen to 41% from 27% in Aug-24
items.quote: In H1 FY26, we added ~4.4 lakh new borrowers, of which 2.2 lakh borrowers were added in Q2 FY26. Notably, 39% of new borrowers added in Q2 were new-to-credit, reflecting our customer acquisition strength.

items.statement: Target ~1 lakh new customers/month; currently trending 70-75k; rejections remain high due to guardrails
items.quote: See, ideally, we would like to add close to around 1 lakh customers every month, right? So we are right now trending around 70,000 to 75,000.

items.statement: Liquidity adequate at Rs 2,176 crore (7.9% of assets); sanctions in hand Rs 3,455 crore + Rs 6,260 crore pipeline; capital adequacy 26.1%
items.quote: The liquidity levels, including cash and cash equivalents, were adequate at Rs. 2,176 crore, amounting to 7.9% of total assets. Additionally, we have sanctions in hand of Rs. 3,455 crore and another Rs. 6,260 crore worth of sanctions in the pipeline. The capital adequacy remained comfortable at 26.1%.

items.statement: Raised Rs 3,519 crore in Q2 at marginal cost 8.9%; foreign borrowings 23.7% progressing toward 25-30% target by FY28
items.quote: During Q2 FY'26, we raised Rs. 3,519 crore, with marginal cost of borrowing stood at 8.9%. Our foreign borrowings stood healthy at 23.7%, progressing toward our medium-term target of achieving 25–30% foreign borrowings by FY'28.

items.statement: Employee base grew to 21,701 (Sep-25) from 21,333 (Jun-25); annualised attrition 28.9% in Q2; engagement and morale strong
items.quote: Our employee base grew from 21,333 in Jun -25 to 21,701 in Sep -25 with annualised attrition rate of 28.9% in Q2 FY'26. Employee engagement and morale remain strong

items.statement: Exploring CGFMU cover for portion of disbursements this year; may scale if experience favourable
items.quote: This year, we will take a certain part of our disbursements covered. So far, we've not taken it. But this year, we may take some of these options available to see how this pans out.

items.statement: PAR 15+ for borrowers with 4 lenders at 15.1% (mid-Sep) vs 14.3% (mid-Jun); >4 lenders at 30.2% vs 31.1%; ~80% of >3 lender customers making regular payments
items.quote: PAR 15+ in case of borrowers with 4 lenders stood at 15.1% as of mid-Sep 25 Vs 14.3% in mid-Jun-25. Similarly, PAR 15 in the case of borrowers with more than 4 lenders, stood at 30.2% in Sep -25 Vs 31.1% as of mid -Jun-25. This shows that the delinquencies have largely crystallised in case of borrowers with > 3 lenders, while around 80% of these customers continuing to make regular payments.

items.statement: Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra seeing delinquency uptick due to rains; Bihar also up; other states range-bound; MP partially rain-related and recent trend
items.quote: Except for Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, we don't see any impact at this point of time. Other things are range bound, right? To a certain extent, yes, Bihar has also gone up. But I think MP, Maharashtra largely due to rains, MP partially due to rains and also probably a trend th at is recent

items.statement: ECL model uses 36-month rolling PD/LGD data; FY26 data points will be in FY27 computation; rates may moderate in FY28 if performance improves
items.quote: Yes. So ECL gets calculated on a longer time period, right? So, if you have better performance during the next year, subsequent year s, the rates could moderate, but it may take some time to come back to normalcy still.

items.statement: Management targets operating margin of 18-20% for core business in FY26
items.quote: Directionally, what we indicated to our investors that between 18% to 20% margin from our core business will be maintained. And we are still confident that we'll maintain the operating margin for our core business between 18% to 20%. That is sure.

items.statement: Order book stood at INR1,667 crores as of 1st October 2025 vs INR1,624 crores on 1st April 2025
items.quote: Company has an order board of over INR1,667 crores as against INR1,624 crores at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Management targets Q3 order booking of INR500-600 crores, with a couple of large orders finalized but not yet signed
items.quote: What we expect in Q3 is we should book orders significantly above INR500 crores, INR600 crores. So that's our target. There are a couple of big orders, which is about half the size of the total years, so the INR600 crores that we talk of, that we have seem to have finalized.

items.statement: Domestic market muted with project clearance delays; export sales lower at INR31 crores in H1 vs INR43 crores prior year
items.quote: Domestic market was muted with various uncertainties causing delay in project clearance and approvals. Export sales at INR31 crores was also lower than the INR43 crores of the previous year H1.

items.statement: Gas compression order intake and execution challenged for nearly two years; no improvement expected in near term
items.quote: We continue to get orders for packages, CNG stations and booster station, but clearly, this has been slowing down quarter-on-quarter for nearly two years now. We don't see this improving in the next quarters either.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 16.4% vs 20% in H1 FY25; Q2 EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 15.7% in Q1
items.quote: EBITDA at 17% in Q2, which is up from 15.7% in Q1 of FY '26. For H1 FY '26 EBITDA is INR109 crores at 16.4%, compared to 20% in H1 FY '25.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at ~70% with headroom for next year's growth; PLI application filed for large Zephyros C plant
items.quote: As far as capacity utilization is concerned, we say that we are about running at about 70%. We definitely have capacity to get the next year's growth always. That's how we plan. The capacity utilization should be at about 70%. So there is headroom for the next year's growth.

items.statement: Revenue mix shift: Gas down to 30-35% from 45%, Refrigeration at 35%+, Air at ~20%, Others growing to 9-10%
items.quote: We used to say that gas is roughly used to 45% came down to 40%. It's probably now down to about 30%, 35%. The refrigeration is about 35% plus and the rest is about 20%, at least air compressors and others.

items.statement: Net working capital reduced to INR202 crores from INR316 crores YoY on strong receivable management and customer advances
items.quote: The net working capital was at INR202 crores. This is significantly lower than the INR316 crores the same period last year. This is on the back of strong receivable management and significant advances from the customers.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with net cash of INR424 crores as of 1st October 2025
items.quote: There is no interest cost relating to any borrowing either for Q2 or H1. As a result, the company is a debt free company. I would like to state that company has a net cash and cash equivalent position of INR424 crores as on 1st October '25.

items.statement: Paid dividend of ~INR42 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: During H1 FY '26, the company incurred capex of approximately INR29 crores and paid a dividend of almost INR42 crores.

items.statement: Lost CNG market share to competitors offering unviable 5-year O&M pricing; not willing to match such pricing
items.quote: Where they seem to be doing things that we would hesitate is that they offer an operating and maintenance price, which is quite unviable. It doesn't work. And how they manage within that is an -- it's an Indian ingenuity at best I can talk of. And clearly, that's not what we will do.

items.statement: Export not a strategic focus; expects ~INR124 crores exports this year (same as last year), primarily to MENA and Southeast Asia
items.quote: Export is not a strategy for us at the moment. There are only a few markets that we export to and that is largely the MENA region and Southeast Asia. The best export we did was INR177 crores. Last year, it was INR124 crores. We have always been saying that we'll do about the same this year as well.

items.statement: Employee cost increased to INR97.4 crores in H1 FY26 from INR87 crores due to headcount additions and salary revisions from April 2025
items.quote: ERE increased to the extent of increase of manpower and impact of salary revision from April '25. During the year, deserving employees were granted increments aligned with the prevailing industry trend. As a result, the H1 cost for FY '26 stands at INR97.4 crores, compared to INR87 crores in corresponding period of FY '25.

items.statement: Subsidiary Systems & Components (55.26% stake) turned profitable with INR9 crores sales in H1; expected to grow with parent support
items.quote: Our subsidiary company, Systems & Components (India) Private Limited, where we have 55.26% holding, too had a muted quarter. Sales is about INR9 crores, and they became profitable for the first time in many quarters. We expect them to grow from here with increased market presence and support from the parent.

items.statement: Revenue target INR 200+ crore for FY26, INR 300 crore by end of FY27, INR 500+ crore vision for FY28
items.quote: The vision for 2026 is to reach revenue of INR 200 plus, which is definitely in our control. 2027, touching revenue of INR 300, and that's why, by the end of 2027.

items.statement: PAT margin target 9-10% for FY26, 12-15% for FY27, 18-20% by end of FY28
items.quote: If we had closed it at 6% last year, then next year, which will close this year, I have to close it at 9-10% and in the future, I have to close it at 12-15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance 15% range for FY27, moving toward 20% thereafter
items.quote: So, in FY '27 it will be in the 15% range? Manprit Singh Chadha: Yes.

items.statement: Factory capex less than INR 1 crore; 30-bed hospital phase 1 capex INR 2 crore; 5-10 lakh per bed average
items.quote: A 30 bed hospital would say require a capex of anything between INR 2- 2.5 crores.

items.statement: PAT margin jumped from 5% in H1 FY25 to 8.81% in H1 FY26 (100% growth); EBITDA improved 200+ bps
items.quote: H1 '25 to H1 '26 was a PAT margin of 5%, which grew to 8.81%, a 100% growth. Even in EBITDA terms may be H125 to H126, 200 plus basis points improvement.

items.statement: Advertisement cost may remain same or reduce 100-200 bps; future profitability from infrastructure utilization
items.quote: This advertisement cost, in the future, will either remain the same, or can come down 100-200 basis points.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 91.9 crore (18% YoY); standalone INR 88.35 crore (17% YoY); May slowdown caused ~INR 6 crore top-line hit
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue stood at INR 91.9 crores, reflecting a healthy 18% year-on-year growth compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Capsule and powder represent 50% of revenue; factory will produce up to 50% of capsule needs (25% of total); tablets not yet launched
items.quote: we plan to just make not more than 50% of our capsule intake, which translates to not more than 25% of our total intake

items.statement: Hospital expansion funded entirely through internal accruals; no plan to raise equity
items.quote: We, right now, we don't have any plan to raise equity [inaudible 00:40:59]. Right now, the entire plan is through internal accruals

items.statement: Ayurveda hospital approvals from Ministry of AYUSH pending; first 30-bed facility operational Q1 FY27
items.quote: It will take some time for that. We have just started it and yes, we will take time for the approval.

items.statement: High customer acquisition costs anticipated; increases from Google/Meta to be offset by operational efficiency and repeat rates
items.quote: I have kept my - like every time a question comes why advertisement cost is high, it would remain the same even when Meta and Google increases that and that increase will be mitigated by my operational efficiency and the repeat rate of the product.

items.statement: ESOP 2025 scheme approved by Board for all employees based on tenure; no distinction by level
items.quote: The ESOP 2025 scheme has been approved by the Board, because we know that Sat Kartar's biggest strength is its people. The best part? We made no distinction between employees, be it at whatever level, except tenure-based eligibility.

items.statement: Acquired Plantomed for low-ticket diabetes product (INR 1,300 vs own INR 2,500-2,600); currently ~INR 60 lakh/month, targeting INR 1 crore+/month in 2 months
items.quote: The rationale of that acquisition was that we are at a high ticket size. Our diabetes is at a ticket size of 2,500 to 2,600. Plantomed also runs a diabetes product, but it is at a ticket size of 1,300.

items.statement: US subsidiary prepared; international territories opened; no immediate revenue expected
items.quote: We have opened international territories, we have prepared our US subsidiary, all these things will not give revenue immediately.

items.statement: May revenue hit ~INR 6 crore due to India-Pakistan tension causing delivery partner denials and distribution disruption; safety prioritized over profits
items.quote: Because of this, we suffered approximately a top line hit of INR6 crores, and a negative bottom line during that period.

items.statement: Premium pricing justified by lifestyle positioning; first-sale ROI model with profitable repeat purchases; high ticket size sustainable
items.quote: My vision is, return for investors, and best of the best product for customers. Because of that, our model is, in the first sale, we should be able to generate an ROI, the second and third and fourth sale, should actually add on to that profit.

items.statement: AI beta testing complete, rollout starting; will enhance CRM, digital ops, customer experience; leverages categorized disease data to convert low-ticket Veda range
items.quote: Our AI initiatives are also entering an exciting phase. The beta testing is complete, and we are now ready for rollout. Through AI-based automation and analytics, we will enhance CRM intelligence, digital operations, and customer experience.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% annual growth while maintaining strong margins
items.quote: As already highlighted in the investor presentation, going forward, we are targeting 20 %-25% annual growth while maintaining strong margins.

items.statement: Planned FY26 capex of Rs 100 crores, Rs 83.30 crores deployed in H1 FY26
items.quote: The total planned CAPEX for the current FY is Rs.100 crores and we are well on track to complete the same.

items.statement: No upward revision to FY26 capex currently; Rs 17 crores balance may be deployed if new opportunities arise
items.quote: And going forward, as of now, we do not see an upward revision. That could come up once we have more clarity on the new opportunities that are coming up.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 129.9 crores executable in FY26, 60% equipment rental, 40% warehousing
items.quote: As of October 2025, our order book stands at a healthy Rs.129.9 crores executable entirely in FY26, 40% from the warehousing segment and 60% from the equipment rental segment.

items.statement: Specialized service contracts order book at Rs 12 crores from current order book
items.quote: So, at present, if I remember correctly, about 12 crores odd currently from the current order book in hand.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 39.20%, up 300+ bps YoY; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin up 300+ bps YoY
items.quote: Importantly, we achieved this while growing our EBITDA by 21% to 26.34 crores with the margin rising by more than 3 00 basis points to 39.20%.

items.statement: Equipment rental standalone EBITDA margin 64% in H1 FY26, committed to 60%+ guidance
items.quote: The overall EBITDA for this segment stood at 56% while the standalone EBITDA for equipment rentals stood at 64% for the said period.

items.statement: Specialized service contracts target EBITDA margin above 20% by end of FY26
items.quote: Our target remains to go upwards of 20% and we are confident that by the end of this year we will be able to achieve them as well.

items.statement: Robust demand across all segments with long-term client visibility; cement, metals, minerals driving growth
items.quote: In the present market scenario, we are witnessing robust demand across all segments and sectors that we operate in. We have long-term visibility from a majority of our clients giving us immense confidence that we shall continue to grow aggressively while maintaining healthy profitability.

items.statement: Shifted from rural/urban infra (20%) to metals/minerals (32%), cement (30%), renewable energy (9%) in equipment rental
items.quote: Among the major sectors served by us in the equipment rental segment, there was a jump in contribution for metals and minerals at 32%, cement at 30% and renewable energy at 9% while rural and urban infrastructure contribution was reduced at 20%.

items.statement: Renewable energy target above 10% of equipment rental revenue for FY26, up from 9% in H1
items.quote: This year, as of H1, it is at 9% and for the entire FY we are targeting that it will be above 10%.

items.statement: Planning to add EV trucks to logistics fleet for new opportunities with current and prospective clients
items.quote: Going forward, while we continue with the CAPEX drive in our equipment rental segment, the company is also working on addition of EV trucks to its logistics fleet with a view to tap into new opportunities with our current as well as prospective client base.

items.statement: Receivable days maintained at 85 days; net cash flow from operations up 268% to Rs 49.99 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: This has led to the receivable days being maintained at 85 days for the same period last year. The debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.96 while the net cash flow from operations rose by a whopping 268% and stood at a healthy Rs.49.99 crores for

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.96 as of H1 FY26
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.96 while the net cash flow from operations rose by a whopping 268% and stood at a healthy Rs.49.99 crores for H1 FY26.

items.statement: Chinese crane imports increasing but no yield impact seen; yields improved over last year
items.quote: There is definitely a lot of increase in the import of cranes from China because of the demand that has been there for the last few years, and they are more cost competitive as you rightly pointed out. items.quote: The risk that we usually look at is if there is a sudden stop of investments across sectors, across the board, which doesn't seem likely, but yes, that is one risk factor. items.quote: Developing talent is ensuring that with our operating crew, there are regular training programs, there is a tie-up with the OEMs and then there are tie -ups with third-party agencies who do the necessary trainings at site. items.quote: That looks like it, yes. Because last year we did about 30 crores odd, and this year as the equipment rental segment is growing at about 30% plus, so similarly the specialized service contracts should see a similar rise in the total revenue for the full financial year.

items.statement: SAIL warehousing project at Dankuni (largest SAIL warehouse by volume) starting in Q3 FY26, fully warehousing
items.quote: It is completely warehousing, the one that we are starting in West Bengal, Dankuni. And that happens to be Steel Authority of India's largest warehouse by volume in India and that is starting just in a couple of days, as we have given out in July that we will start operations in Q3.

items.quote: Definitely, as I talked about earlier, we have improved our share for the revenue in the cement sector to about 30 % odd a nd we are looking at growing with our clients and we have order visibility as well as growth opportunities with the clients in the cement sector as well as other sectors. With that kind of CAPEX as you talked about laid out, yes, that three-year horizon is definitely visible f

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR1,100-1,200 crores
items.quote: With trajectory, we are confident of closing the year in the range of INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores, making yet another year of strong growth and scale.

items.statement: FY30 revenue target of INR4,000-5,000 crores
items.quote: So, FY 2030, we look around INR4,000 to INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 9-10%
items.quote: So, 9% to 10% should be EBITDA sustainable.

items.statement: PAT margin target of 4.5-5% with potential upside from diamond jewelry
items.quote: And now we have started real diamond jewelry also. So, we hope our business, profit is going to increase by 4.5% to 5%. It can go above that also.

items.statement: Installed capacity grew from 750 kg in FY22 to 1.5-1.6 tons in FY25
items.quote: Our installed capacity has grown from 750 kg in FY22 to 1.5 to 1.6 tons in FY25.

items.statement: Target capacity of 6-7 tons annually by FY30
items.quote: Approximately around 6 to 7 tons.

items.statement: 25% volume growth in kgs in H1 FY26 YoY
items.quote: Yes, the demand was much because we have improved on 25% of our sales also in terms of kgs. This six months.

items.statement: Volume up 25%, value up ~35% in H1 FY26
items.quote: See, volume wise, we have 25% volume has increased. And growth wise, I think around 35% it's increased value wise.

items.statement: Diamond jewelry recently started, currently ~2% of stock, targeting INR200-500 crores in 2 years
items.quote: 2 years? Pankaj Jagawat: Around INR200 crores-INR300 crores in 2 years. It can be more, it can be INR500 crores

items.statement: Focus on lightweight designer jewelry with higher margins
items.quote: We are more into lightweight jewelry and all, Yes. And margins are very good there.

items.quote: So, Yes, we are completely into B2B. We don't do B2C at all. And our clients are like Kalyan Jewelers, Lalita Jewelry, and a lot of customers in South, North, and all the places, Yes.

items.quote: See, receivable means we have got now 70-80 odd customers new. So, according to that we have given them the leverage. And that is why our cash flow is going little above the time which is again going to become normal after 3-4 months.

items.statement: Short-term borrowing at INR100-125 crores, 8.5% interest rate, planning additional INR50 crores borrowing
items.quote: Yes. Yes. We are going to borrow more from the bank. Around INR50 crores we are planning to borrow.

items.statement: Comfortable with debt-to-equity of 1.5-2x
items.quote: 1.5 to two times we can go.

items.statement: Participating in Dubai exhibition in November, planning Dubai office, have existing Middle East contacts
items.quote: So, we are now participating in international exhibitions in Dubai which is going to be held in November. So, Yes. We are going international level also by exhibiting over there. And we have a plan to open an office in Dubai.

items.statement: Gold sourced locally from bullion dealers or banks, no import
items.quote: We source the gold from either from the bullion dealer or from the bank

items.statement: Capital turnover of 4.5x annually
items.quote: Four and a half times.

items.statement: No retail expansion planned, management separate from group company Shanti Gold
items.quote: At present, we have not thought about any retail. At present, we have not thought about the retail sector.

items.statement: Company on track to open 800 new COCO stores in FY26; 355 opened by 30 Sep 2025
items.quote: Company is on track to open 800 new COCO Stores in the FY26 out of which 355 stores have been till 30th September.

items.statement: Board approved fund-raising up to ₹500 crore via QIP for store expansion
items.quote: To support our next phase of growth, the Board has approved a fund-raising proposal of up to ₹500 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP).

items.statement: QIP proceeds primarily for Davaindia store expansion
items.quote: Primarily, it is for Davaindia expansion only.

items.statement: Opened 103 Davaindia stores in a single day on Independence Day (79 COCO, 24 FOFO)

items.statement: Added 310 new stores in Q2 FY26 (89 COCO, 221 FOFO); 473 in H1 FY26 (118 COCO, 355 FOFO)
items.quote: During this quarter, we have adapted 310 new store s with a mix of 221 FOFO and 89 COCO. So, during current financial year, in first half, total 473 new store s adapted with a mix of 355 FOFO and 118 COCO.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA turned positive at ₹796 lakhs in Q2 FY26 vs loss of ₹32 lakhs in Q2 FY25

items.statement: Mature COCO stores (3+ years) target EBITDA margin 30-33% at ₹6.5 lakh monthly revenue; can improve further
items.quote: Currently, if revenue will come to nearly INR 6.5 lakh, EBITDA will be somewhere about 30%- 33%.

items.statement: Per-store rental cost trending around ₹35,000 per month, well controlled
items.quote: Yes, so the per-store rental cost ranges close to around INR 35,000. Yes, INR 35,000 is what we have a trending pattern. So, if you see the trend pattern, it is not only in control, it is well in control in terms of the rental parameters considered in the country.

items.statement: Other expenses rose ~₹10 crore YoY to ₹31.98 crore; includes logistics (warehousing, last-mile) and advertising (+₹3 crore)
items.quote: In Q1 last year, other expenses were around INR 21.32 crores, whereas this quarter they stand at INR 31.98 crores — an increase of approximately INR 10 crores. despite 30% of our revenue growth. So proportionately our expenses has not grown much. T he "other expenses" category includes supply chain costs, and our advertising expenses which has gone up by roughly INR 3 crores this quarter

items.statement: Incremental advertising cost estimated ₹8-10 crore for FY26 (₹3 crore per quarter Q2-Q4); will rise further in FY27 due to brand ambassador fees and marketing
items.quote: Yes, excluding the first quarter, we estimate an incremental cost of around INR 8 to 10 crores for the current year — assuming approximately INR 3 crores per quarter from Q2FY26 to Q4FY26. This cost is expected to increase further next year, as we have already signed Mr. Dhoni and Mr. Sunil Shetty as a brand ambassador.

items.statement: COCO store quarterly footfalls rose to 29.6 lakh from 23.0 lakh in Q1 FY26; FOFO footfalls improved to 13.9 lakh from 12.4 lakh
items.quote: quarterly footfalls at COCO stores increased to 29.6 lakhs from 23.0 lakhs in Q1 FY26, while FOFO store footfalls improved to 13.9 lakhs from 12.4 lakhs in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Davaindia contributed 74% of consolidated revenue; domestic 14%, exports 8%, Everyday Herbal 4%
items.quote: During the quarter, Davaindia continued to be the primary growth driver, contributing 74% to the consolidated revenue, followed by domestic operations at 14%, exports at 8%, and Everyday Herbal Group at 4%.

items.statement: FOFO stores given 37% margin upfront; GMV to revenue conversion ~55% for franchisee stores
items.quote: In franchisee we are giving a 37% margin upfront. So, in our books, GMV to revenue will be roughly 55% for franchisee store.

items.statement: Largest retail pharmacy chain in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal; expansion focused on high generic medicine demand states
items.quote: So, keeping in view of all these considerations, we have focused on Uttar Pradesh and also good to know that as I speak, we are the largest chain of pharmacy, retail pharmacy in Uttar Pradesh and Bengal have also been a good track record for us, for generic pharmacy and Maharashtra definitely.

items.statement: Cash burn remained nearly flat over last 2-3 quarters despite aggressive expansion; expected to stay similar for next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Over the last two to three quarters, our cash burn has remained nearly flat, despite aggressive expansion and the opening of several new stores. This stability indicates that revenue from our mature stores is increasing, effectively offsetting the initial losses from new store additions. Given this trajectory, we expect our cash burn to remain on a similar path for the next two to three quarters.

items.statement: Standalone entity profitable; consolidated negative due to other factors; declared 10% dividend
items.quote: The standalone performance is not negative in fact, it reflects a healthy profit. The consolidated figures show a negative impact, but that's due to other factors outside the standalone entity. Given the strong standalone results, we have declared a 10% dividend.

items.statement: Increased stake in Everyday Herbal Beauty Care by 9.98% to 65.98%
items.quote: In line with our backward integration strategy, we have increased our stake in Everyday Herbal Beauty Care Pvt. Ltd. by 9.98%, taking our total holding to 65.98%..

items.statement: Onboarded M.S. Dhoni as brand ambassador for Davaindia alongside Suniel Shetty
items.quote: we have now onboarded also Mr. M.S. Dhoni as the brand ambassador for Davaindia, further reinforcing our brand's cred ibility, trust, and nationwide appeal.

items.statement: Mature COCO stores (3+ years) average monthly revenue ~₹7 lakh; 6-8 stores already above ₹10 lakh
items.quote: out of the 29 stores, roughly 6 to 8 stores are currently generating more than INR 10 lakhs in monthly revenue. This indicates strong potential, and we expect more stores to reach the INR 10 lakhs mark possibly within the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: COCO store breakeven at ~₹2.5 lakh monthly revenue (12-18 months); full maturity at 3+ years
items.quote: To break even, a store typically needs to achieve monthly revenue of around INR 2.5 lakhs, which usually happens within 12 to 15 months of operations.

items.statement: Inventory delays in some new stores due to high demand growth; management views as sign of strong footfall
items.quote: When you are growing at this stage, you are having more footfalls in your store. You are having customers coming and asking for monthly stock of the chronic medicine. So this is a good sign, don't you think so?

items.statement: Expect 54 stores (currently at ₹4.63 lakh monthly revenue) to reach mature stage by end of FY26; total mature stores ~80
items.quote: 54 store which currently generate the revenue of around INR 4.63 lakhs. Based on the performance trajectory, we expect these stores to reach the mature stage by the end of the current financial year

items.statement: Consumer Group cost expected to remain stable with operating leverage

items.statement: Consolidated expenses expected to remain flat with minor changes, revenues growing faster

items.statement: Consumer Group growing faster than auto industry due to digital shift and market share gains

items.statement: OLX traffic and conversion metrics improving from product initiatives over last 6-9 months

items.statement: Jharkhand coal block PL-cum-ML application under review; mining to start after state government clearances

items.statement: Domestic segment grew 12% YoY in Q2 FY26; half-year revenue Rs 2,723 cr, PAT Rs 278 cr (highest ever).

items.statement: Gross margin back to 60%+ on raw material softening (boron and alloy steel); contribution margin ~28%; EBITDA 18% for quarter, 17.7% for H1.

The second is we have also got some new businesses in the passenger car segment and the tractor segments
