items.statement: Unit 3 Phase 1 structure complete, Phase 2 civil started, partial production begun, full production by end FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: On the capex side, Unit 3 Phase 1 Single structure is complete. Phase 2 civil structure has already started and partial production in the phase 1 has already started and the full-fledged production will be starting from end of this financial year or probably by Q1 next financial year.

items.statement: Unit 3 will enhance production capacity 8x over current facility
items.quote: If you compare the present facility and once Unit 3 is ready, we are enhancing our capacity to eight times. Present this thing to, once our Unit 3 is ready, it is almost eight times enhancing the production capacity.

items.statement: Order book slightly under INR800 crores as of September end plus new development orders received in last 1-1.5 months
items.quote: So, little less than INR800 crores is the order book as on September end, actually. Okay. Over and above that in last 1, 1.5 month, we have received a few more orders, you know, and little amount of production orders, but significant amount of new development orders for the next generation weapon programs and next generation platform programs, actually.

items.statement: Order book expected to reach 3x FY25 level by March or Q1 FY27 driven by large cap projects like MIGM, QRSAM, ESWT
items.quote: We have initially given a guidance by March, you know, we will be having owing to some large caps projects which we were expecting. As the day stands, it is actually going on track. We are also fingers crossed waiting keenly for it. Even if it in case misses by March, you know, by first quarter, it should happen.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 28% in H1 FY26, Q2 at 26.3%; margins vary quarterly by product mix but expected in 26-28% range for FY26
items.quote: Yes. As we told, quarter-on-quarter basis, the different product mix have a different margin profiles actually. So, broadly, it is all guided based on that actually. So, it will be varying in those ranges actually.

items.statement: Production currently 25-30% of revenue vs development; expected to rise to 40-45% as large projects convert to production
items.quote: 25% to 30% in between band, you know, is the production size compared to the development, development to core development, development cum production orders, actually. Going forward, it may increase up to 45%, you know, that is what we are contemplating.

items.statement: Receivables INR360 crores; significant reduction expected by Q4 FY26 as long gestation projects complete and production orders with 30-day payment cycles increase
items.quote: So this financial year end, you will see a significant reduction in the receivables, actually. Some of the long gestation projects which the receivable, this thing is over. It has almost come to a final phases, actually. I think, Q3 to some extent visibility will be there. Q4 significant reduction will be there.

items.statement: Export opportunity pipeline >INR100 crores for critical avionic system; export process requires MOD/DRDO approvals; no revenue split guidance yet
items.quote: As the day stands, we are having a little over about, INR100 crores opportunity of, you know, as an export order, which is presently a kind of a development project, actually. Okay. And it's a very critical avionic system. And as far as the mix is concerned, at this point of time, we are not able to give any guidance for it.

items.statement: ALWT AON approval received; EHWT order from Navy expected by March; QRSAM in RFQ stage with order expected before March or Q1 FY27; MIGM DAC approval expected by Dec, order 2-3 months after
items.quote: ALWT AON approval has already come, which is there in the market last couple of weeks back, Ministry of Defense already given. You will also see a good order flowing for EHWT to Bharat Dynamics Limited from Indian Navy and we having a significant participation in the program, we are also going to get. Most likely that this EHWT order, most likely we may get within March, is what we are getting to

items.statement: BrahMos: one subsystem order received, 5-6 projects in technical evaluation, more orders expected in 2-3 months
items.quote: BrahMos, one project already we are doing. And if I remember correct, some five to six projects already we have participated, technical evaluation is going on. Once that completes, they are going to decide actually. We are expecting more and more orders from BrahMos next two, three months' time.

items.statement: Mechatronic Fuse ToT from DRDO absorbed; prototypes in 1-2 quarters, validation in ~1 year, customer interest already emerging
items.quote: Mechatronic Fuse, recently we have taken a mechatronic, so basically a mechanical fuse. We have developed few mechanical and mechanical plus electronic fuses indigenously. But for certain applications, instead of redeveloping, we have taken a ToT from DRDO, which is applicable for certain motor applications, that is the thing. The opportunity size is very big, it is a recent ToT. So, we will be ab

items.statement: UK order INR113 crores held; expecting more orders from Saudi and Europe; overseas companies auditing Unit 3 for MOUs
items.quote: I think we have already announced one project, a good project from the UK. We are holding one order. It is the INR113 crores order we are holding and we are expecting more and more orders from Saudi also. We are expecting some orders and Europe side also we are expecting some orders.

items.statement: Government considering allowing wholly-owned foreign defense subsidiaries as Indian vendors; management sees both risk and opportunity but limited impact on DRDO strategic programs
items.quote: Particularly, you know, we would not say that, it's not a welcoming gesture, but definitely not a very good move is what we can say. But in one way, we can also say that by this fully owned companies, which are 100% investment by these companies. Once these companies start establishing their offices here in India, a lot of further, you know, ecosystem also gets developed, and the existing ecosyste

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduced to ~35%; targeting zero pledge within 6 months
items.quote: Yes, like if you see, we are reducing. I think next one week time, we are going to see, you know, I think every month we are reducing something. Yes, definitely. Next six months' time, I'm going to close all the pledge part. That's what I'm planning.

items.statement: Board evaluating funding options for IDL overhaul and growth; will announce when approved
items.quote: I would reserve my answer for this. You know, there are certain things which we are contemplating as and when the Board gives the kind of an approval, I think, we will reach out to you for packaging.

name: Home First Finance Company India Limited

items.statement: AUM grew 26.3% y-o-y and 5.2% q-o-q to Rs. 14,178 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The AUM growth remains strong, growing at 26.3% y-o-y and 5.2% q-o-q to reach Rs. 14,178 crores.

items.statement: Guiding for 25% plus AUM growth for FY26
items.quote: We are guiding to that 25% plus AUM growth, so this quarter it was 26%.

items.statement: Credit cost expected at 40 bps for full year FY26
items.quote: On credit cost, we are still looking at 40 bps for the full year.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing targeted under 8% by March 2026
items.quote: We are aiming to get it under 8%, let us say, by March.

items.statement: Spreads expected to be maintained in 5% to 5.25% range
items.quote: The spread, we should be able to maintain in the 5% to 5.25% that we have always guided.

items.statement: NIMs expected to expand faster than spreads in coming quarters
items.quote: As far as the NIM s are concerned, they will marginally expand from here with now large part of the cash consumption done post the QIP and leverage also picking up. So, NIMs will expand faster than spreads

items.statement: Added 5 branches in Q2 FY26; plan to add 4-5 branches in Q3 FY26
items.quote: In this quarter, we added five branches, with the latest additions comprising three in Maharashtra, one in Andhra Pradesh and one in Gujarat. We plan to add four to five new branches in the upcoming quarter.

items.statement: Branch expansion guidance of 5-7 branches per quarter going forward
items.quote: Branch count, again, around that five to seven branches per quarter is what we have been maintaining as a guidance.

items.statement: Net interest margin improved to 5.4% in Q2 FY26 from 5.2% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q2 was 5.4%, up from 5.2% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Ex-co-lending spread at 5.3% with cost of borrowing at 8.1% and disbursement yield at 13.3%
items.quote: With proactive management, we were able to reduce our cost of borrowing, excluding co-lending, by 30 bps at 8.1%, supporting our ex-co-lending spread of 5.3%. Disbursement yields for the quarter were at 13.3%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing reduced by 30 bps q-o-q to 8.1% ex-co-lending; incremental borrowing at even more competitive rates
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing has already reduced by 30 bps, driven by downward shift in benchmark rates, with incremental borrowing now being secured at even more competitive rates.

items.statement: Individual housing loans constitute 83% of portfolio; LAP growing faster due to base effect
items.quote: Our origination yield continues to be healthy at 13.3% despite an 83% share of individual housing loans.

items.statement: Co-lending disbursements up 179% y-o-y and 24% q-o-q to Rs. 97 crores; co-lending book at Rs. 508 crores (3.6% of AUM); target 10% of disbursements
items.quote: Our disbursements under co-lending business increased by 179% y-o-y and 24% q-o-q to Rs. 97 crores for Q2, taking co-lending book to Rs. 508 crores or 3.6% of the total AUM. Co-lending will continue to be an important part of our strategy to strengthen our ability to cater to higher ticket size segments. We aim to take co-lending contribution to 10% of disbursements as we scale.

items.statement: Long-term 1+DPD expected around 5%, 30+DPD between 3-3.5%
items.quote: Broadly, I would say , if you were to ask me for a very long-term trend, I would say it should remain in that 5% ballpark number. Siraj Khan: 1+DPD, and 30+? Manoj Viswanathan: 30+, between 3% to 3.5%, in that range it should be, on a long-term basis

items.statement: Disbursements at Rs. 1,289 crores, up 9.6% y-o-y and 3.7% q-o-q; growth moderated due to proactive credit restrictions in stressed segments
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter stood at Rs. 1,289 crores, up 9.6% y-o-y and 3.7% q-o-q. Overall, disbursement momentum has remained healthy despite subdued macroeconomic environment stemming from prolonged monsoon and tariff uncertainty.

items.statement: Rejection rates increased; certain customer cohorts restricted proactively due to delinquency trends
items.quote: Yes. In fact, rejection rate has gone up and, in some cases, we have softly conveyed to the market that these are certain segments of customers that we will not be onboarding.

items.statement: Market share increased from 1.5% to 2.2% over three years; 4-5% in mature markets like Indore, Surat, Ahmedabad, Nagpur
items.quote: If you see a three -year period, market share has moved up from 1.5% to about 2.2%. This is across all the markets that we are operating in. Of course, in some of the specific markets our market share is touching, somewhere between 4% to 5% where we have ope rated for a longer period

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 48.4% (Tier 1 48.0%) as of Sep'25
items.quote: Our Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio as of Sep'25 stands at 48.4%, with Tier 1 at 48.0%.

items.statement: Employee count ~1,700; attrition inched up to 34% from ~30%; productivity lower due to moderated disbursements
items.quote: Attrition has slightly inched up. We used to be trending at around 30%, but last quarter it was 34%. But for productivity, the number is basically a derivative of disbursement. Since we have moderated disbursement, the productivity is also looking a bit lower.

items.statement: PMAY 2.0 traction: 3,500+ applications received, 38 customers received first subsidy tranche, 53 more approved
items.quote: PMAY 2.0 scheme saw further traction. As on date, we have received over 3,500 customer applications. Of these, 38 customers have already received their first tranche of the subsidy, with an additional 53 cases approved, where the subsidy will get credited shortly.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty impacting leather (Chennai), textile (Coimbatore-Tirupur), diamond (Surat), shrimp (southern TN/coastal AP); spillover from MFI/MSME stress amplifying delinquencies
items.quote: It got accentuated by this whole tariff uncertainty. And so, in some places, the impact became even larger. That is really what it is. Also, some of it is also spilling over to the disbursement side, because when you see a clear impact in certain segments, then you obviously do not want to underwrite those segments.

items.statement: Digital adoption strong: 83% approvals via account aggregator, >80% loans digitally fulfilled, 96% customers on mobile app, 87% service requests digital
items.quote: 83% of our approvals in Q2 were facilitated via the account aggregator framework. o More than 80% of our loans are digitally fulfilled through e-agreements and e-NACH mandates. o 96% of our customers registered on the mobile app, with 87% of the service requests now raised

items.statement: ESG: 240 Green Homes certified; Morningstar Sustainalytics reaffirmed 'Low ESG Risk' with improved score 13.6 vs 16.2
items.quote: During Q2, we got 50 additional Green Homes certified, taking the total to 240. I am pleased to share that Morningstar Sustainalytics reaffirmed our 'Low ESG Risk' category with an improved score of 13.6 versus 16.2 last year.

items.statement: UPI interchange is 1.1-1.2% to issuer; merchant pays ~1% with acquiring margin added on top
items.quote: UPI has a concept of interchange, which means that the issuer side will get something like 1.1 - 1.2%, depending on the category of merchants. Everything around it comes out about merchants paying 1%.

items.statement: Acquiring business can sell to merchants at 1.5% or 1.9% depending on commercial choice
items.quote: So can we sell it for 1.5 or 1.9%, depending on who and what commercial is the choice of acquiring business, which is also approved into our acquiring side of business.

items.statement: EMI ecosystem aggregates financial institutions, brands, and merchants; three subvention types exist
items.quote: So three kinds of EMI work in the market. Straightforward, customer base. Number two, brand subventions. Number three, financial institutions also subventions. And in one product, like Apple, by the way, all three could be subventioning.

items.statement: Paytm is gaining market share in EMI and capturing large market during festivities
items.quote: We are cornering, actually. We are taking away the market share, chipping off the market share from the erstwhile existing players.

items.statement: Hired 5,000 sales employees this quarter vs typical 1-2k to dominate merchant ecosystem offline
items.quote: This quarter it's been 5000. What's the sort of thought process behind, you know, hiring so many? Mr. Vijay Shekhar Sharma: You want to dominate in the merchant ecosystem. I will acquire a large number of enterprise onboarding now offline or online. And we will be even more aggressive in offline small merchants. I mean, 5000, I wish we could have done like 2x of this

items.statement: AI agents for small businesses will generate subscription and inference fee revenue
items.quote: Paytm is selling agents for small business and charging subscription and inference fees once the subscription usage grows ahead of it.

items.statement: No material capital investment plan for AI; investments beyond $20-50M will be proactively announced
items.quote: Whenever we are going to do any capital investment, capital investment is an investment that goes beyond $20 - $50 million onwards, we will be very much sizing it up, we will be very much proactively announcing it in advance, et cetera. So right now, what you are hearing, there is no material investment plan here.

items.statement: Postpaid launched in September; numbers currently insignificant; merchant loans growing QoQ with better collection performance increasing take rate
items.quote: Postpaid was launched in September. So the numbers, financial numbers currently are insignificant. That was not a driver. Merchant loan continues with a nice trajectory of quarter on quarter growth on volume terms. In revenue terms, we are seeing better collection performance, which is increasing take rate.

items.statement: Personal loans facing headwinds but slightly better take rates; non-lending financial services (Paytm Money, Wealth, gold) showing positive signs
items.quote: Personal loan, we have given commentary that due to headwinds, we're not seeing growth there, but we are seeing slightly better, slightly better take rates on economics, but again, not a major driver. And we are seeing this growth in other financial services like Paytm money or Wealth and gold, as Vijay mentioned.

items.statement: Focus shifting from bottom-line generation to revenue generation; acceleration expected on revenue-generating line items
items.quote: Up till now, we are bottom line generating focused. We have started to become revenue generating focused, so you can start seeing it.

items.statement: Credit card on UPI market share is better than generic UPI market share; generic UPI share skewed by P2P
items.quote: Our credit card, UPI credit card market share is better for us than our generic UPI market share. Generic UPI market share is actually skewed towards P2P transactions because they're always larger in volume, per ticket is very large.

items.statement: Subscription revenues expected to be overtaken by MDR revenues in near future
items.quote: We do foresee that, that month is not very far when our subscription revenues get toppled by our MDR revenues.

items.statement: Omni-channel merger enables new VAS (spend analytics, settlement, payout) increasing per-payment revenue
items.quote: Yes, not just this element, but there are other VAS elements like spend analytics, like settlement, like payout. All those things start to show up as new value-add items. So per payment, we make more bps or more money than we will make standalone and offline or standalone and online.

items.statement: Postpaid early days with tens of thousands users; targeting couple of million; 10-12M previous customers on platform
items.quote: Numbers are very early, tens of thousands. So the opportunity is way more forward. I mean, the good thing I can say is that we experienced that this country, we had signed up around 10 - 12 million customers.

items.statement: GMV growth should be higher than UPI growth (20%) driven by market share gains and improving unit economics
items.quote: We do think that if UPI is growing at 20%, our GMV growth should be higher than that. And that's what we'll continue to drive.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of $1 billion by FY28 and $2 billion by FY30 reaffirmed with strong visibility
items.quote: There is good traction and there is good momentum in the business. So $1 billion by FY '28, certainly visibility is there, and we are sure we'll do it.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR80,994 million for Q2 FY26, up from INR54,228 million in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our current order book for Q2 FY '26, which stands at INR80,994 million compared to INR54,228 million in Q2 of FY '25.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 190 bps YoY to 16.3%; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 270 bps YoY to 16.5%
items.quote: Operational EBITDA for the quarter was INR1,480 million, registering a growth of about 80% over the same period last year. This translates into an EBITDA margin of about 16.3%, an expansion of 190 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex of INR840 crores; PCB project equity contribution of INR600-800 crores over 2-3 years at INR250-300 crores per annum
items.quote: total equity that we have to bring in is about 30% of the total capex only. And so for INR1,400 crores, we have already done the finance planning. For the remaining INR2,300-odd crores, and perhaps there could be scope increases later. So we have to bring in about INR600 crores to INR800 crores of money from an equity

items.statement: Sanand OSAT facility operational and ramping; Chennai PCB Phase 1 (up to 76-layer boards) targeting readiness by year-end with shipping from April; Phase 2 within 3 years
items.quote: by the end of this year, th e plant should be ready and at least the Phase 1 in the Oragadam area. And once that is ready, then maybe some customers approvals also will be there, and we'll start shipping like I have communicated earlier from the month of April onwards

items.statement: Targeting positive operating cash flow and lower net working capital days by FY26 end via VMI, receivables discounting (INR300 crores legacy), and even billing
items.quote: So we are quite pleased with this thing and the increase in inventory is a reflection of strength of the business actually at this point in time. And hopefully, by end of this year, we will bring it down to the kind of nu mbers that we are talking about in terms of working capital days, net working capital days

items.statement: QIP proceeds used for debt repayment; debt increase offset by inventory buildup; targeting VMI to reduce inventory funding needs
items.quote: there is a reduction in debt. And of course, the increase in debt is corresponding to the increase in inventory. That's what we are saying that we will make sure that the inventory increase does not happen at our end, but we ask the supplier to keep it so that we don't have to borrow and fund it.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifting: automotive ~26%, industrial ~40%, railways targeting double-digits, aerospace/defense nearing 10% in 2 years, IT/IoT/space ~12%
items.quote: Similarly, our automotive is about 26% of our total. And we hope to get into 2-digit number for railways, electronics and then, of course, for the aerospace, defense, we will come nearer to this 10% number in a couple of years' timeframe. We already are about 12% in the IT and IoT and space.

items.statement: OSAT capacity 60% committed by Alpha & Omega, L&T Semiconductor, Infineon; 14 more prospects; PCB has 16 interested customers; large Tier 1 automotive customer acquired
items.quote: almost 60% of the capacity is already committed by large players, and they have actually gone on record in public itself to say that. There are people like Alpha & Omega Semiconductor, Larsen & Toubro Semiconductor, also Infineon.

items.statement: Government approval received for advanced PCB manufacturing projects with capital subsidy; PLI scheme coverage for 6 years
items.quote: The recent government of India approval for our advanced PCB manufacturing projects, including Kaynes marks a watershed moment for nation's industrial and technological ambitions. It signifies not only policy support, but also India's readiness to lead the high-value manufacturing of critical electronic components.

items.statement: PCB backward integration expected to reduce costs as company spends ~10% of sales on PCBs; HDI PCB margins expected significantly higher than consolidated margins
items.quote: Kaynes Technology is also a user of PC boards, almost 10% of our total sales money is spent on PC boards. So we hope to get some important cost down because of being able to manufacture the high-tech PCBs ourselves.

items.statement: Kavach railway program TAM estimated at INR34,000 crores (INR50 lakh/km x 68,000 km) over 5-7 years; company's own product approved and supplied
items.quote: the Kavach program has already been announced by government and they cannot not do it. So that's, as you know, 68,000 kilometers are there. And the TAM, if I were to make an estimate of TAM, it's about INR50 lakh per kilometer. So it's about INR34,000 crores of business out there.

items.statement: Receivables skewed to quarter-end due to customer billing patterns; legacy receivables (not due) of ~INR300 crores in other non-current assets being discounted
items.quote: the legacy receivable of which is receivable but not due, which is sitting on other noncurrent assets. We are trying to make sure that we have found a method now. So we should probably by end of the year discount it off and get it off the balance sheet.

items.statement: Focus on talent pipeline, leadership development, TPM culture, and digital transformation (Industry 4.0, predictive maintenance) to drive productivity
items.quote: Our priorities are clear, to drive significant improvements in productivity, cost and delivery while embedding a culture of total predictive maintenance across all sites. This will not only enhance asset reliability, but will also instill mindset of owners hip, discipline and continuous improvement at every level of the organization

items.statement: August Electronics integration completed, adding profitable customers, talent pools, and high-margin markets; inorganic expansion remains strategic toolkit
items.quote: Our integration of global businesses, especially August Electronics further adds synergy, accessing new talent pools, customer bases and high-margin markets.

items.statement: High-end consumer work for export markets (non-appliance, high-tech); aerospace/defense final approval expected from major US customer by year-end
items.quote: we are also doing some high-end consumer work, which is not the appliances of like the TVs, etc., but something else, something a little different, which is more high-tech for export markets.

items.statement: PCB project aims for self-sufficiency in copper clad laminates, prepreg, and high-tech PCBs; machinery manufacturers developing process off-site for transplant
items.quote: we hold, let's say, the distinction of being able to be self-sufficient on copper clad laminates, prepreg as well as the PC boards, especially in the high-tech area.

items.statement: Guided 5-7% quarter-on-quarter AUM growth and credit cost may increase 10-15 bps before peaking
items.value: 5-7% QoQ AUM growth; credit cost +10-15 bps
items.quote: We hope to continue to grow at 5% to 7% AUM quarter-on-quarter. And we hope that the credit cost here will start getting range-bound, but may increase another 10-15 basis points from here.

items.statement: ROE guidance maintained at 15%
items.quote: We had guided a 15% ROE. Let us first build to that and then we will talk about plans ahead. At the moment, the guidance continues to be 15%.

items.statement: Spread at 9.05% in Q2, above guided range; no further increase anticipated
items.quote: No, we are already above our guided range and do not anticipate any further increases from here.

items.statement: AUM reached Rs 10,000 crore, up 29% YoY and 6% QoQ; MSME AUM 82% of total
items.quote: Our AUM as of September is Rs. 9,938 crore, and as Aseem said, we achieved Rs. 10,000 crore now, and this is with a growth of 29% on a YOY basis and 6% on a QOQ basis.

items.statement: Added 5 branches in Q2, total 220; plan 20-25 branches per year
items.quote: We have added five branches during the quarter, with the total branch count at 220 as of September 2025.

items.statement: Gold loans offered in 185 of 220 branches; plan to add ~15 gold loan branches in next two quarters
items.quote: We are currently closer to 185-odd branches out of 220 branches where we offer gold. Incrementally, you would see more number of branches coming in for gold. My sense is that in the next two quarters, we should add close to around 15 branches for gold.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost down 80 bps vs book cost at start of fiscal; OPEX down 112 bps since IPO
items.value: 80 bps borrowing cost reduction; 112 bps OPEX reduction
items.quote: Incremental borrowing cost is down 80 basis points over the book cost at the beginning of this fiscal. Over time, this will keep feeding into the P&L. Cost of operations has come down 112 basis points since our IPO, and incremental benefits will keep feeding into the P&L.

items.statement: GNPA 2.77%, PCR 46.17%, credit cost 1.29% in Q2; 1+ DPD flow calmed but not fully stemmed
items.quote: In terms of asset quality, our GNPA is range-bound in Q2 at 2.77%, with PCR at 46.17%, with credit cost at 1.29% for the quarter.

items.statement: Stopped lending below Rs 7 lakh; minimum CIBIL 700; tightened credit screens further this quarter
items.quote: We have further tightened our credit screens, stopped lending below 7 lakhs and raised the gate of entry to a CIBIL of 700 at a minimum level.

items.statement: Karnataka exposure ~12% of AUM; portfolio stressed since Jan 2025 ordinance; recovery will take several quarters
items.quote: Karnataka is a classic case in point where a superb portfolio till January '25 got rudely shaken up in two months, and this now is going to take several quarters to fix once it starts to flow.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity sub 2x; permitted up to 5x by covenants; target 3-4x before raising equity
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity is sub 2, while asset-to-equity is 3, but debt-to-equity is sub 2. From a banking covenant point of view, we are permitted to go to debt equity of 5. But what we believe is anywhere between 3 and 4 is somewhere we will go to the market and start raising equity capital.

items.statement: ROA 4.56%, ROE 14.09% in Q2; PAT Rs 109 crore, up 30% YoY and 8% QoQ
items.quote: Our Return on Average AUM for the quarter is 4.56%, with Return on Average Tangible Equity further improving from 13.53% in Q1 to 14.09% in Q2. We made a PAT of Rs. 109 crore for the quarter, thereby reporting a growth of 30% on a YOY basis and 8% on a QOQ basis.

items.statement: Average ticket size increased to Rs 10.2 lakh from ~9 lakh; driven by higher co-origination with ICICI
items.quote: If you look at our average ticket size for this particular quarter, that's moved up marginally from closer to 9 lakhs to 10.2 lakhs for this quarter, and that's largely also because of a higher co-origination with ICICI.

items.statement: 95-96% of new disbursals to customers with CIBIL >700; approval rates dropped below 40% from 45-50%
items.quote: If I were to talk about the new disbursal, almost I think 95%-96% of the customers onboarded are more than 700 and some of them more than 725.

items.statement: Disbursements ~Rs 800 crore per quarter; leaving ~10% on table due to tighter filters
items.quote: We are disbursing close to around Rs. 800 crores in a quarter. If we were to just stay where we are, that's Rs. 3,200 crores in a year.

items.statement: NBFCs lack SARFAESI advantage available to HFCs; resolution timeline 3-3.5x longer; regulatory arbitrage exists
items.quote: It is a level playing field that NBFCs deserve to be on. And there is a regulatory arbitrage against the NBFC, and I hope that it gets recognized and removed.

items.statement: Political risk and climate risk emerging; Karnataka ordinance caused portfolio stress; credit cost may rise 10-15 bps before peaking
items.quote: What has changed over the years are the two risks that did not exist to this level earlier, political risk and climate risk. Karnataka is a classic case in point where a superb portfolio till January '25 got rudely shaken up in two months.

items.statement: Gold loan business employs ~1,500-1,600 staff across front and back end
items.quote: Coming to answer your question on gold, we have close to around 185 odd branches. There are close to around 8 to 10 people in a branch that comes in. So, roughly around 1500 to 1600 odd employees, including the front end and the back end would be on the gold side.

items.statement: Promoter Aseem Dhru sold shares for personal liquidity; all personal wealth was in company stock
items.quote: Since eight years, all the money that I have ever made is in this stock, and the purpose is to create liquidity for myself.

items.statement: Order book visibility remains strong for contrast media marketed products and NCE intermediates; iodinated intermediate commercial scale expected in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The visibility of our order book in this segment on the marketed product is stable. The order book for intermediate for the NCE molecule is encouraging. The commercial scale of the iodinated intermediate is expected in Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: SBI AMC and SBI General Insurance are right candidates for listing; boards to decide timing
items.quote: SBI AMC and SBI General are right candidates for listing in our stable. It also provides some value unlocking and, more importantly, value recognition for the industry. We would soon be working on that.

items.statement: Draft M&A funding guidelines cap at 10% of capital; final guidelines awaited
items.quote: I think the draft guidelines put some cap on that, 10% of capital.

items.statement: Deposit rates stabilized; further repricing only on repo rate action
items.quote: I think the deposit rates have stabilized. Further deposit repricing or recalibration will only happen if there is any monetary, I mean, Repo rate action.

items.statement: 10-year G-Sec yield range-bound at 6.2-6.65% internal view
items.quote: I think it is now range bound. We feel like the range can be 6.2-6.65 kind of range for the 10-year G-Sec. It is just an internal house view.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margin through material cost, logistics, fixed cost, scheme optimization and counter-level extraction
items.quote: Our intent is to achieve double-digit margin by addressing all the five points which I have spoken now along with the enhancing counter-level extraction and expanding the market share on each individual product category.

items.statement: Material cost reduction initiatives expected to deliver Rs 200 cr annualized savings for appliances division
items.quote: ongoing material cost reduction initiatives are expected to deliver annualized savings of Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Rs 14 cr material cost savings realized in H1 FY26; Rs 60-70 cr expected in H2 FY26
items.quote: Out of that, Rs. 14 crores we have realized already in first half and balance amount of around Rs. 60 crores to Rs. 70 crores will be realized in second half of the year.

items.statement: Logistics cost optimization project targeting 10% reduction on Rs 154 cr base with Alvarez & Marsal
items.quote: On logistic cost of approximately Rs. 154 crores, a cost optimization project targeting a 10% reduction has been initiated.

items.statement: Fixed cost reduction project with Alvarez & Marsal; initial results expected from Q4 FY26
items.quote: On fixed cost reduction, we did not do well in this area. The team has been prepared, the team is focusing now to address this area, and initial results are expected to materialize from Q4 of the current fiscal.

items.statement: Reversed Rs 28 cr from dealers missing volume targets; annual scheme payout Rs 1,500 cr
items.quote: Up to 30th September 2025, we have reversed Rs. 28 crores from dealers who did not achieve their volume target as part of the tie-up letter. The annual scheme payout, including consumer finance and scheme of service stands at Rs. 1,500 crores up to 31 March 2025.

items.statement: Home Appliances division to grow at more than double-digit pace, faster than industry
items.quote: It has to be more than that. It has to be around double-digit. It will be more than double-digit.

items.statement: Washing machine demand momentum continuing; October good, November secondary sales on track
items.quote: What we feel is the momentum is still continuing. And October was good. And November also, if we see the secondary sales, it's on track. So, we expect the momentum to continue in both the categories.

items.statement: Refrigerator volumes 30% short of internal target despite no-frost addition and 5% realization increase
items.quote: However, in refrigerator overall if you see, we are still unhappy with the volumes. And as a percentage if you see, there has been sizable i ncrease, but compared to our internal target we are still about 30% short

items.statement: Front-load capacity 85,000/month at 92-93% utilization in Sep-Oct; planning 10-15% capacity increase
items.quote: As far as the front load is concerned, our capacity has been 85,000 per month. And in the month of September and October, we are almost used to 92% to 93%. And going forward, we are doing activities which we want to enhance the capacity by another 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Top-load capacity 60,000/month at 95% utilization in September; planning 10% capacity increase
items.quote: As far as top loader is concerned, our capacity is 60,000, and in September, we have almost achieved 95% utilization. Same way, we are looking forward to about 10% increase in our capacity.

items.statement: Engineering division expanding stamping capacity in Bangalore and planning greenfield plant in Gujarat near Maruti/Hero
items.quote: We are also looking at setting up a plant in close to Maruti, in Maruti and Hero in close to Manesar. So, two facilities to come up, one in Gujarat and one close to Manesar is what we are thinking of.

items.statement: Engineering division debottlenecking fine blanking with newer technology tools to free up capacity
items.quote: In Fine Blanking, there's marginal, there's some CapEx going in, but a lot of work is going into productivity improvement, including making tools with newer technology, which will free up existing capacity and all.

items.statement: Bid for railway engineering company (Rs 300 cr sales) but outbid; evaluated 60 targets, formal bids on 3-4
items.quote: We bid for a company recently; it was significantly into the railway segment. We bid for a company, but we were outbid by others. The company had sales of close to about Rs. 300-odd crores.

items.statement: Advanced Electronics division started machining for Titan; more updates expected in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Advanced Electronics venture has started. We supply to Titan. We are doing work for Titan. So, that has started. And it has started slowly. I think we will have a lot more to say about this in the January quarter.

items.statement: AC capacity 65,000/month; peaked at 55,000 (90% utilization); OEM development underway
items.quote: As far as the air conditioner capacity is concerned, we are about 65,000 per month. Capacity is available. And in the peak, we have touched about 55,000, about 90%.

items.statement: BLDC motor production started for washing machines (full supply to Goa plant) and ACs (20,000-30,000 in November); OEM development ongoing
items.quote: Washing machine supplies have started full-strength to IFB Industries Goa plant. We do not have any other customers though. We are only supplying internally now, and AC has also supplied now. I think we supplied in October certain dates, certain number, and November I think we will do about 20,000 or 30,000 numbers.

items.statement: Price increases implemented in top-loaders from Nov 1; front-loader increases under evaluation to offset commodity/forex
items.quote: In top-loader, we have increased the price from 1 of November. In front-loading washing machines also, we are looking at price increase, and judicially, we will do the price increase.

items.statement: Dishwasher GST benefit offset by 10% euro appreciation on imported inputs; no net margin benefit
items.quote: Since the inputs are denominated in euros, so the cost has gone up by 10%. So, to that extent, the price has gone up. So, after the GST increased, after passing on the benefit to the customer, there is no net benefit to IFB in terms of margins.

items.statement: 521 IP points contributing 12% of sales
items.quote: Currently, we have got 521 IP points across the country, and they contribute to around 12% of our sales.

items.statement: CSR headcount increased by 600-700 to 5,300; variable pay structure being rationalized by city by mid-November
items.quote: 700 we have increased and our current number of CSRs is 5,300 across the country.

items.statement: Customer satisfaction score above 90% and improved YoY; monitored weekly by service director
items.quote: The customer satisfaction survey is being done. The score is above 90% and it has improved over last year.

items.statement: Cashback/consumer finance attachment 40-50% for industry and IFB; competing on features not cashbacks
items.quote: In this current season, Diwali season, our cashbacks and schemes, they have been very competitive in line with the competition. And for the industry and also for IFP, the attachment for cashbacks, consumer finance is 40% to 50%.

items.statement: McKinsey 12-month engagement on e-commerce modernization and marketing cost optimization (target 15-20% on Rs 100-120 cr spend)
items.quote: It's about a 12-month thing basically on e-commerce. We realize that the processes, etc., we may need to update, or the better word is modernize that we have internally vis-à-vis the best practices followed by other leading firms.

items.statement: Ancillary cost Rs 140 cr in FY25 (78-80% engineering, 18-20% appliances); includes apprentice allowance regrouping impact of Rs 9 cr YTD
items.quote: If you talk about '24-'25, Rs. 140 crores, out of that, approximately 78% to 80% is pertaining to our engineering division. Engineering division, they are doing many ancillary jobs which are happening inside the factory, which are going outside the factory, that are being booked under ancillary cost.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue Rs 1,327 cr (+11.5% YoY); PBDIT Rs 102.5 cr (7.7% margin, +30% YoY); PAT Rs 50 cr (3.8% margin)
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter was Rs. 1,327 crores against last year's Rs. 1,189 crores, which is a growth of 11.5%. PBDIT for the period was Rs. 102.5 crores and its percentage to revenue is 7.7% as compared to last year's Rs. 79.04 crores, which was 6.6% on revenue. PBDIT amount came across a growth of 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue Rs 2,637 cr (+8.4% YoY); PBDIT Rs 172.45 cr (6.5% margin); PAT Rs 75.11 cr (2.8% margin)
items.quote: Revenue for the period was Rs. 2,637 crores against last year's Rs. 2,434 crores which is a growth of 8.4%. PBDIT for the period was Rs. 172.45 crores, its percentage to revenue is 6.5% as compared to last year's Rs. 165.57 crores which is 6.8% on revenue.

items.statement: Engineering division growth below internal target due to customer schedule drops and marketing underperformance
items.quote: Our internal target was much, much more. But many customer schedules dropped. And I think marketing has not done what they are supposed to do, because our internal thing was much, much better, but it's not happened.

items.statement: Front-load growth below potential in states with weak management; changes being made
items.quote: There was room for further improvement. And in some of the states where the management is not good in that state, changes are being made.

items.statement: Poultry segment margins fell unexpectedly in Q2 FY26 due to lower realizations in day-old broiler chicks, CBF birds, and broiler hatching eggs.
items.quote: For the quarter ended September '25, the company's financial performance was affected mainly due to the unexpected fall in the profit margins to the poultry and poultry products segment.

items.statement: Demand was impacted by festivals (Ganesh Chaturthi, Navratri, Pitrapaksh) and abnormal rains/flooding in the northern region.
items.quote: This is mainly also due to the festival during this period, which is like Ganesh Chaturthi, Navratri, Pitrapaksh and abnormal rains and flooding in the northern region where the company operation is there.

items.statement: Day-old broiler chick realization dropped to INR26.48 per chick in H1 FY26 from INR37.22 in H1 FY25, a decline of INR10.74.
items.quote: Day old broiler chick prices for this half year period in 9 months -- 6-month period is INR26.48 per chick, whereas the previous year, the same period of 6 months, it was INR37.22. That means there is a decline of INR10.74 per chick in broiler chick segment, day old chick segment.

items.statement: CBF bird realization fell to INR80.57/kg in H1 FY26 from INR98.50/kg in H1 FY25, a decline of INR17.93/kg.
items.quote: In regard to the CBF bird per kg realization for this 6-month period is INR80.57, whereas in the last 6 months period, it is INR98.50 which means there is a decline of INR17.93, there is a decrease of INR17.93 per kg broiler chick -- broiler bird.

items.statement: Broiler hatching egg realization declined to INR17.02 in H1 FY26 from INR27.81 in H1 FY25, a drop of INR10.79.
items.quote: In regard to the broiler hatching eggs, it was earlier INR17.02 -- this 6-month period, it is INR17.02 whereas the last 6 months, it was INR27.81 -- so there is a decline of INR10.79 per broiler hatching eggs.

items.statement: Maize price averaged INR25,290/ton in H1 FY26 vs INR26,421/ton in H1 FY25, down INR1,131/ton.
items.quote: The average rate for the maize -- maize for this 6-month period is INR25,290 per metric ton is the maize price. For the corresponding period, it was INR26,421 per ton maize prices. There is a reduction to the extent of INR1,131.

items.statement: Soya meal price averaged INR36,154/ton in H1 FY26 vs INR43,316/ton in H1 FY25, down INR7,163/ton.
items.quote: In regard to the soya, the price of this 6 months is average of INR36,154 per ton, whereas last year, it was INR43,316 per ton soya prices. So there is a reduction of INR7,163 per ton soya prices -- soya meal prices.

items.statement: CBF bird production cost is INR85-86/kg for H1 FY26, similar to prior period.
items.quote: As far as our costing is concerned of CBF bird -- CBF bird it is almost INR85 -- INR86 per kg is the production cost of commercial broiler bird for this 6-month period, whereas the last time, it was again on the similar line, almost

items.statement: Q2 FY26 realizations: broiler chick INR21.42, layer chick INR45, CBF bird INR71.27/kg, broiler hatching egg INR18.96.
items.quote: You can note down the second quarter data is also available. Commercial broiler chicks rate is INR21.42, layer chicks rate is just INR45 per chick. As a commercial broiler chicks rate, INR71.27 and broiler hatching it is INR18.96.

items.statement: Prices improved from last week of October, currently above production cost; management expects to cover losses and make profit in H2 FY26.
items.quote: Yes, sir. We are sure of that because we are having the pack production and the realization also seems to be better from the October last week onwards till date, things are very much positive and better. And hopefully, we'll cover up the -- not only the losses, we will try to make the money also because we are having the pack production with us.

items.statement: Current broiler chick prices range INR38-39; broiler bird prices range INR98-106/kg across states.
items.quote: As far as the current prices of broiler chicks and broiler birds is concerned, broiler chick prices ranging INR38, INR39 per chick -- and it's all 12 states which we are operating under Venky's. As far as the broiler birds are concerned, it is ranging from -- at present. I mean from yesterday, we can say it is INR98 to INR105 or INR106 is a price realization in the different states starting from J

items.statement: Broiler chick production cost is INR28-30; layer chick production cost is INR36-37.
items.quote: The cost of production for the broiler chicks is to the extent of almost INR28 to INR30 per chick. And for the layer, it is somewhere around almost INR36 to INR37.

items.statement: Animal Health Products revenue was INR335 cr in FY25; targeting INR370-380 cr in FY26.
items.quote: Last year, we closed something at INR335 crores. This year, we are hoping to cross INR370 crores, INR380 crores in the year-end further.

items.statement: AHP revenue split: 45% external customers, 55% group companies.
items.quote: In the outside customer, it is to the extent of 45% is the business. And in the group companies, it is 55% business of that AHP segment.

items.statement: Capacity utilization: broiler 67%, layer 75%, feed mill 52%, SPF 50%, oilseeds 50-55%.
items.quote: As far as the broiler segment is concerned, we are utilizing the 67% of capacity inbuilt with us. So there is a good room of 1/3 numbers can be jacked up if the opportunity comes. As far as the layer segment is concerned, again, it is almost 75% we are utilizing the capacity. And now the season will come from January, February onwards till June, July and all. As if the opportunity we get, we'll su

items.statement: Layer segment capacity expansion planned for FY27-28; SPF expansion ongoing post-monsoon; AHP expansion completed at Kesavadi.
items.quote: Expansion plan is as far as the SPF segment is concerned as far as is -- already going on. After the rainy season, it will start moving up as far as the capacity buildup is concerned. For the AHP segment already the capacity expansion was taken place. In regard to the poultry, we are thinking to plan in this '27, '28 in the layer segment to some extent.

items.statement: Soya and maize trading 25% below MSP in October; soya prices stable for next 6 months.
items.quote: It is true. The soybean and maize, both the prices are -- even the Bajra, even the pulses, all in October, they have traded 25% below the MSP prices in the whole country.

items.statement: Maize cost benefit expected to reflect in Q3 FY26; soya prices likely stable for next 6 months.
items.quote: It should reflect in the second -- yes, third quarter.

items.statement: US-India tariff talks on soy create uncertainty; US corn imports for ethanol may not benefit due to DDGS export logistics.
items.quote: Another thing that we are -- that the USA, our tariff discussions are pending. So there's a quite uncertainty about the soya factor, what kind of a treaty, what kind of a tariff arrangements are going to take place with the USA.

items.statement: No structural change in competitive intensity; Q2 weakness attributed to seasonal factors.
items.quote: Yes. Yes, it is there. Yes.

items.statement: Oilseed segment EBIT margins near 3%, below prior 4.5-5.5% levels due to soybean trading below MSP and weak demand.
items.quote: There are 2 things are taking place. One thing, the soybean, which is a raw material for the company, that has grown by the minimum support price. And material is already trading below almost 20%, 25% below MSP. So the possibility of getting a good margins happens only when there is upward trend in the market.

items.statement: Poultry segment assets at INR814 cr as of Q2 FY26.
items.quote: So if you see our financial results on the segment asset side, the poultry and poultry products for the quarter ended, it is INR814 crores whereas -- which is the same for all the periods.

items.statement: Farmers quickly shut farms when prices fall, but oversupply persists as birds gain weight, delaying price recovery.
items.quote: There is still -- as I told you, if the normal body weight is 2 kg in the summer, it is 1.8. But if the market is not taking the absorption of the material available. So automatically, the people will postpone the demand. So next day, the body weight will go up. When the body will go up, it will further make the material available, the price will have a negative effect on the price. So that's the

items.statement: QSR business breakeven delayed due to low poultry demand; expected to improve in H2 as poultry prices recover.
items.quote: It is still in the phase of, I mean, making the breakeven point because a lot of stress is there, all like the same is poultry because if the demand is not there, demand is on the low side, the breakeven point is also in a question. So during this second quarter, particularly, the sales prices or -- I mean, volume or business in terms of the QSR, also has -- gone down, which is not in the first ti

items.statement: GST reduction on QSR (18% to 12%) passed through to customers; no impact on company realization.
items.quote: If the price was INR100 and the GST was 18%, now it is INR12%. So ultimately, we are collecting less and paying the same thing to the government. So it's not having our -- impact on our realization and all.

items.statement: SSG expected to grow 30-50% over next 6-12 quarters; last year SSG grew ~22-23%
items.quote: Last year, we grew about 22%, 23%, if I aggregate all of the SSG pieces year-over-year. But this year, we can already see directionally we headed 40-plus. So, we will continue to work on it.

items.statement: PC refresh cycle and AI PC penetration seen in India; overseas PC market flattish
items.quote: We see signs of the PC refresh cycle. And we also see increased AI PC penetration, especially in the commercial space, and we see that in India, and estimate that the growth could be higher in the second half of the year if this trend continues.

items.statement: Mobility grew 18% driven by premium segment demand and NPIs; strong D2R execution in India
items.quote: Mobility grew by 18%, contributing to 35% of the top line, driven by stronger demand in the premium segment, impactful NPIs.

items.statement: Group PAT margin 1.33% for quarter; excluding Arena PAT margin 1.57%
items.quote: Overall, PAT for the group was standing at 1.33% for the quarter, and excluding Arena, PAT was at 1.57%.

items.statement: SSG delivers higher-than-average PAT vs group; gross margins higher on SSG business
items.quote: It also delivered higher-than-average PAT compared to the group, which contributed to our results being what it is.

items.statement: Several large TSG deals in pipeline for Q3 and Q4 in India and overseas
items.quote: We also have several deals in the pipeline on Technology Solutions, which we expect to fruition in Q3 and Q4, both in India and overseas.

items.statement: Investing in CloudQuarks digital platform, technical presales teams, Redington Academy, and marketplace ecosystems for SSG
items.quote: continue to invest on the digital platform, CloudQuarks. We have been talking about that. We already have the platform, and we are continuing to improve it to add more analytics, to add white labelling, to add automation, to add marketplaces, etc

items.statement: Working capital days lowered to 31 due to efficient management and higher mobility mix
items.quote: I want to talk a little bit about working capital and opex, very efficient management of working capital and a higher mix towards mobility led to the overall lowering of working capital days to 31.

items.statement: Arena debt currently ~$130M, down from ~$160M; Connect divestment to reduce debt by $50-55M
items.quote: Arena debt levels are currently at about 130-odd million, used to be about 160 plus.

items.statement: Arena interest cost high due to Turkish lira loans; winding down lira business to significantly reduce debt and interest
items.quote: See, the important point is the interest cost today is very high in Arena because of Turkish lira loans. If we exit or wind down significantly the Turkish lira business, then the debt that we need to raise in the local currency is much lower.

items.statement: Factoring cost Q2 FY26 INR 45 cr vs INR 33 cr YoY; total interest and factoring cost INR 161 cr vs INR 117 cr YoY (37% increase)
items.quote: Okay. So overall, the factoring cost for this quarter is about INR 45 crores. And for last year, same period, about INR 33 crores. That takes the total interest and factoring cost to INR 161 crores vis-a-vis INR117 crores last year, a 37% increase.

items.statement: SSG now 16% of revenue, grew 48% YoY; cloud, cybersecurity, application software, professional services all double-digit growth
items.quote: It grew by 48%, contributing to 16% of the top line. If you remember, we talked about it the previous Information Classification: RL\General Business\Redington quarter that this group for last year grew somewhere between 20% and 25%, so we clearly see signs of accelerated growth in this area

items.statement: SSG revenue mix roughly equal between security, cloud, software; software slightly higher; professional services <10%
items.quote: you can say that there is somewhat of an equal mix between security, cloud and software business with software being a little bit higher, but somewhat of an equal mix. And the professional services part of it is less than 10% right now

items.statement: D2R channel in India with 5,000+ outlets selling premium phones key growth driver for mobility
items.quote: The D2R channel, the direct to retail channel, that we have built with over 5,000 outlets are getting only premium phones, has been one of the key drivers for this.

items.statement: Two distributors (Ingram and Redington) for Apple in India; share roughly 50/50; upcountry growth expanding distribution TAM
items.quote: As you may be aware, there are only 2 players in India, Ingram and us in the Apple space. And there are times when we do a bit better, and there are times that they do a little bit better. So, the numbers are roughly 50 plus minus.

items.statement: Turkey concordat cases elevated at ~4,400 Jan-Sep vs normal 2,000-3,000/year; collections slow, 18-24 month timeline
items.quote: Roughly in the current year, between January to September, about 4,400 cases had got reported, which normally would be in the range of 2,000 to 3,000 entities in a year.

items.statement: AI PCs 22% of commercial PC sales in India this quarter; consistent monthly activation growth for 6-7 months
items.quote: Specifically on AI, we've seen about 22% of our commercial PCs in this quarter came from the AI classified PCs.

items.statement: Hardware commoditization risk in TSG and ESG; OEMs pushing for lower margins; SSG digital platform stickiness critical
items.quote: Now clearly, hardware part of the market is getting more commoditized. And as it gets more commoditized, the expectation from brands and OEMs is to really give lower and lower margins to you.

items.statement: ~125 professional services resources in India focused on migration, modernization, DevOps; scaling via productized models
items.quote: So, our own resources, we roughly have about 125 resources in the company, mostly in India in professional services. And these resources are focused on things like migration, modernization, spinoffs, DevOps, a range of services.

items.statement: Exploring small inorganic opportunities in SSG (cybersecurity, cloud, competencies); early stages
items.quote: We are exploring, I would say, very early stages right now.

items.statement: Board to discuss dividend policy flexibility; current 40% payout may constrain growth reinvestment at 20% ROCE
items.quote: We will bring it to our Board as well and have a discussion. But your point is bang on because if -- we don't want to leave growth on the table at the cost of dividend

items.statement: Positive outlook for India, UAE, KSA for next 2-3 quarters across all business units including mobility, PC, TSG
items.quote: In terms of outlook, so far, India, UAE, KSA, all 3 geographies, we definitely see good outlooks. At least in the near term, the next 2, 3 quarters, there is good reason to believe in all business units as well

items.statement: Arena IT business (USD) ~$500M annualized; flat to declining currently; expected ~$500M next year
items.quote: That will be roughly around $500 million plus/minus, Sarvesh. And that business will continue. Right now, it's flat to decline because of the market situation. We expect it will be depending on the market size and our share, roughly $500 million next year as a number

items.statement: Windows 10 to 11 migration not yet driving big PC refresh; extended support rumors; wait-and-watch approach
items.quote: Clearly, consumers are still waiting and a lot of them have not migrated. Commercial, maybe a little bit more. But I think there seems to be a wait-and-watch approach rather than a whole hold of people trying to migrate from 10 to 11.

name: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 is Rs 28,000 crore, with potential to reach Rs 28,000-30,000 crore
items.quote: Our commitment for capex for financial year 2025-26 is about Rs. 28,000 crores which will have TBCB projects worth Rs. 19,062 crores and RTM projects Rs. 3,554 crores and others will be about Rs. 5,384 crores.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is Rs 35,000 crore and for FY28 is Rs 45,000 crore
items.quote: FY '28, we told it is Rs. 45,000 crore. G. Ravisankar: Rs. 45,000 crore. R.K. Tyagi: Rs. 35,000 crores is FY ’27. FY '28 is Rs. 45,000 crores

items.statement: Capitalization target for FY26 revised to Rs 20,000 crore from earlier Rs 22,000 crore
items.quote: So we are still targeting about Rs. 20,000 crores projects to be Power Grid Corporation of capitalized by this financial year 25-26. By March 2026, we should be in position to commission up to Rs. 20,000 crores

items.statement: Capitalization guidance for FY27 is Rs 25,000-26,000 crore and for FY28 around Rs 28,000 crore
items.quote: And next year it will follow like it may be about Rs. 25,000 crores, Rs. 26,000 crores because last year we got CAPEX of Rs. 26,000 crore. So, we expect that about Rs. 25,000 crore work projects will be capitalized next year. And similarly, in '27, '28 also, it will be around Rs. 28,000 crores.

items.statement: Works in hand total Rs 1,52,287 crore, including Rs 1,02,992 crore TBCB, Rs 37,100 crore new RTM, Rs 9,542 crore ongoing RTM, and Rs 2,653 crore others
items.quote: So Rs. 1,52,287 out of which Rs. 1,02,992 crores in TBCB . Then the new under RTM Rs. 37,100 crores. Then ongoing RTM Rs. 9,542 crores and others like data center, and cross border, smart metering about Rs. 2,653 crores.

items.statement: Bid pipeline for H2 FY26 estimated around Rs 45,000 crore, potentially more with HVDC projects
items.quote: Around Rs. 45,000 crores. R.K. Tyagi: We will exactly tell, but it may be around Rs. 45,000 crore worth. It may be more. Actually, considering HVDC, it will be more

items.statement: ISTS transmission awarding pipeline of Rs 3.5 lakh crore pending out of Rs 9.15 lakh crore NEP target
items.quote: So exact figure I will check, but it is somewhere about Rs. 3.5 lakh crores out of Rs. 9.15 lakh crores is still pending.

items.statement: H1 FY26 capex of Rs 15,385 crore vs Rs 10,002 crore in H1 FY25
items.quote: In project execution and commissioning, we have done a capex of Rs. 15,385 crores as against Rs. 10,002 crores in last financial year.

items.statement: Leh-Ladakh project cost revised from Rs 20,000 crore (HVDC) to Rs 30,000 crore (AC), not yet factored into works in hand
items.quote: Now, cost is coming about Rs. 42,000 crores, considering various challenges and constraints shown by manufacturers or suppliers, So, it may not be possible for us to continue with HVDC and we have already done detailed studies. So, AC is another option which we are considering and cost of AC will be in the range Power Grid Corporation of of about, it will be close to Rs. 30,000 crores

items.statement: Commissioned 3x1500 MVA ICTs at Khavda III, 2x1500 MVA at Ahmedabad, 2x1500 MVA at New Navsari, 2x1500 MVA at Fatehgarh III, 1x1500 MVA at Bikaner, and various 400kV bays and substations
