items.statement: Core clusters (Telangana, Andhra) at sustainable 25-30% EBITDA margin; new hospitals in Maharashtra, Kerala, Karnataka cause consolidated margin drag of INR20-30 crore EBITDA loss each during ramp-up
items.quote: As far as the core clusters are concerned, like Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, they are into something like 25%, 30% EBITDA margin, which is sustainable EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Andhra margin expansion from 22% to 28% driven by Srikakulam ramp-up (150 bed addition) and Vizag acquisition turning EBITDA positive
items.quote: one Srikakulam hospital, which we commissioned a new facility, the ramp-up there is happening quite well. And the margin erosion that is happening in the new acquisition of Vizag, that has come to almost negligible.

items.statement: Positioning as affordable vs competitors in new markets (Thane, Bangalore, Nashik, Kerala); pricing kept lower deliberately during ramp-up, will correct over time
items.quote: We are focused on a similar positioning, Alankar. We're trying to be more as affordable as we can in each of these markets.

items.statement: IP volume grew 15.3% YoY and 12.2% QoQ to 64,288; OP volume grew 25.1% YoY and 18% QoQ to 592,725 in Q2 FY26
items.quote: IP volume 64,288 grew by 12.2% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and 15.3% on a year-on-year basis. OP volume, 5,92,725 grew by 18% on quarter-on-quarter and 25.1% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Nashik requires 17(2)(ii)b license for CGHS/ECHS/ESI empanelment (35-40% of market); historically takes 9-12 months post-commissioning; expected in 2 months
items.quote: you need something called a 17 (2)(ii)b license, which typically takes time. Even historically in Andhra and Telangana, it has taken us at least 9 months to 1 year to get that after the hospital gets commissioned.

items.statement: Average revenue per operating bed grew 9.8% YoY but declined 2.3% QoQ; average revenue per patient grew 7.3% YoY but declined 1.6% QoQ
items.quote: Consolidated average revenue per operating bed grew by 9.8% and a decline of 2.3% on year-on-year and a quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively. Average revenue per patient grew by 7.3% and a decline of 1.6% year-on-year and a quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively.

items.statement: Andhra adding oncology, mother & child, other specialties across hospitals; Kondapur onboarding oncology, transplant specialties in first year
items.quote: We are adding capacity in almost all our current hospitals. Either we are adding oncology, we're adding mother and child, and we're adding other specialties that don't exist.

items.statement: Nashik payer mix: 35-40% CGHS-related, 30% insurance, 30% cash; Thane/Bangalore: 5-10% CGHS, rest cash & insurance; Nagpur similar to Nashik
items.quote: Place like Nagpur and Nashik will have similar payer mix. So even if you look at our Nagpur hospital today, 25% will come from CGHS-related businesses. 20% to 40% will come from insurance and the remaining will be cash.

items.statement: Bangalore micro-markets have untapped potential; KIMS confident with right location, clinical talent, management team despite Narayana, Aster, Apollo presence
items.quote: there are certain micro markets, right, which are still untapped. So some of these micro markets, also there are potential even for future expansion also in Bangalore, not that every micro market is covered in Bangalore.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents (cash, bank balances, <12m deposits, mutual funds) at INR120 crore as of 30 Sept 2025
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents includes cash, bank balances, deposits with maturity less than 12 months and investments in mutual funds at INR120 crores as on 30th September 2025.

items.statement: More consultants interested to join Bangalore and Thane units; doctor onboarding underway for PES hospital pending license
items.quote: more and more consultants are interested to join. So, we are very-very confident the things will move as we plan.

items.statement: Insurance empanelment delays in new markets (especially Nashik) risk doctor onboarding and revenue ramp-up as 70% of market is credit-based
items.quote: doctors who have committed to come and join KIMS to join before this empanelment is done because they fear that their business could get impacted.

items.statement: Thane conducted >1,000 surgeries in <6 months; Kondapur installed first Medtronic robotic guidance system in Telangana/AP; Gachibowli launched Asia's first XR experience lab
items.quote: The unit conducted more than 1,000 surgeries in less than 6 months, a testimony to the growing goodwill. ... At KIMS Kondapur, we introduced a Medtronic major robotic guidance system. This is the first in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh states.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guided at 20-21% including Raipur losses
items.quote: So for FY '26, we should be at around 20%, 21% EBITDA margin. This is including the initial losses of the Raipur Hospital.

items.statement: FY26 ARPOB growth guided at 5-6% for the year
items.quote: That is the guidance for the year. We have already achieved around 5%. Balance will be incrementally done in H2.

items.statement: FY26 top-line growth guided at 15% overall
items.quote: We are on track to grow at the expected commitments itself.

items.statement: Raipur EBITDA loss for FY26 expected at INR10 crores
items.quote: It will be at around INR10 crores because the hospital performance is picking up. The EBITDA loss is going to come down as we move forward.

items.statement: Raipur monthly breakeven expected at 13-14 months with ~25% occupancy
items.quote: By the end of the year, we expect it to go to around 25% occupancy, where we should be breaking even on a monthly basis around the 13 -to-14-ton mark.

items.statement: Raipur FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 8-10% at ~35% occupancy
items.quote: So for the full year, we can expect EBITDA profit of around 8% to 10%. As I said, we would be breaking even on a monthly basis around the 12 to 15 th month, at an occupancy of around 25%. So, for the full year FY '27, we expect around 8% to 10% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Jamshedpur FY27 EBITDA loss expected at INR4-5 crores
items.quote: And in that FY, we expect around INR4 crores to INR5 crores losses for Jamshedpur.

items.statement: New hospital first-year EBITDA loss template of INR9-10 crores
items.quote: So, INR10 crores, we can take whenever we open a new center for the full year, around INR9 crores to INR10 crores loss will be there

items.statement: Jamshedpur hospital MOU signed for 150 beds with INR70 crores investment
items.quote: We have signed an MOU for a hospital in Jamshedpur, which will have a planned capacity of 150 beds with an estimated investment outlay of INR70 crores. The hospital is expected to be commissioned by the end of Q3 FY '27

items.statement: Target to become 1,000-bed chain over next two years
items.quote: As shared earlier, we remain firmly committed to our goal of becoming a 1,000 -bed hospital chain over the next two years.

items.statement: Jamshedpur commissioning expected by November-December FY27
items.quote: Jamshedpur will be commissioned by around November to December of FY '27.

items.statement: Raipur occupancy expected to reach 25% by end of FY26
items.quote: By the end of the year, we expect it to go to around 25% occupancy

items.statement: Q2 FY26 hospital-wise occupancy: Salt Lake 64%, Agartala 54%, Dum Dum 69%, Howrah 45%, Raipur 12%
items.value: Salt Lake 64%, Agartala 54%, Dum Dum 69%, Howrah 45%, Raipur 12%
items.quote: Sure. So Salt Lake was at 64% occupancy, Agartala at 54%, Dum Dum at 69%, Howrah at around 45% and Raipur having started was at around 12%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin at 20%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR24.1 crores with an EBITDA margin of 20%.

items.statement: Bangladesh patient flow at Agartala recovered to 3-4% of volumes from 10% historically
items.quote: Even though the flow is not completely as per what the historical numbers were, but the same has started to the tune of around 3% to 4% right now of our patient volumes, which was earlier around 10%.

items.statement: Average length of stay reduced from 5.8 to 4.3 days at Dum Dum via department mix change
items.quote: If you see, our average length of stay has gone from 5.8 days to almost 4.3 days over the course of one year, which is an intentional change in strategy from our end to divest some of the long-stay departments to short-stay departments.

items.statement: Raipur added renal transplants, chemotherapy, oncology surgeries; liver transplant license received
items.quote: We have started renal transplants, chemotherapy and oncology surgeries at this facility and received the license to start liver transplant, which we shall be commencing very soon.

items.statement: Howrah added surgical robot for orthopedics, first in Eastern India
items.quote: We've recently a dded the surgical robot for orthopedics also, which is the first of its kind in Eastern India

items.statement: 92% revenue from cash and insurance patients
items.quote: Approximately 92% of our business continues to come from cash and insurance patients, reflecting the strength of our neighborhood tertiary care model.

items.statement: Dum Dum facing increased competition but revenue dip due to intentional department mix realignment
items.quote: So with increased hospitals, definitely, there is a sense of, there is an increased competition in that area, but it is more from a perspective of us realigning our department mix in that hospital.

items.statement: Ranchi project stuck awaiting government clearances
items.quote: It is still, we are still awaiting clearances from the government. That is still stuck

items.statement: Actively evaluating Varanasi, Patna, Cuttack for organic and inorganic growth; greenfield preferred asset-light
items.quote: We are actively evaluating multiple cities in Eastern India, including Varanasi, Patna, Cuttack, et cetera. And we are seeing some exciting opportunities in this city, which hopefully we should be giving some news soon.

items.statement: Doctor-led organization helps consultant retention via remuneration, facilities, clinical comfort
items.quote: Being a doctor -led organization, there is obviously a higher level of comfort consultants have than interacting with our mana gement team and promoters because we can understand the viewpoint of doctors

items.statement: Q2 FY26 ARPOB INR38,376; Salt Lake INR41,062, Agartala ~INR35,000, Dum Dum INR42,000, Howrah INR34,900, Raipur INR40,869
items.quote: Our average revenue per occupied bed stood at INR38,376, aligned with our focus on middle to high-income segment.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 consolidated bed occupancy 44.7% dragged by new Raipur hospital
items.quote: Bed occupancy currently stands at around 44.7%, mainly due to the operations of the new hospital.

items.statement: Raipur rent INR35 lakhs per month (~INR4 crores annually) sits in depreciation and interest
items.quote: That's around INR4 crores. That's around INR35 lakhs per month.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 12-15% from 18-20%
items.quote: Consequently, we are revising our FY '26 revenue growth guidance from 18% to 20% to now around 12% to 15%.

items.statement: Revised FY26 EBITDA guidance down by about 1% to 15-16%
items.quote: So we should be in that. I think the guidance was about 16% to 17%. So we should be between the 15% to 16% given the projections.

items.statement: Order book at INR5,354 million as of September 30, 2025
items.quote: As of September 30, 2025, our order book stood at INR5,354 million.

items.statement: Advanced discussions for new projects worth approximately INR2,700 crores
items.quote: Additionally, we are in advanced discussions for new projects worth approximately INR2,700 crores with encouraging conversion costs.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin compressed to ~3% vs 11.6% in H1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin have been compressed in H1 nearly 3% compared to 11.6% in last H1.

items.statement: Targeting 18-20% EBITDA margin over longer term for CBG business
items.quote: As I said, for any business that we like to run, we generally like to target about 18%, 20% sort of EBITDA numbers over longer terms.

items.statement: IPO proceeds to fund capacity expansion up to INR1,300-1,400 crores revenue capacity
items.quote: with the new investments that we will be putting in from the proceeds that we raised in the IPO, getting up to INR1,300 crores, INR1,400 crores is not a problem

items.statement: O&M and spares targeting 40-45% of revenues
items.quote: We want it to kind of grow to 40%, 45% of revenues.

items.statement: Strong domestic inquiry pipeline from large corporates like Tata Motors, Tata Steel
items.quote: I think, you know, the relationships that we've had with the large corpo rate, especially people like Tata Motors, Tata Steel, we are reaping those benefits today

items.statement: International demand strong in Mexico and Africa due to stricter wastewater regulations
items.quote: So, for example, Mexico will go by March 27. They have obligations for a lot of the industries to meet the new standards.

items.statement: L1 in seawater desalination tender worth ~INR400 million for nuclear sector
items.quote: this is a seawater desalination tender that we have – we are L1 in that tender.

items.statement: Expect nuclear desalination order to materialize by end of November or early December
items.quote: we are currently expecting this to – order to materialize end of November, early December.

items.statement: CBG projects expected to contribute INR45+ crores revenue in next two quarters
items.quote: we have penciled in about a INR45 plus crores top-line in the next two quarters, so in terms of execution of two of the three tested projects.

items.statement: Carbon capture pilot stabilizing in Q4 FY26, revenue expected from H2 2027
items.quote: Consequently, we expect kind of revenue to come in H2 of kind of 2027 from thereon.

items.statement: Operating cost advantage up to 50% vs global players in ZLD
items.quote: we are able to provide, in certain cases, a very massive advantage to the client in terms of operating costs, where the technology that we provide can lead to up to a 50% operating cost advantage in many cases.

items.statement: Captive power requirement 12-18% lower than competing bids in recent desalination orders
items.quote: our captive power requirement has been at least 12% to 18% lower than what the other bids our customer has received.

items.statement: Switching new export orders to USD denomination to contain forex risk
items.quote: we have switched our order currency mainly to US dollars. So wherever we are taking new orders, the exposure for supply of equipment, which is done from our India and Sharjah entities, is all going to be dollar denominated.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected between 12-14% given UAE free zone status and India operations
items.quote: we expect the average tax rate to be between the 12% and 14% sort of a wage.

items.statement: Africa project delayed due to pending local approvals, $5.7M revenue shifted to FY27
items.quote: And the balance, about $5.7 million, is what we expect to go next year, I mean, in terms of execut next year.

items.statement: Long-term growth target remains 20% annually
items.quote: the long-term guidance remains at 20%. We see the business growing very strongly over the years.

items.statement: Higher employee costs due to leadership and business expansion for CBG and carbon initiatives
items.quote: higher employee costs. This is mainly due to ongoing leadership and business expansion with the CBG and carbon initiators for the business

items.statement: India launching recycling mandates for large water consumers
items.quote: India is kind of launching certain recycling applications to large water consumers. So that will also kind of help the business in the upcoming years.

items.statement: India is global leader in ZLD technology and experience
items.quote: India is being one of the leaders in zero-liquid discharge and recycling. So, if you look at the global marketplace, on a global scale, India is the leader.

items.statement: Technology licensing deals in advanced stages, deployment expected in current quarter
items.quote: There are a couple of advanced stages that we are in. So in the current quarter, we expect to kind of deploy some of these funds.

items.statement: Management targets 20-25% year-on-year revenue growth and aims to outperform prior year EBITDA margins, but declines to give a specific EBITDA margin range to avoid overcommitment.
items.quote: As Aman just mentioned, from last H1 to this H1 and last year to this year, we always look for a sustained growth from 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 90,441.87 lakhs as of July 31, 2025, with a 7-9% incremental growth seen by September 2025.
items.quote: Our order book remains strong at INR90,441.87 lakhs as on July 31, 2025, providing a clear visibility for the sustained revenue momentum in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Management sees a hot pipeline with ~9% quarterly order conversion growth; order book grew 7-9% from July to September 2025.
items.quote: If I would say there is a 9% growth per quarter that we are looking at in terms of the order conversions. This year it was 90,441.87 lakh order book as of Jul y 2025 and we have seen a 9% growth as of September 2025

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 14.7%; management focuses on structural efficiencies and aims to sustain and grow margins yearly, not quarterly.
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR2,839.99 lakhs, with margins improving significantly to 14.7%.

items.statement: Management expects FY26 EBITDA margins to be better than last year, targeting sustenance and growth, but refuses to commit to a specific range.
items.quote: Better than last year, for sure. Our main focus has been to outperform each quarter and each year. But the main goal in management is sustenance and growth.

items.statement: Strong demand in MENA/GCC/ECO Zone regions driven by pharmaceutical self-reliance and healthcare infrastructure investment; Saudi Vision 2030/2040 supports long-term opportunity.
items.quote: During the period, we secured several high -value turnkey projects across the MENA, GCC, and ECO Zone regions, markets that continue to drive growth through increased investment in pharmaceutical, self -reliance and the healthcare infrastructure.

items.statement: Projects in emerging pharma markets typically have 18-24 month cycles; clients progress from generic facilities to more complex, regulated plants over time.
items.quote: Each project moves in a cycle of 18 to 24 months for us. And we have a strong pipeline from the region.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing covers ~30% of turnkey project supply (process, air, water systems); rest is integrated procurement and engineering.
items.quote: About 30% is in -house manufactured of the products that we supply to a turnkey plant. So, process, air and water. But these are the lifelines of the facility. And the rest is integrated in the entire project.

items.statement: Receivable days currently in market range of 120-150 days; management sees room for incremental improvement via better collection procedures and timely project completion.
items.quote: So the market average range is in this period, between 120 to 147, 150 days. So we have not a drastic, but yes, there is a room for improvement, which we are working on.

items.statement: Signed MOU with KP Group for sustainable energy solutions to broaden service offerings and enhance market positioning.
items.quote: Currently, we have signed a positive MOU for sustainable energies with KP Group and we are looking at entering new projects with our partnership in MOU terms with KP Group so that we can broaden our services, go after sus tainable offering in the projects that we currently do and increase our product profile also by offering these sustainable solutions to our existing and new clients

items.statement: Differentiation via in-house manufacturing of critical process/air/water systems, 30+ years experience across 62 countries, and single-window turnkey model ensuring speed and compliance vs Western competitors.
items.quote: Number one, the in-house manufacturing of process air and water, the criticalities is what makes us positioned better than competitors from the West, which is European mostly. Number two, experience that Fabtech already has in over 62 countries up to now in the design and build space.

items.statement: Projects target compliance with USFDA, EU GMP, Saudi FDA, African regulatory bodies, UK MHRA; regulatory adherence is a key client requirement in all emerging pharma markets.
items.quote: Be it USFDA, be it EU GMP, be it Saudi FDA, or PPB and the African regulatory bodies, be it UK, MHRA, each one of these regulatory approvals are very important, independently for the client to produce effective and compliant facilities and medicines.

items.statement: Operates across 22 countries with focus on pharmaceutical emerging markets (Middle East, Africa, GCC, Persian Gulf); revenue is international.
items.quote: FTL today operates across 22 countries, delivering start -to-end turnkey solutions across processes, air, water systems, three critical pillars of clean, compl iant and efficient pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturing setup.

items.statement: Project execution timeline of 18-24 months from concept to completion is a key sector KPI for turnkey pharma engineering.
items.quote: So, execution plan of all our projects has a total period of 18 to 24 months. Right from concept, design, complete supply chain and then execution. 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Revenue and margins are lumpy quarter-to-quarter due to project-based model; management emphasizes yearly guidance over quarterly predictability.
items.quote: We are into a project company where our business and projects go as per the client readiness. So sometimes our business is lumpy in some quarters and we do not measure our EBITDA quarter on quarter. Generally, we focus only on the yearly model.

items.statement: Core offering is end-to-end turnkey design and build for pharma/healthcare/biotech covering process, air (HVAC/cleanroom), and water (purification/WFI) systems; not pursuing data center or semiconductor segments.
items.quote: If a client wants to make medicines, medical products, devices in the pharma, healthcare, biotech industry, then we design those plants and we build those plants. End to end turnkey project management, design and build. We have in-house process, air and water, the critical lifelines of the facility.

items.statement: Clarified that Fabtech Technologies Limited (mainboard) is separate from Fabtech Technologies Cleanrooms Limited (SME), which paid a dividend; FTL did not commit to dividend.
items.quote: in the Fabtech universe, we have these two dedicated segments. One is Fabtech Technologies Limited, who you are currently talking to. That is the international pharma, healthcare, biotech, design and build company, focused in the pharma emerging m arket international, right. And the second company is Fabtech Technologies Clean rooms Limited. That is the integrated clean room player focused in Indi

items.statement: Monthly run rate guidance of Rs.35-40 crores by March FY26 reiterated with confidence from IndiaAI orders
items.quote: Now, we had made a guidance for FY26 March for the monthly run rate where we mentioned a number of anywhere say between 35 and 40 CR per month.

items.statement: Received two large orders from IndiaAI Mission worth Rs.88 crores and Rs.177 crores for domestic LLM model building
items.quote: So, your company received two reasonably large orders from IndiaAI Mission for Rs.88 crores and Rs.177 crores.

items.statement: Planning to acquire 2,048 Blackwell GPUs (mainly B200) immediately, potentially doubling to 4,096 before March FY26
items.quote: So, as we are immediately planning to acquire about 2,048 Blackwell, so as soon as they are deployed or while we are in the process of deploying them if we see that like there is potentially more capacity that can be utilized based on the input that we keep getting from overall the market and the ecosystem, we might decide to kind of like double up that number all the way to 4,096 before March.

items.statement: Chennai facility went live on August 1st; total data center capacity ~10 MW supporting 8,000-10,000 cloud GPUs with ability to expand at Chennai
items.quote: We have some of the older capacity that we classify close to 1 megawatt or so. Then the newer capacity that we built in the recent past like last two years or so including the Chennai one, the capacity available to us is about 9 megawatts plus 1 megawatt older capacity. So, that is an overall of about 10 megawatts or so of capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 41% in Q2 FY26 from 29% in Q1 FY26; medium-term target remains 70%+/-
items.quote: EBITDA margin has significantly improved to 41% from 29% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin on newly deployed assets expected to range 80-85%
items.quote: So, from a GP margin perspective, what we foresee across our GP margin should be ranging from 80% to 85% across on that newly deployed assets.

items.statement: Robust global demand for cloud GPUs at H100 and Blackwell price points; IndiaAI Mission orders indicate strong domestic demand
items.quote: Now, we are also continuing to see a very robust global demand for cloud GPUs. The demand continues at a price point at which Hoppers are available globally, and at a reasonably higher price point for Blackwell GPUs, we are also seeing a lot of demand globally.

items.statement: Debt facility of Rs.450 crores to be fully utilized by end of March or early April FY26
items.quote: So, debt what we have taken the facility is Rs.450 CR, which would be utilized as per the terms of agreement with the vendor during the payment cycle. So, by end of March or earlier April, that completely should be utilized.

items.statement: Other current assets increased due to advances given for procurement of new GPUs; GST input already factored in March financials
items.quote: During the current quarter, it has gone up primarily because of advances given for the procurement of new GPUs.

items.statement: Focus on NVIDIA GPUs (H100, H200, Blackwell) where customer demand exists; no immediate plans for AMD GPUs
items.quote: Currently, we are very focused on where the customer demand is coming from. So, primarily, we feel that the customer demand today is for NVIDIA GPUs, especially at least in India.

items.statement: Purchase of services and consumables run rate ~Rs.14 crores; not expected to change drastically unless adding more GPU clusters
items.quote: See, some difference would be there before the Blackwell capacity gets added, when your utilization goes high, the cost obviously goes higher, and we continue to build capacity for non-flagship GPUs or GPUs for storage and many other things. So, that being said that like broadly that is in range that like it will not change drastically unless we add a few more clusters of a couple of thousand GPUs

items.statement: Depreciation run rate ~Rs.42 crores; expected to increase to ~Rs.50 crores with Chennai cluster active from August 1st
items.quote: So, I think the number will be broadly similar, but only one point that Chennai cluster became active on 1st August. So, one month depreciation would be an additional number.

items.statement: GPU useful life assumed at 6 years for depreciation (Companies Act); economic life seen as 7-8 years with demand across Ampere, Hopper, Blackwell generations
items.quote: For the depreciation purpose, I believe it is like as per the company's act which is six years for all the GPUs, and mostly useful life we see that like for GPUs or CPUs is at least like happily and easily about seven, eight years.

items.statement: Committed to sovereign technology stack built on open-source with minimal reliance on international software; three levels of sovereignty: Indian-owned infrastructure, India-located data centers, homegrown/open-source software
items.quote: So, essentially, sovereignty, we have defined it for our customers. One is that we are an Indian cloud GPU provider, where the infrastructure is owned by us. The data centers are physically located in India. And the software being operated on our cloud is primarily built by us or is Open-Source with an ability to redistribute that Open-Source however we see fit.

items.statement: Acquisition of Jarvis Labs assets completed to access global self-service demand cohort and tech talent
items.quote: I would also like to once again share the news about the ongoing acquisition of Jarvis Labs assets. So, primarily, the reason for kind of like acquiring the business of Jarvis Labs was essentially to be able to service like a lot of additional self-service demand for a cohort of customers we were currently not serving, especially the customers who operate globally.

items.statement: Authorized capital increased by ~Rs.1,000 crores; no imminent fund raise timeline or details disclosed
items.quote: So, we will obviously keep everyone informed about our plan. So, we will make it when appropriate.

items.statement: Obsolescence risk managed through prudential capacity planning across multiple GPU generations; regulatory compliance with Indian and origin-country laws for equipment procurement
items.quote: We have been in the compute business for almost past 16 years. We have seen multiple cycles of these. So, essentially, there are so many moving parts to kind of like take care to kind of like not have to worry about obsolescence as long as we have done things like in a prudential manner.

items.statement: Exit MRR Rs.16 crores in Q2 FY26 vs Rs.14.5 crores in Q1 FY26; held capacity for IndiaAI Mission workloads causing temporary dip
items.quote: See, broadly as soon as we receive the long-term order from IndiaAI Mission, we had to kind of free up the capacity from longer-term users or refuse from longer-term users and kind of like work with only capacity which could be deployed as per plan.

items.statement: Differentiation through full-stack cloud platform, customer support, solutions, and team; not a data center player but cloud services provider
items.quote: We are a cloud player, not a data center player. Essentially, we have this whole stack of services. So, we have been supporting GPUs all the way since 2019-20 kind of timeframe, and we have been working on our software platform for the last so many years, and then we have the ability to provide the solutions of the kind that customers need.

items.statement: Compliance with Indian laws and equipment origin-country laws; no services to unauthorized users; Trump administration Blackwell export restrictions question deferred as above pay grade
items.quote: I think that question is a bit above my pay grade. So, basically like we do our level best to kind of like follow like all our laws of India and laws of the country of origin of where we are buying our equipment. So, we ensure fully that like none of our services are utilized by anyone who is not allowed to utilize those services.

items.statement: L&T partnership opens doors and conversations; exploring inside and outside use cases for collaboration
items.quote: I think I mentioned that in the past, that L&T is one of the best partners for an India-centered company. So, what I believe is that L&T is a very large group which has been able to open a lot of doors, a lot of conversations with us, and we continue to work with them to explore the various inside and outside use cases where we can work together.

items.statement: Jarvis Labs team integrated into E2E Networks; continued focus on acquiring tech talent in India
items.quote: And even more importantly for the people who were a part of Jarvis Labs, now they are a part of E2E Networks. And essentially, we believe in their ability to contribute overall to building up like a very fine DNA for E2E Networks.

items.statement: No current talks with TCS for their planned 1 GW data center; will evaluate when capacity available for sale
items.quote: I think this is a question which is a bit premature. I think we would like to see a data center where we are buying capacity. So, once they build those data centers and they have the capacity available for sale, we would be happy to consider them along with all the other players.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs. 2,000-2,200 crores for FY26 maintained
items.quote: Guidance was somewhere near Rs. 2,000 crores, Rs. 2,000 crores to Rs. 2,200 crores, and which was based on the commissioning of our Line-3 and Line-4.

items.statement: Working capital expected to reduce to 80-85 days by end of FY26
items.quote: we expect working capital to reduce to approximately 80 days to 85 days by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: Board approved new Bengaluru facility with Rs. 140 crore investment for Maruti Suzuki and Toyota orders
items.quote: Also, the board has approved the setting up of a new manufacturing facility in Bengaluru, Karnataka with a capital investment of approximately Rs. 140 crores. The plant will cater to newly secured orders from Maruti Suzuki and from Toyota.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 2 on track to commence operations in H2 FY26 for Skoda and Volkswagen
items.quote: The Chakan Phase 2 is on track and to commence operations from H2 of FY'26 which will primarily cater to Skoda and Volkswagen.

items.statement: No new long-term debt planned; capex to be funded through internal accruals
items.quote: As of now, we don't foresee that we'll need to have some extra debt. We'll do it through internal accruals.

items.statement: Bengaluru plant targeted for commissioning by Q4 FY27 with peak annualized turnover of Rs. 450 crores
items.quote: Once fully ramped up, the plant is expected to achieve a peak annualized turnover of around Rs. 450 crores. The facility is targeted to be commissioned by the Q4 of FY'26-'27.

items.statement: Order book healthy at over Rs. 1,800 crores with 85% LED-based
items.quote: Our order book remains healthy at over Rs. 1,800 crores providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters and reinforcing a confident outlook. I am happy to share that about 85% of our current order book is LED-based indicating strong alignment with future market demand.

items.statement: Order book conversion: 15-20% in FY26, ~1/3 in FY27, ~1/3-40% in FY28, residual 5-7% in FY29
items.quote: So, out of the total order book, which we are sitting at Rs. 1,850 odd crores, this year we only expect close to about a 15% to 20% of it coming into the P&L. As I mentioned earlier, almost one-third of it will come in FY '27, almost close to one-third to 40% in FY '28, and then a negligible residual 5% to 7% in FY'29.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 9%, impacted by forex; ex-forex would be 70-80 bps higher than Q1
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins stood at 9%. I would like to highlight that margins during the quarter were impacted by exceptional foreign exchange fluctuations. Excluding this one off Forex impact, EBITDA margins would have been around 70-80 bps higher than Q1 FY'26.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 9.1%, up 32.6% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA came in at Rs. 175 crores up 32.6% with margin at 9.1% again marginally impacted by the Forex movement in Q2.

items.statement: Raw material consumption expected to stay at 64%-65%; manpower cost to decline from ~12.5% to 11%-11.5%; other fixed costs to decline from 14%-15% to 12%-13% over next few years
items.quote: I think on raw material consumption, I would expect the raw material consumption to be in a similar state of about 64% odd to 65% odd. The manpower cost definitely should lower with the growth. Currently, I think we are sitting at close to around 12.5%. I definitely see this going down to perhaps more like closer to 11% or 11.5%. And also the other fixed costs will get offsetted. And currently, th

items.statement: LED share increased to 61% of revenue in Q2; front lighting 69%, rear lighting 22%
items.quote: During the quarter, we saw a strong growth of 24% in our revenues led by the increasing share of LED lighting to 61% which has led to higher content per vehicle and better performance of the models we are presenting.

items.statement: PV segment 64% of revenue, 2W 30%, others 6%; order book similarly two-thirds PV
items.quote: The passenger vehicle segment continued to dominate given the higher complexity and higher content per vehicles in PV lighting. PV contributed 64% of our revenue while 2 wheelers contributed 30% and the remaining 6% came from other segments. This trend is reflected similarly in the order book where nearly two -third is PV lighting with a balanced large ly in 2 wheeler lighting

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute 79% of revenue: Maruti, Mahindra, Tata, Honda Motorcycle, Hero MotoCorp
items.quote: I think if I look at our top five customers today we have pretty much the key brands like Maruti, Mahindra and Tata Motors from the passenger car side and we also have Honda Motorcycle and Hero MotoCorp from the two-wheeler side.

items.statement: First headlamp business win for Toyota Kirloskar Motor; taken from competition
items.quote: Coming back to your question, this is the first time we have actually won a headlamp business for Toyota Kirloskar Motor. And that's the reason we will have to expand our headlamp capacities. And yes, we would have gotten this business from the competition.

items.statement: Forex impact from rupee depreciation (Rs 86-86.5 to Rs 89); import 25-30% components in USD
items.quote: So, I think it is known to us that the current global scenario wherein the rupee has depreciated from the range of Rs86-86.5 to Rs.89 or so. And that's the key reason that and since we import over almost 25% to 30% components in USD, so that is a broader reason that it has given an impact to us in this quarter.

items.statement: No significant rupee devaluation expected in next 3 months; forex impact should stabilize
items.quote: As of now, whatever certain analysts predict, I do not expect a significant devaluation of the rupee, at least in the next three months. So, I would still probably perceive tha t we should be able to maintain it at a certain level and not have any significant further hits to the P&L on account of currency

items.statement: Content per vehicle increasing; ADB technology and animation/customization driving higher value; some models already at 2x content value
items.quote: I think going forward there is a lot of animation, there is also a lot of customization which we foresee happening. A lot of new technologies like the ADB which was recently introduced on one of the models will become a lot more deeper penetration across different models. With that I do feel that the content per vehicle will also increase and again there are some models out there where we already

items.statement: EV constitutes only ~9% of order book (PV + 2W); expect EV penetration to plateau at 8-10% in 2-3 years
items.quote: EV constitutes only about 9% of our entire order book, which includes passenger vehicles as well as two-wheeler models. My sense is very simple. Yes, there are big names coming in and I think the EV industry in passenger car, there are a lot of forthcoming models, there are a lot of plans. However, given the current state also, it's a mere single digit penetration on EV clo se to about 4% -5%. Eve

items.statement: Inventory turnover ratio improving; working capital efficiency to support ROCE expansion to 15-18% in 2-3 years
items.quote: The second thing is, in terms of the working capital also, with the efficiency improvement, we see that our ITR is improving and that will also give us some leverage in working capital.

items.statement: SL Lumax JV (dedicated to Hyundai) subdued last 2 quarters due to Hyundai volume decline; new plant overheads also impacting
items.quote: we see that there's a comparatively lower bottomline and it is because their topline is also not picking up since they are primarily supplying to Hyundai and Hyundai was relatively lower in terms of the market growth there. So for coming next H2 also, it all depends how the Hyundai will pick up in the market. So in case they will pick up good then the SL will also start looking at a better growth

items.statement: HVAC production started Q3 FY24; currently supplying one OEM with peak revenue Rs. 35-40 crores annually; no significant new order wins
items.quote: Yes, I think HVAC, we already started production of it in Quarter 3 of FY'24. Currently, we are supplying to one OEM with a peak revenue of approximately Rs. 35 crores to Rs. 40 crores annually. And we are currently engaged with other customers as well to see how we could scale up this business. But as of now, we don't have any significant order wins for the HVAC.

items.statement: LED modules still imported; PCB assemblies and electronic components localized at 25-30%; target 50-60% localization
items.quote: So I think as of now the LEDs are still imported, the LED as in the LED module which is the source of light. We have been able to localize some of the PCB assemblies, PCB boards and certain other electronic components as well. I think going forward the current localization is about 25% to 30% and going forward it will probably get enhanced to maybe a 50% to 60%.

items.statement: Small car revival signs but sustainability uncertain; product mix impact unclear
items.quote: So, the small car is definitely seeing some signs of revival. However, it's too premature to say whether this is sustainable. Also, even if the production gets increased, how much of the product mix will really change is something which we'll have to wait and watch.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 12-15% revenue growth and 15-20% profit growth
items.quote: Yes. We are sticking to our earlier guidance, I think. So more or less, things will be around that figure only.

items.statement: Export automotive market growing with additional business expected this year and next 2 years
items.quote: So the export automotive market is growing because of additional business. And we expect that the business will grow this year also and in the coming 2 years also.

items.statement: Export share increased from 38-40% in Q1 to 42% in Q2, expected to keep increasing
items.quote: As you've seen in last quarter, June quarter, it was 38% to 40%. Now it is 42%. So it will be keeping increased.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin increased 2% YoY and 4-5% QoQ; consolidated gross margin increased 2% YoY but impacted by inventory provisions
items.quote: Gross margin is also increasing. If you see in this quarter, our gross margin has increased 2%. And if we compare then in last quarter to this quarter, our gross margin has increased around 4%, 5%.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin increased 2% YoY but provisions for old inventory reduced full reflection
items.quote: Consolidated basis also increased 2% on Y-o-Y basis. 2% because we are keeping some provisions for old inventories also. Therefore, it is not getting full reflection.

items.statement: No tariff impact so far as supply routed through Mexico warehouse near US border
items.quote: So far, we have not impacted with tariff because we are supplying through Mexico, our warehouse. And the customers who are taking material from us all are located in Mexico-U.S. border.

items.statement: South India capacity expansion on drawing board, no definitive timeline; Mexico plant on hold due to strategic uncertainty
items.quote: We have not taken a definitive plan, but we can say very soon. I cannot give you a number that we will start from tomorrow. We are discussing about it. We will take a decision soon.

items.statement: New South India plant planned as single line adding 4-5 lakh meters/month or 5-6 million meters/year
items.quote: And we have plan on drawing for the South India. But wherever we will be putting the plant, it will be one line basis and capacity will be adding around INR4 lakhs to INR5 lakhs per month or INR5 million to INR6 million a year.

items.statement: PU volume 314,000 meters, value INR7.8 crores in Q2, up 21% volume and 32% value QoQ; PU utilization 23-25%
items.quote: Our volume from PU plant is, for the quarter, 314,000 and value is INR7.8 crores, which has increased by 21% in quantity and 32% in value over the last quarter.

items.statement: PU division loss INR5.8 crores last quarter due to depreciation, no cash loss
items.quote: Last quarter, it was INR5.8 crores loss -- actual, there is no cash loss, but the loss is because of depreciation.

items.statement: Export breakup: General INR29 crores, OEM INR71 crores; Domestic: Auto OEM INR49 crores, Replacement INR36 crores, Footwear INR43 crores, Furnishing INR8 crores, Others INR138 crores
items.quote: Export general, INR29 crores, export OEM, INR71 crores. Total exports is INR100 crores. Auto OEM domestic, INR49 crores, replacement, INR36 crores, footwear, INR43 crores; furnishing, INR8 crores and remaining is others, which comes to INR138 crores and total is INR238 crores.

items.statement: Major export customers: Stellantis Group and Ford in US market; Benz and BMW in South Africa; some business with Daimler
items.quote: Our major export is to the U.S. market with Stellantis Group and Ford, and the business is increasing with -- mostly with Stellantis and Ford and some portion with Daimler also.

items.statement: Talks ongoing with H&M and Adidas for sports shoes; samples submitted but no agreement yet
items.quote: Regarding the two brands for India like for sports shoes that you mentioned and H&M, still talks are going on. Samples are submitted, but no agreement has come to effect till now.

items.statement: Net cash balance ~INR450 crores; surplus cash kept for capex and new projects
items.quote: That will be -- we are keeping for the capex, new capex or any new projects.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on Chinese PU imports creates 20-40% price difference, aiding domestic PU competitiveness
items.quote: As you know, most of the PU material is coming from China and there is huge under advising. They have put anti-dumping duty. Now, what happens in anti-dumping is that you cannot under advise. But you can reduce or increase the quantity.

items.statement: Full year export revenue expected INR350-400 crores (up from ~INR250-300 crores last year)
items.quote: It will be around INR350 crores to INR400 crores. Up to July INR100 crores. April to September...

items.statement: Total sales volume 8 million meters in Q2
items.quote: Yes. 8 million meters for the quarter.

items.statement: Mexico plant decision deferred until March 2026 due to US policy uncertainty
items.quote: We will see, until next March. On that basis, we will take a final call whether we actually want to go over there or we want to keep that decision pending only.

items.statement: Chairman Suresh Poddar present and well; succession planning question deferred
items.quote: The day it happens, we will announce it. We are also as worried as you are.

items.statement: CSR: 45,000 plants planted; adopted schools for education, healthcare, sanitation, family welfare initiatives
items.quote: Under the Corporate Social Responsibility programs, we have contributed towards the regular plantations and 45,000 plants we have already planted and completed and have a plan to do it at a larger scale in coming years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 18-22% broad range for B2B business
items.quote: So on an EBITDA basis, we continue to track in the broad range, 18% to 21%, 22%. That's a broad range of our EBITDA guidance. W e are fairly confident of achieving

items.statement: B2B export revenue expected to grow at healthy double-digit CAGR over 2-3 years
items.quote: We believe we can naturally grow at a healthy double-digit clip over a 2, 3 year on a CAGR basis, without a doubt.

items.statement: ORIGEM targeting 20-25 operational stores by March 31, 2026
items.quote: By March 31, 2026, the company will have 20 to 25 operational ORIGEM stores.

items.statement: QIP raise of INR202 crores to fund 50-65 COCO stores for ORIGEM
items.quote: During Q2, Goldiam successfully raised INR202 cro res through a QIP to accelerate expansion of ORIGEM

items.statement: 15-18 additional ORIGEM stores at various stages of fit-outs and negotiations
items.quote: About 15 to 18 additional stores are at various st ages of fit-outs, negotiations, and legal formalities

items.statement: Order book position at INR200 crores as of September 30
items.quote: Goldiam's order book position as on September 30, was about INR200 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable at 21.6% for H1 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin for H1 FY '26 remained stable at 21.6%.

items.statement: Gross margins steady on full-year basis, potentially slightly growing next couple quarters
items.quote: On average, I would look at our gross margins on a full year basis, which would be pretty s teady if not slightly hopefully growing at least for the next couple of quarters

items.statement: U.S. casting model enables passing additional costs to customers at slightly higher prices
items.quote: We will need an increment on our pricing with them. And various customers, we've offered various deals as a slight increment to our costing, which has, of course, all been accepted.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond demand robust globally; new customers added in Israel, Middle East, Australia
items.quote: We still see demand very, very robust globally. In fact, coming back to Mr. Bhavya's question also, I forgot to mention that we have also started and cracked a customer in Israel, one in the Middle East, and further penetration with one smaller existing customer in Australia.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond prices rising; smaller diamonds up 5-11%, solitaire prices very tight
items.quote: in the smaller diamonds, that is $0.12 and below, right, pri ces have gone up 5% to 11% in lab-grown diamonds. Even though the production is there, the de mand has exceeded production

items.statement: Wallet share expansion with existing large customers driving B2B growth
items.quote: So th e wallet share also the growth in revenue has come, I would say, predominantly from wallet share, but also additions of som e new customers in other geographies

items.statement: Inventory increased due to holiday season build-up and 30 days additional gold investment for U.S. casting model
items.quote: particularly this year, there has been an increase in inventory because of even -- the U.S. casting model, where we have had to effectively invest in an ad ditional approximately 30 days of gold in our factory by keeping that investment running continuously in the United States

items.statement: Inventory expected to normalize in Q3 as gold cycle stabilizes
items.quote: We see this normalize in Q3. We will see this normalize in Q3. We're already seeing that play out as the gold cycle has now normalized, as well with the addi tional investment into the business and into inventory from our side

items.statement: ORIGEM Q2 revenue INR2.8 crores with average 6 stores; October sales nearly matched full Q2
items.quote: During Q2, ORIGEM recorded a total revenue of INR2.8 crores, with an average store fleet of only 6 stores.

items.statement: Consolidation in lab-grown retail; within 6 months only 3 players may have >15 stores nationally
items.quote: If I have to put it this way, within 6 months, you will have pe rhaps only 3 players that would have more than 15 stores in the country in the lab-grown space

items.statement: ORIGEM vertically integrated with cost advantage vs start-ups; national distribution to be key differentiator
items.quote: ORIGEM is perhaps one of the only retailers that is truly vertically integrated. That means every single diamond that is sold at ORI GEM is either grown or purchased in-house loose by the same teams that are purchasing diamonds for our export business at those same aggressive rates

items.statement: Dot-com operations face operational complexity with U.S. casting adding lead time
items.quote: It's very important for us in this quarter to execute in Q3 to execute on our dot-com sales, which end up bei ng a large portion of sales of the quarter

items.statement: U.S. casting model operationally complex but fully running in Q3
items.quote: in Q3, all products are continuously running wit h the U.S. casting model. So we -- that system is now well set in place. Of course, there is -- it's just operationally complex and much more of a headache than in terms of the day-to-day

items.statement: U.S. casting model minimizes tariff to diamond and labor components only; likely to continue even if tariffs normalize
items.quote: So again, the U.S. casting model offers minimizes tariff to the extent that we pay duties on the diamond and labor component. It is extremely lucrative. So we p erhaps would most likely continue that moving

items.statement: QIP proceeds sufficient for 50-65 COCO stores; franchise model to open next calendar/financial year
items.quote: the fundrais e provides us liquidity capital and investment capital for about 55 to 65 stores, in that range , depending on the type of store, store format that we open, 50 to 65 stores. That's completely u nder the COCO model

items.statement: Brand ambassador onboarding still 1-2 quarters away; marketing campaigns planned
items.quote: we are working on it, where our marketing team is reaching out to a respective brand ambassadors and work ing on the strategy. I think we're still a few -- maybe 1 or 2 quarters away from locking

items.statement: Jewel Fleet B2C vertical passed to wholesaler; no longer a focus area
items.quote: Regarding Jewel Fleet, that business vertical, we sort of passe d it over to a wholesaler, and it's now integrated with that wholesaler sales. So we're not focusin g -- it's been over a year since we've really focused on that

items.statement: Management targets INR 1,500 crore revenue for FY26
items.quote: I expect at least I'll reach INR 1,500 crores.

items.statement: Management confident of achieving INR 1,500 crore revenue in FY26 with INR 900 crore in H2
items.quote: Yeah, that is what I'm saying. We must -- I'm confident we will achieve INR 1,500 crores, the past year.

items.statement: Export sales fell INR 150 crore in H1 FY26 due to customers delaying purchases amid falling rice prices
items.quote: Yes, this quarter or this six month the export sales have come down by INR150 crore approx., but the profitability ratio is almost okay, perfect.

items.statement: Customers delaying purchases waiting for price bottom; buying now picking up quickly
items.quote: People are waiting for the -- I mean, waiting for the bottom down, and which I feel it is now. And in this particular season, the sales are very quickly picking up now.

items.statement: Good Basmati crop across India with minimal flood impact; prices low at INR 60-66/kg
items.quote: And secondly, this year the crop size is very good, Basmati. And overall, it's 100, 150, 1-million-ton rice production of the country

items.statement: Paddy prices currently INR 64-66/kg for key varieties, down from INR 71/kg average in FY23
items.quote: The price of 1718, 1509, 1401 varieties are INR 64, INR 65, INR 66 roaming around.

items.statement: Rice prices at multi-year lows around $800/ton; good procurement opportunity
items.quote: So, now the bottom out is there, prices are very low, INR 665, INR 600, you divide by 88, it's nothing, it's less than $800, around $800 costing, I'm talking.

items.statement: H1 FY26 margin 9.3%; expects margins to grow in H2 due to low-cost procurement
items.quote: definitely our sale will grow, our margin will grow. Because our buying is absolutely perfect, perfect time. We are regularly buying, every day we are buying. It's a good price, cheap price, and we know where and how to sell.

items.statement: All planned capacity commissioned: three SORTEX plants in Karnal, new Gandhidham unit opened July, old rented unit ready for trial runs
items.quote: Everything is commissioned now. The plants which were promised in Karnal, they are complete and working. In Gandhidham, new unit was put up, that was opened in July. And one old unit, which was in a rented godown, that has been brought out to the family. That will be in production, maybe -- I mean, it's ready, only the trial runs have to be done.

items.statement: Current operational capacity 25-30 containers per day; can achieve INR 2,000 crore revenue if demand exists
items.quote: Look, the capacity wise, we can achieve INR 2,000 crore if we really have the demand. But I will be little conservative and the INR 1,500 crore we are targeting and that definitely we are going to achieve.

items.statement: Inventory peaked at INR 500 crore; expected to cross that level in FY26 due to large procurement at low prices
items.quote: The peak level of inventory has been INR 500 crores, approx INR 500 crore because I raised my insurance accordingly. And I think it will cross this year.

items.statement: No inventory loss in H1 FY26; company holds stock until profitable sale due to financial strength
items.quote: No, we have not got any hit at all. You see, let's assume we have some rice purchased at a higher price. And if we sell at a low price, definitely we are going to hit. I believe that's your question. But the company is strong enough to keep the stock for any long period. We are cash rich.

items.statement: Exports to 95 countries with ~400 customers; 10-15% Maharani brand, rest private label
items.quote: Because we are in 95 countries. We have multiple, around 400 customers around the world.

items.statement: Private label customers loyal for 5-30 years; minimal switching despite competition
items.quote: Some people don't -- I mean, the customer who are with me for 10 years, 20 years, 30 years, 5 years, 6 years, they don't deviate you know. I mean, somebody buying from us, if they are happy, why should -- why would they go here and there?

items.statement: US exports impacted by tariffs but not halted; buyers absorbing tariff cost
items.quote: Supply has never stopped. It is going. But yes, of course, it has come down. It is going. I mean, complete halt is not there. It's going.

items.statement: Growing demand from non-ethnic consumers in Europe, US, Australia, Sweden
items.quote: But now you see even the British, these Gora people, Americans or Europeans, they love our rice. If you go to any Indian restaurant now in Europe, you will be -- sometime I feel I'm alone Indian, all our local German people sitting.

items.statement: MEP (Minimum Export Price) removed long back; open trade now governed by economic laws
items.quote: There is no longer MEP issues. It's long back it was withdrawn. There's no MEP issue.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues (US tariffs, Gaza freight) caused temporary demand pause in Q1
items.quote: The first quarter, this geopolitics issues matter a lot. When US came out with these tariffs. So, it hit not only US-India business, it hit all around business.

items.statement: Domestic sales volume Q2 FY26: 4,650 tons; company not focusing on domestic market
items.quote: Sir, the volume for domestic for Q2 was 4,650 tons.

items.statement: Aging requirement 1-1.5 months for new crop rice to reach optimal cooking quality
items.quote: So, with the aging of one month or one and a half month, it will start going quicker.

items.statement: Saudi client deal near maturity; contributes to INR 1,500 crore confidence
items.quote: That is almost at maturity state or a complete set of orders have come. But before the commencement or shipping, still some discussions are going.

items.statement: Russia business progressing: 2-3 existing customers plus 1-2 new from exhibition participation
items.quote: Yeah, yeah. We have two, three customers right now, and there is addition also, two -- one or two more have come. We, because we participated there in Russia, in the exhibition, and we got customers.

items.statement: Basmati cultivation expanding beyond traditional GI areas to UP, MP, Rajasthan; Punjab/Haryana quality superior
items.quote: Now in entire Punjab, entire Haryana, UP, the new evolved varieties of Basmati, they are grown all around. It's grown in MP also, grown in Rajasthan also. So, it's growing.

items.statement: No significant competition in private label; high switching costs for buyers due to quality consistency needs
items.quote: We have no competitions, truly. It's not so easy to do private label work. It's very hard. And for large quantities and continued sales, there is competition, but not too much.

items.statement: Targets CD ratio of 80%, NIM 3%+, ROA 1%+, cost-to-income 55-56% by end of FY26
items.quote: CD ratio is 80%. NIM, as I was always telling 3% plus, ROA 1% plus, and cost-to-income ratio to between 55% - 56%.

items.statement: Expects ROA between 1.1% to 1.2% by end of FY26
items.quote: We expect to end the year with the ROA between 1.1% to 1.2%.

items.statement: NIM fell to 2.72% in Q2 FY26 from 2.82% in Q1 FY26 due to repo rate cuts impacting EBLR-linked book
items.quote: Net Interest Margin stood at 2.72% for Q2 FY '26 versus 2.82% in Q1 FY '26 and 3.23% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Expects NIM to bounce back to 3%+ supported by higher-yielding retail loans and easing cost of funds
items.quote: We are expecting a bounce back of yield on advances supported through our focus on higher-yielding retail and direct to corporate advances and combined with expected easing in cost of funds, which should see us going back to the previous level of around 3% plus.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced to 5.54% in Q2 FY26 from 5.73% in Q1 FY26 due to lower bulk deposits
items.quote: Owing to our reduction in composition of bulk deposits in total deposits, our cost of deposit has reduced on a Q-on-Q basis from 5.73% for Q1 FY '26 to 5.54% for Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Cost of funds at 5.58% in Q2 FY26, expected to improve further as repo rate cuts transmit
items.quote: Cost of funds stood at 5.58% in Q2 FY '26 compared to 5.77% in Q1 FY '25 and 5.58% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio grew INR 400 crores in October; targets INR 1 crore per month per branch from 800 branches
items.quote: In the month of October itself, around INR400 crores of growth in gold loan has come.

items.statement: RAM segment net book accretion of INR 392 crores Q-on-Q led by MSME, housing and gold loans
items.quote: Our overall strategy is to continue to focus on growing Retail, Agri and MSME, where the growth was led by MSME, housing and gold loan portfolio with a net book accretion of INR392 crores Q-on-Q in the RAM segment.

items.statement: IBPC portfolio reduced by INR 1,455 crores Q-on-Q to INR 1,860 crores, replaced with higher-yielding direct loans
items.quote: IBPC portfolio as on 30th September 2025 was INR1,860 crores as against INR3,315 crores as on 30th June 2025. Accordingly, around INR1,455 crores of IBPC advances have been replaced in Q2.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 3.33% from 3.46% Q-on-Q; Net NPA improved to 1.35% from 1.44%
items.quote: Gross NPA percentage as on 30th September 2025 stood at 3.33% that is INR2,453 crores as against 3.46% in June 2025, thereby showing an improvement of 13 basis points.

items.statement: Credit cost improved to 0.03% in Q2 FY26 from 0.16% in Q1 FY26; gross slippages at 0.35% vs 0.53%
items.quote: Credit costs showed a remarkable improvement at 0.03% in Q2 FY '26 as against 0.16% in Q1 FY '26. Gross slippages at 0.35% in Q2 FY '26 as against 0.53% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Standard restructured advances at INR 939 crores; 48% (INR 447 crores) requires 30% recovery for upgradation
items.quote: Standard restructured advances stood at INR939.35 crores on September 30th, 2025 as compared to INR888 crores as on 30th June 25.

items.statement: Technically written-off book at INR 2,700 crores; sold INR 490 crores to ARC realizing INR 42.5 crores in Q2; recovered INR 100 crores
items.quote: As on 30th September, the write off book was INR2,700 crores. We have sold during the September quarter a portfolio of INR490 crores, realizing INR42.5 crores by way of sale to ARC.

items.statement: RLPCs (regional loan processing centers) extended to all regions; regional heads empowered with delegated sanctioning powers
items.quote: RLPCs, regional loan processing and sanctioning centers have been set up in all the regions, which initially started with 3 regions. Now it is extended to all the regions.

items.statement: CASA ratio improved to 31.01% from 30.84% Q-on-Q; absolute CASA grew 0.15%; fresh CA+SA additions of INR 870 crores in H1

items.statement: Total wood coatings market estimated at INR 9,500-10,000 crore across all technologies

items.quote: Thirdly, also, you know, the polyurethane as a technology is becoming a commodity, and, you know, it is gaining a lot of retail traction, and there is a shift of the product from technology of melamine to PU, which is, again, contributing in the growth of the sales of polyurethane products.

items.statement: Acquired Wembley brand on March 21, 2025 and Welcome brand in June 2024 from two brothers; provides horizontal and vertical expansion
