So, with the oil cost, this year, we are, expecting a business of 10 crore out of the total co mpany revenue, which is, in terms of number, not big, but yeah, it is a high gross-margin product

items.statement: Runs Sirca Parivaar app with 16,000 registered contractors in North India for training and loyalty rewards
items.quote: Secondly, we run an app called Sirca Pariva ar app, where we have 16,000 registered contractors only from the northern part of India, which scan the products daily, and, you know, on the yearly basis, they become a part of an attractive rewar d program, which is, you know. which is given by the company in the form of gifts and also trips

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guidance maintained at 18%-20% despite 24-25% H1 growth due to Uniclan consolidation base effect
items.quote: But if you see in the second half in the base period, Uniclan was already consolidated. So there, we'll see the growth in line with our 18% to 20% targeted range.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 16.5%-17.5% range for full year
items.quote: 16.5% to 17.5% is a decent range that we'll be comfortable operating in.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated capex of INR150 crores including capital advances; full-year guided range INR210-225 crores
items.quote: For the 6-month period, we have done a consolidated capex of approximately INR150 crores including capital advances and are on track for our guided full year capex estimate in the range of INR210 crores to INR225 crores.

items.statement: 44-acre expansion project: first building possession expected Q4 FY26, commercial production from Q1 FY27; pencil capacity addition in first building
items.quote: But we are confident of getting the possession of the first building in Q4 FY '26 and start commercial production from Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Pen capacity increased by ~1 million pens/day over past year; current capacity 3-3.25 million pens/day; targeting 5 million pens/day by end of FY26
items.quote: So by the end of this year, our combined capacity for pens, you know, which includes the regular ballpoint pens and one-time use examination pens, all put together to be close to 5 million pens a day.

items.statement: Core scholastic stationery/art capacity utilization upwards of 95%; office supplies/hobby & craft at 75%+ with continuous ramp-up
items.quote: But having said that, across all our core products like scholastic stationery, scholastic art material, our capacity utilization is upwards of 95%.

items.statement: GST 2.0 transition caused temporary disruptions in September (inventory clearance, order postponement); sales could have been 3-4% higher without transition impact
items.quote: But we believe that if this transition impact would not be there, our sales could have been about 3% to 4% higher than what we reported for the quarter.

items.statement: Post-GST restocking at distributor/retail level will be ongoing process coinciding with back-to-school period from December; no significant impact expected in Q3
items.quote: And the restocking at the distributor and the retail level will be an ongoing process and coincide with the back to school period, which will start from December.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 17.5% at upper end of guided 16.5%-17.5% range; employee cost increased 1% sequentially and 0.85% YoY due to hiring ahead of capacity ramp-up and GST disruption
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 17.5%. This consistent maintenance of EBITDA margins towards the upper end of our guided range of 16.5% to 17.5% demonstrates our operational efficiencies.

items.statement: GST rate reduction led to MRP reductions (e.g., pencil pack from INR60 to INR58); primary sales pricing increased 3-4% due to ITC loss on 0% GST products
items.quote: In terms of the company sales at the primary level, if you are asking me, the sales pricing would have increased by about 3% to 4%, not more than that, 3% to 4%.

items.statement: No significant margin impact from GST transition as cost increase from ITC loss passed through via revised MRPs
items.quote: So overall, I don't see a significant impact of this on the margins of the company.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 consolidated operating revenue INR567.9 crores (+24.1% YoY); domestic gross product sales +28% YoY, international +18.5% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated operating revenues for Q2 FY '26 stood at INR567.9 crores, a growth of 24.1% compared to the same quarter last financial year.

items.statement: 45-50% of total products impacted by GST rate reduction (45% from 12%/5% to 0%, 6% baby hygiene from 12% to 5%)
items.quote: So in terms of the product categories where GST has come down from 12% and 5% earlier to 0%, it currently contributes about 45% of our overall sales if we look at FY '25.

items.statement: Scholastic stationery, art, kits & combos combined grew ~4% YoY in Q2 and ~5.5% in H1 due to no significant capacity additions; growth from product mix change and slight ASP increase
items.quote: Like you said, this growth has been lower purely because there have no significant capacity additions that have happened in this segment. It's purely been growth due to change in product mix and slight increase in ASPs.

items.statement: General trade contribution declined to ~71% from 77% due to higher baby hygiene share (35% e-com), GST transition impact on GT, and festive season shift to gifting/decorative items; GT expected to return to ~75%
items.quote: And in the baby hygiene segment, almost 35% of sales come from e-commerce. Therefore, you'll see the modern trade and e-commerce segment on an overall consol basis increasing and GT coming a little low.

items.statement: US tariffs introduced in September; no significant Q2 impact as open orders fulfilled; going forward some orders postponed, capacity diverted to Chile (FILA distribution), Middle East, Sri Lanka, Nepal; no overall export sales impact expect
items.quote: So we believe that while from a U.S. perspective, in the current quarter and going forward, there will be an impact until the tariff issue is not resolved. But there have been alternative strong demand from markets.

items.statement: Discount incentives/rebates increased in Q2 due to GST transition credit notes for MRP reductions on channel stock
items.quote: In this quarter, we've had a slight impact, a little more scheme discount rebate given, again, because of the GST transition for whatever stock the channel had and the reduction in MRP that we did, we had to give a little -- we had to issue credit notes for that.

items.statement: Sales team expanded from ~800 to >900 people over past year; hiring ahead of production ramp-up for new plant, adhesives, mechanical pencils
items.quote: If you see over the last few quarters. Our sales team now is more than 900 people. And if I remember correctly, last year, same time, we were close to about 800 people.

items.statement: Revenue per rupee of capex target: INR3 revenue for every INR1 invested in capacity; plan capacity enhancements at 50-60% utilization
items.quote: So basically, for us, wherever we are investing INR1 in building capacities, we target to achieve revenues of INR3. And as soon as we believe that for a particular product or a category where demand also is still strong, and we believe a lot of value DOMS can add, as soon as we reach about 50%, 60% utilization, we plan for other capacity enhancements.

items.statement: GST 2.0 reforms slashed rates on key categories (12%/5% to 0%, baby hygiene 12% to 5%); structurally positive long-term but caused temporary September disruptions
items.quote: A notable highlight for the quarter was the government's announcement of GST 2.0 reforms, slashing rates across some of our key product categories. Although we believe GST reduction is structurally positive, it led to temporary disruptions in September.

items.statement: Kits/combo packs taxed at 18% GST (mixed supply rule); standalone 0% GST items in kits become ITC eligible; no strategic shift to push kits over standalone products
items.quote: Most of our kits and combination packs are sold at a GST rate of 18%. And for the 0 percentage items that go in that kits and combination pack where you're actually charging 18%, you become eligible for input tax credit.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guided flattish vs FY25; growth expected from FY27
items.quote: In the earlier calls, the guidance that we had given for this year is that we would remain flattish in this year because these are the changes that we intend to make.

items.statement: FY27 expected to return to growth trajectory
items.quote: So FY '26 will be flattish like FY '25. And the year after that, we certainly expect to see growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided 27-30% range
items.quote: Our EBITDA will remain in the range of 27% to 30% as we've always guided. In a bad time, it could be 27%. In a good time, it could be 30%.

items.statement: Capex funded through internal accruals, no leverage planned
items.quote: So, Apurva, we -- whatever capex or growth plans we have, we should be able to fund that through internal accruals. There should not be any leverage on the balance sheet for that purpose.

items.statement: Opened 5 premium flagship stores in H1 FY26; 4-5 more in pipeline
items.quote: As a part of this transition, we opened 5 new premium flagship stores in high potential and strategic locations during H1 FY '26.

items.statement: Net store count flattish for next 2 years; opened 15, closed 13 in H1; target ~23 closures and similar openings full year
items.value: 15 opened, 13 closed in H1; ~23 closures full year
items.quote: So in H1, we have opened 15 new stores and closed 13 old stores. And we intend by the end of the year to close totally about 23 stores out of 13 have already been closed. And we intend to open a similar number of stores by the end of the year.

items.statement: Soft demand and muted footfalls in H1 FY26
items.quote: Operationally, the first half of the year, we continued to face soft demand and muted footfalls.

items.statement: H1 FY26 gross margin 59%, up 200 bps YoY due to product mix change
items.quote: Supported by a gross margin of approximately 59%, up 200 basis points year-on-year, driven by a change in product mix.

items.statement: Website sales more than doubled YoY in H1 FY26
items.quote: Sales through our website have mor e than doubled year -on-year in H1 FY '26, reflecting a stronger brand salience, improved digital image and an enhanced omnichannel journey

items.statement: Working capital days 217 in H1 FY26; expected to revert to 170-180 days as sales normalize
items.quote: Our working capital days stood at 217 days for H1 FY '26. This increase is purely a reflection of our business model and current market conditions and not a structural change.

items.statement: Receivables fully secured via deposits; zero bad debt history
items.quote: Importantly, receivables remain fully secured through deposits and long-standing partner relationships and MUFTI has never incurred a bad debt in its history.

items.statement: Bangladesh supply chain disruption delayed ~2 lakh pieces (~INR20-25 cr revenue) from Q2 to Q3
items.quote: Around 1 lakh pieces, which we expected to come from Bangladesh in September and sold got delayed to October, November. And similarly, around 1 lakh pieces, we picked up earlier from -- last year, it was in October. This time, we picked up them back in September. So around 2 lakh pieces, the sales got impacted by around 2 lakh pieces, which should be around INR20 – 25 crores.

items.statement: 60-70% of portfolio below INR2,500 realized sale price; GST rate cut benefit to be passed on
items.quote: About 60% to 70% would be below.

items.statement: Supported franchisees and MBO partners during slow liquidation; long-standing relationships
items.quote: In a softer demand environment, we supported our franchisees and MBO partners due to slight slower stock liquidation and corresponding payments.

items.statement: Brand lifecycle differs from peers like Cantabil, Rare Rabbit; confident of bounce back
items.quote: See, I would say that depends on the life cycle that the brand is in its journey. Over a period of time, we have seen many ups and downs. We are very confident that we'll bounce back to our levels again.

items.statement: GST rate changes: some products below INR2,500 benefit, some above see price increase; benefit passed on per government directive
items.quote: What we see is that higher footfalls have been created for hard goods and not so much for apparel. However, in a brand like ours, we have to wait and watch as to how it pans out because not everything we make is below INR2,500. A lot of the products we make are above.

items.statement: Investment phase may keep profitability lower for next 1.5 years; marketing spend increasing to 6-7%
items.quote: However, profitability would still be lower in the forthcoming year because we will be enhancing our expenditures on marketing.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR284 cr vs INR310 cr YoY; PAT INR25 cr; ROCE 16%, ROE 14.5%
items.quote: crores in H1 FY '26 as against INR310 crores in H1 FY '25. Gross profit stood at INR167 crores with a GP margin of 59% for the half year ended. EBITDA for H1 FY '26 stood at INR79 crores. Our EB ITDA margin stood at 27.9%. PAT for H1 FY '26 stood at INR 25 crores. Our PAT margin stood at 8.9%. ROCE and ROE as on September 2025 basis stood at 16% and 14.5%, respectively

items.statement: No plans to enter women's or kids wear in medium term
items.quote: Anywhere in the medium term, we don't have in our mind to enter the kids wear or women wear.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR 1,750 crores will not be met due to Modasa plant commissioning delay of 4-5 months
items.quote: It will definitely not be possible to meet the guidance. Initially, we were saying that we will get the commissioning in July -August. So, we were assuming that we will get the benefit in our festive season.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 8-9% for Q4 FY26 under review; will reassess after sales numbers stabilize
items.quote: As Navinji said, we are assessing the situation. So, we will assess the sales number. Accordingly, we will revert back to the margin guidance.

items.statement: GST rate reduction caused trade disruption in September-October; revenue impact of INR 15-18 crores across two months
items.quote: In September in terms of value, there was an impact of around INR 8-10 crores. And in October there was an impact of INR 3-4 crores. In total, there was an impact of INR 15-18 crores.

items.statement: Festive season contributed INR 10 crores positive growth in Q2 FY26 despite low base and supply chain issues
items.quote: If we quantify it we get a positive growth of INR 10 crores due to the festival.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gross margin 26.4% including INR 5.3 crores subsidy income; EBITDA margin 6.4%; PAT margin 6.8% with exceptional income
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR 99.2 crores, translating to a gross margin of 26.4% compared to 26% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to stay in 25-26% range for rest of FY26 with 3-4% potential upward movement in raw material prices
items.quote: We are expecting the balance of the remaining year , there will be more or less stable prices around it. 3-4% upward movement can come but not much in expectation.

items.statement: Modasa plant capex mostly complete; INR 7-8 crores remaining to be spent in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Almost majority portion is completed some portion will come in Q3 because in October trial run has started, so some portion will come in October that is Q3 which will be in the range of INR 7 crores to INR 8 crores.

items.statement: Besan plant being installed at Nagpur; INR 20 crores capex for Rajkot reinstatement; no other major capex planned
items.quote: We are installing a besan plant in Nagpur that is under process. There it will come a little and somewhere else, as of now we don't feel the further capacity requirement.

items.statement: Modasa plant trial production started; billing for 3 hero products begun; full 26-product basket expected by end of November 2025
items.quote: The billing for 3 hero products has started from there . We are adding one product every day. We are adding a total of 26 products. So, by the end of November, all the products will be added.

items.statement: Third-party manufacturing agreements at Hiriyur (Karnataka) and Kashipur (Uttarakhand) add over 10,000 metric tons per annum capacity
items.quote: Together, these facilities add over 10,000 metric tons per annum of capacity, enabling us to serve southern and northern markets more efficiently and reduce lead times.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 41-45%; target of 70% utilization pushed out to 2-2.5 years from FY27
items.quote: Yes, I am saying that our current capacity utilization is around 41% to 45% It will take around 2 to 2.5 years to reach that.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR 697.8 crores; Q2 FY26 revenue INR 375.7 crores up 16.6% Q-o-Q; H2 FY26 revenue expected to exceed INR 700 crores
items.quote: It will definitely be more than INR 700 crores.

items.statement: GST reduction improved company retention by 0.5%; distributor margin maintained at 6.6% post-GST; retailer margin unchanged at INR 51 per strip
items.quote: In channel margin, our retention goes up by 0.5%. Earlier, we were giving 7.5% to the distributor at the gross level. Since 12% was GST, he used to get 6.6% post deducting 0.9%.

items.statement: Wafer realization improved ~6% via price hikes; trade incentives reduced (retailer margin cut); channel distributor margin fixed
items.quote: If you see, in wafer, our revenue growth as compared to volume growth is higher . That is a reflection of roughly 6% higher. We have improved our realisation in wafer.

items.statement: New product launches: popcorn (sustainable run rate INR 40-43 lakhs), wafer biscuits (INR 42 lakhs), Jeera Popcorn (INR 1.05 crores in October); target to reduce palm oil dependent products by 25% in 3-5 years
items.quote: So, in next 3 to 5 years, we intend in percentage term palm oil dependent products contribution we should reduce by 25%.

items.statement: INR 5 price point SKU contribution improved from 66% to 62% in Q2 FY26; focus on improving product mix for better realizations
items.quote: In INR 5 price points sku this quarter, it has improved from 66% to 62%.

items.statement: 858 active distributors as of Q2 FY26; double service initiative re-initiated in Gujarat; expanding depth in 350km radius of Nagpur and 200km clusters at Hiriyur and Kashipur
items.quote: By Q2 FY26, we had 858 active distributors, reflecting steady expansion and better on-ground execution.

items.statement: E-commerce revenue progression: INR 1.92 crores in Q2 FY26; H1 FY26 e-commerce INR 3.5 crores vs INR 1 crore H1 FY25; modern trade INR 1.32 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our last 6 quarters e-commerce progression is INR 37 lakhs, INR 63 lakhs, INR 1.19 crores, INR 1.03 crores, INR 1.53 crores and INR 1.92 crores.

items.statement: Wafer pricing had 17% gap vs competition; price hike reduced gap but impacted volume; supply chain disruption affected distribution pull for second product
items.quote: The aggressive stance we took in the wafer, we understand that it has not been converted into numbers. In that, the price hike we took was probably because there was a 17% gap between us and the competition.

items.statement: Potato inventory covered till December 15, 2025; new crop pricing uncertain; last year Q4 potato rates rose 3.5x to INR 35/kg impacting margins
items.quote: Last year, the rate of potatoes went up disproportionately in Q4. So, we have the cover till 15th December. We expect that we will be in control at that time.

items.statement: Insurance claim: INR 19.99 crores interim payment received; total loss INR 47 crores; expecting similar amount in FY26 in 2-3 more installments
items.quote: If I talk about this financial year, we are expecting the similar amount which has come now We are expecting some amount around this in this financial year.

items.statement: Acquisition budget up to INR 200 crores; no target finalized; focus on food business in Gujarat (core states), not namkeen; funding structure to be decided later
items.quote: Madam, nothing has been finalized yet, we are seeing it now but yes, one thing will be that we will acquire it, it will be in a similar kind of industry, if not same.

items.statement: Acquisition target: similar food business in Gujarat core states; category should not cannibalize existing portfolio; focus on inside-home consumption products
items.quote: We are looking for a category that does not cannibalize our existing product category, number one. Number two, which comes under the fitment of our yard vision, that how to make a brand of inside home consumption.

items.statement: Gujarat run rate target: INR 125+ crores per month in 2-3 years; current throughput per outlet to jump 30-40% via double service and marketing
items.quote: So, in Gujarat, we aspire that in the next 2 -3 years, our run rate per month should go beyond INR 125 crores.

items.statement: Supply chain disruption to reduce 90% after full Modasa product basket; conservative estimate 6-7 months to recover lost consumer base
items.quote: After getting the full product basket from Modasa, our supply chain disruption will reduce by 90%.

items.statement: Rajkot facility reinstatement on track; production not constrained as Gondal covering output; relocation from Gondal to Rajkot when ready
items.quote: Yes, it is on track . One thing is that our production is not constrained anywhere . So, whatever will be in Rajkot will shift from Gondal to Rajkot.

items.statement: Order book stands at over INR2,600 crores with INR1,600+ crores government and INR960+ crores corporate, executable over 3 years
items.quote: And to give you a little idea on the order book, we are sitting on an order book position of more than INR2,600 crores. And it has a great bifurcation, almost more than INR1,600 crores is government and more than INR960 crores is corporate.

items.statement: Corporate revenue grew 53% YoY in H1 FY26 with 92 new clients added across pharma, manufacturing, logistics, warehouse, IT/ITES
items.quote: Revenue from this segment grew by almost 53% year-on-year in the H1 FY '26. We added 92 new corporate customers during the H1 FY '26, building on the 114 clients added in the FY '25 totally.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.32% down 7 bps YoY due to higher employee and admin costs from expansion; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.47% up 11 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding the other income for the quarter stood INR17.91 crores, up 5.3% year-on-year. Despite moderate growth in operating profit, EBITDA margin declined slightly by 7 basis points to 6.32% primarily due to higher employee and administrative cost associated with business expansion and establishment of new offices as a part of our pan-India penetration strategy.

items.statement: Cost of material consumed rose from INR18 crores to INR48 crores due to capex in IT/ITES smart city business where capex incurred before billing
items.quote: In our service profile, we also have our the -- IT/ITES business, which is a smart city business that we have been doing. So when this business is rolled out, the re is a certain capex, which is done in this vertical first and then the billing happens. So therefore, you are seeing a little spurge in the capex.

items.statement: Total branches increased to 33 from 26 at FY25 end as part of pan-India penetration strategy
items.quote: Today, our total branches stand at 33 as compared to 26 as on FY '25.

items.statement: All contracts are variable with inflation pass-through; pricing methodology based on headcount or square foot remains unchanged
items.quote: So these are variable contracts where we get a benefit of any fluctuation or any inflation that takes place. Rushil: All

items.statement: Receivables improved with substantial collections in last month; working capital expected to come back on track
items.quote: These numbers actually have improved because there has been substantial amount of collection, which has already come in the last month. So therefore, going forward, the situation what is reported is not going to be there. So our working capital will come back on track.

items.statement: Strategic bidding for profitable tenders only; added security manpower to Delhi Education contract; expanding into O&M, wastewater, solid waste, ports, solar EPC
items.quote: We consciously chose to build only for projects which offer healthy margins. And therefore, there were a couple of tenders that we chose intentionally not to bid. So this strategic call, I'm sure, is going to strengthen our margins in the coming quarters and the years to come and have a good balance as we always have between top line growth and healthy margins.

items.statement: Corporate client quality significantly better than prior year; penetration across pharma, manufacturing, logistics, warehouse, IT/ITES; MNCs welcoming participation post-listing
items.quote: The quality of these clients is significantly better than what we acquired in the earlier year. Also our penetration into various segments has been way better. So I will be very, very happy to tell you that now we are across length and breadth of various sectors, whether it is pharma, manufacturing, logistics, warehouse, IT /ITES, so on and so forth.

items.quote: Krystal Aquachem it is 97%. Krystal Aquachem, it is 97%. It is not 100%.

So that delay -- so for example, if you are in the last week of the quarter ending and the documentation spills over the next quarter, my reporting actually spills over the next quarter, all of a sudden.

items.statement: Employee costs rose due to hiring experienced teams across business development, service delivery, back-end operations for pan-India expansion and new subsidiaries

We view this as an investment in future scalability and operational resilience.

And this should get completed in the next, I think, seven to eight months. And afte

items.quote: Post our listing status, we also are welcomed by a lot of MNCs. There are many MNCs in various sectors who are coming. Because of our listing status now the companies are welcoming us to participate in the

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 17-20% for FY26 with EBITDA margin target of 13-15% and PAT margin of 8-10%
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect to maintain top-line growth in the range of around 17% to 20%, supported by margin stability through technology-led efficiencies.

items.statement: Conservative FY26 revenue guidance of 17-20% despite 28% H1 growth, expecting to outperform
items.quote: Although we maintain our 17% to 20% forecast, yes, we are conservative in our forecast, but we would outperform rather than overpromise.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 11.47% down 333 bps YoY due to Rs 79.14M doubtful debt provision; underlying margin flat YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margin comes at 11.47% down from 14.79% last year. That means 333 basic point decline, which was mainly due to, as Rajesh said, one-time, Rs. 79.14 million doubtful debt provision.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin 11.74% vs 14.36% YoY; excluding one-time provision, margins roughly flat YoY
items.quote: H1 EBITDA reached to Rs. 464.2 million, that is 4.8% increase over last year with an EBITDA margin of 11.74% as compared to 14.36% in FY '25. Again, excluding the Rs. 79.14 million one-time provision, our H1 margin are roughly flat year-on-year.

items.statement: Q2 volumes grew 33.5% YoY; onboarded 67 new enterprise clients, active base up 39% to 1,470
items.quote: Total volumes grew by a healthy 33.5% in Q2 FY '26 compared to Q2 FY '25. It reflected sustained enterprise demand and underscored our ability to scale rapidly and efficiently across high value mobility segments.

items.statement: Added 67 new enterprise clients in Q2 across IT, BFSI, pharma, manufacturing, consulting; active client base 1,470
items.quote: During the quarter, we on boarded 67 new enterprise clients, taking our active client base to 1,470, almost a 39% increase over Q2 FY '25. These new engagements span key sectors such as IT, BFSI, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, and consulting.

items.statement: Fleet expanded to 18,000+ vehicles including 1,002 owned; added ~3,200 vehicles in Q2 YoY
items.quote: Our fleet capacity expanded to over 18,000 vehicles in use today. This includes 1,002 owned units, enabling an agile, yet asset-light scalability. During Q2 FY '26, we added almost 3,200 vehicles, which include both owned and outsourced fleet, as compared to Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: H1 capex ~Rs 18 crore, mostly vehicle purchases (~Rs 17 cr) and ~Rs 1 cr tech investments
items.quote: It is mostly vehicle purchase and some tech investments also. Approximately Rs. 1 crores is towards the tech investments and the rest is all vehicle purchase.

items.statement: Actively looking for acquisition targets with exponential benefits; cash reserved as dry gunpowder
items.quote: we are adding on. And rest, we are also leaving enough dry gunpowder if we find the right acquisition target which gives an exponential kind of benefit to the organization so that we are ready with the cash to put into it

items.statement: ~1,100 employees, ~800 frontline operations; headcount grows proportionately with revenue at frontline level
items.quote: So, out of this almost more than 1,100 employees, almost 800 are actually operations team on the ground. And this strength tends to increase proportionate to the increase in the revenue.

items.statement: Conservative guidance to buffer for black swan events; business first to get affected in downturns
items.quote: Typically, even a Black Swan happens, we are the first to get affected. So, we would like to take a conservative stance only.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 25-30% from previous 25%
items.quote: On the back of this visibility and a strong H1 FY26, we are revising our top-line growth guidance for FY26 from 25% 30%.

items.statement: FY26 pre-IndAS EBITDA margin guided at 7-8%, pre-IndAS PAT margin at 3-4%
items.quote: Our pre-IndAS EBITDA margin is g uided at 7 -8% and pre -IndAS PAT margin at 3 -4

items.statement: FY26 IndAS EBITDA guided at 14-15%, IndAS PAT margin without exceptional gain at 2-3%
items.quote: IndAS EBITDA is guided at 14-15% and IndAS PAT margin without exceptional gain will be between 2-3%.

items.statement: FY27 pre-IndAS PAT margin target of 4-5%
items.quote: The target for FY27 is between 4 to 5%, the PAT on the pre-IndAS.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth aspiration of 25% with SSSG of 6-7%
items.quote: I would like to start the year with a 25% revenue structure. And as the year goes, if there is an increase, we would change the guidance. But the business plan will be created on the 25% revenue growth with the SSSG of again 6-7%.

items.statement: FY26 total capex planned at INR 100 crores, INR 20 crores for H2
items.quote: So, our plan is to have around INR 100 crores as our total CAPEX throughout the year. And as we have already opened more than 36 stores in the first half, I think our target is to open between 40 to 50 stores. So, for the balance 6 months, the INR 20 crores is the planned CAPEX that we have in our mind.

items.statement: Digital transformation investment of INR 20-25 crores in FY26 for SAP, Infor, Domo implementation
items.quote: We are making significant headway in our digital and warehouse transformation journey with a planned investment of INR 20-25 crores this year towards building an integrated and intelligent technology backbone.

items.statement: Target 40-50 net store openings in FY26, 36 added in H1, 38 total so far, ~10 more in pipeline
items.quote: We are well on track to meet our new store opening guidance, having achieved 72% of our FY26 target with 36 net stores added in the first half, we are in guidance with the growth of 40 -50 stores for this fiscal year.

items.statement: Total retail area 2.3 million sq ft, up 38% YoY; 250 stores total, 152 mature (L2L), rest under 18 months
items.quote: Total store count reached 250 in Q2 FY26 up 36% year-on-year, retail area now stands at 2.3 million square feet, a 38% increase from last year.

items.statement: Private label sales grew 119% YoY in Q2 FY26, contributing 58% of sales; target 65% by FY27
items.quote: The growth traction continued in our private label sales, which grew 119% year-on-year in Q2 FY26 and contributed to 58% of overall sales.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gross margin 31%, up ~90 bps YoY; full-year gross margin expansion guided at 50 bps to ~34%
items.quote: Gross margin remains healthy at 31%, expanding by nearly 90 bps on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: H1 FY26 pre-IndAS store-level EBITDA 12.83%, corporate cost 6%; mature stores ~14% EBITDA
items.quote: So, at the company level, our total EBITDA stands at 6.8% on pre -IndAS, out of which the store stands at 12.83% and 6% is the HO cost for the first half of this year.

items.statement: Passed on full 6.25% GST benefit to consumers across all MRPs above INR 1,000, including negligible >INR 2,500 items
items.quote: We have passed on because that is a very negligible quantity that we have in the store. So, we have passed on the entire 6.25% benefit to the consumer or across all the MRPs above INR 1,000.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced to 86 in Q2 FY26 from 108 in Q2 FY25; trade payable days 70 vs 81 YoY
items.quote: Inventory days for the quarter reduced to 86 from 108 days while trade payable days stood at 70 compared to 81 for the same period last year.

items.statement: Expect further inventory reduction by March 31 with ARS system implementation
items.quote: And I believe that the ARS system and the thing that we are implementing on the tech side, we are working on reduce further. So, you will see that in expecting the 31st of March also.

items.statement: Lease reassessment under IndAS 116 yielded one-time exceptional gain of INR 55 crores; will reduce pre/post-IndAS profit gap
items.quote: As a result, we recognize a one -time exceptional gain of INR 55 crores which has been disclosed separately in the financials. Going forward, this will help in reducing the gap between the pre-IndAS and IndAS profitability.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS depreciation to increase 10% QoQ (INR 10 cr to INR 11 cr quarterly); IndAS depreciation+interest benefit INR 5 cr QoQ
items.quote: Because of the reassessment, our leasehold improvement depreciation will increase, right, and that will be a 10% increment quarter-on-quarter going forward.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 same-store sales growth 22%, H1 FY26 10%; focus states SSSG 13% vs core 10% in H1
items.quote: Same-store sale growth stood at 22% in Q2 FY26 and 10% in H1 FY26.

items.statement: Sales per sq ft 865 in Q2 FY26, up 22% YoY; H1 FY26 768, up 12% YoY
items.quote: Sales per square feet stood at 865 in Q2 FY26, up 22% year–on-year and 768 in H1 FY26, up 12% from last year.

items.statement: New stores in Metro/Tier-1 yield SPSF >INR 10,000; Tier-2/3/4 ~INR 8,000-8,500; new stores this year averaging >9,000 SPSF
items.quote: Metro stores typically gives you a SPSF of more than INR 10,000 per square feet, whereas, Tier 2, Tier-3 gives you a SPSF of around INR 8,000 to INR 8,500 typically.

items.statement: New store ramp-up: Year 1 EBITDA 5-6%, Year 2 8-10%, mature Tier-2/3/4 13-15%, Metro/Tier-1 12% (pre-IndAS store-level)
items.quote: when a store gets open ed, so the financial year that it gets open ed, it delivers a EBITDA of 5-6% on an average. And when it completes one full year, it gives you EBITDA of 8 - 10%. And on the maturity, which is the L2L stage, it gives you EBITDA of 13-15% if you are in Tier 2, Tier-3, Tier 4. And if you are in Metro and Tier 1, it gives you around 12% of EBITDA when it gets matured

items.statement: Q2 demand boosted by early Durga Puja; Q3 strong with winter, wedding, Chhat festivals; winter traction good so far
items.quote: For us, because the festival of Durga Puja came in September, so obviously there has been a preponement of festival which led to a higher growth in Q2. But while saying that, Q3 remains a very strong quarter for us both in terms of revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment positive across zones; rain impact Sept 15-Oct 15; winter sales uptick good
items.quote: So, in terms of consumer sentiment, I think we have witnessed a positive sentiment across the zone. The only challenge was I think with the rain this time, the rain effect was from end of September till 15th of October. So, the rain was there. But apart from that, the footfall looks good to us.

items.statement: 12-15% of assortment priced above INR 1,000; very low sales contribution from >INR 1,000 items
items.quote: Maybe 12% to 15% of the assortment is above INR 1,000 range. So, the percentage of sales is very lower on the INR 1,000 and above side on the garment side.

items.quote: In terms of product, as we speak, it is not that the fabric, there has been a tax change in the fabric side. items.quote: I think it will take at least FY28 I would say things to get settled in terms of revenue contribution coming from both Bengal, Assam and other states put together.

items.statement: Winter sales unpredictable; climate changes can suddenly drop sales; conservative 30% guidance maintained
items.quote: But the winter is very unpredictable, now it looks good, and we have seen over the years, sometimes the climate changes suddenly which leads to a drop of sale also.

items.statement: Insurance claim: asset portion INR 3.48 cr received; inventory claim assessment in progress, no fixed timeline
items.quote: On the insurance claim, as we said in the last call also that we have received already the asset part, which is INR 3.48 crores. And in relation to the inventory, the company has submitted all the documents related to the insurance claim and the assessment process by the insurance is in progress.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 144 crores with 70:30 export-domestic split; INR 10 crores spills into H1 FY27, rest to be executed in H2 FY26
items.quote: As on date, our order book stands at INR 144 crores, with a similar 70:30 ratio of exports to domestic sales.

items.statement: Order book was INR 131 crores on 30th September last year, now INR 144 crores
items.quote: Order book in September'24 was INR 131 crores. Compared to that, this year order book is INR 144 crores.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining EBITDA margins similar to previous year (~14%); Q1-Q2 margins lower due to exhibition expenses that will spread out in H2
items.quote: Coming back to margins, yes, we are confident that we will maintain the margins as for our previous year.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 deferred; order intake window open for 6 weeks (converting), 4 weeks (packaging), 2-3 weeks (extrusion)
items.quote: Like I said, we still have a window for new order booking and execution in coming in current financial year. That window is approximately six weeks. So, we would like to wait for six weeks before we can give a figure, or we can float a figure for our investors.

items.statement: US tariff headwinds assessed as transient; diversified portfolio and growing global footprint provide natural hedge
items.quote: Our assessment is that these headwinds are transient, and we remain fully committed to our presence in the US market.

items.statement: US exposure is INR 15 crores out of INR 144 crores order book; historically ~15% of top line from USA alone
items.quote: Out of that 70%, the US exposure is about INR 15 crores.

items.quote: Now, as things stand today in Mamata Enterprises, the execution in current financial year in Mamata Enterprises is approximately INR 41 crores.

items.quote: we have been able to create a film structure by making spe cial designs in our co -extrusion blown film lines. That would allow somebody to make a good barrier film at a much lower cost. items.statement: Aggressive recruitment program to expand US sales and service team; spent ~quarter million dollars at PACK Expo
items.quote: In fact, our resolve to become stronger in the U.S. market has increased. The proof is that we have currently an extremely aggressive recruitment program to expand our sales team as well as our services.

items.quote: The answer is INR 71 crores and not INR 41 crores. So, I stand corrected. The cash on hand as on 30th September was INR 71 crores.

items.statement: Building war chest to finance opportunistic acquisitions identified in near future for inorganic growth
items.quote: We are building up war chest for financing our expansion plans a nd also finance any opportunistic acquisitions that we may identify in near future because the growth can be had organically as well as inorganic

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with no bank line of credit; operating through own approvals
items.quote: We continue to remain debt free almost and we do not see that thing changing. We are operating thr ough our own approvals. We do not even have a line of credit from the bank

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow in H1 due to cash converted into FDs (non-current); FDs ~INR 41 crores
items.quote: The additional cash that was approved has been converted into FDs and because FDs are not considered as current, they are considered as non-current.

items.quote: As of now, our assured business stands at about INR 63 crores as compared to INR 46 crores. Currently, we sell our packaging machine lines only in In dia and in North America. Right? items.quote: So, basically you will do INR 64 crores versus INR 36 crores machinery sales

items.statement: Claims leadership in recyclable film technology with first-mover advantage; non-recyclable film consumption ~10 lakh tons in India FMCG, 10% annual conversion would be substantial
items.quote: We are leading this. So, we are leaders of the pack. Obviously, there is a pack. The word that I am using is a pack. So, that means there is going to be competition. But since we will have the first mover advantage in this particular case, we should be able to garner a good chunk of the market expansion that will happen.

items.statement: EPR norms under Solid Waste Management Rules 2018 driving recyclable packaging adoption in India; Gen Z consumer preference also a factor
items.quote: Regulatory norms are EPR and they are well stated. You can always read it up. It is called Solid State Management Rule 2018.

items.statement: 70:30 export-domestic ratio maintained; US tariffs apply only to sales within USA, not to Canada/Central-South America routed through US subsidiary
items.quote: Only for the sales that happen within USA. There is no tariff applicable within USA for sales that are done by Mamata Enterprises into Central South America or Canada.

items.statement: Two full-time packaging sales people in place led by President Rajashekar Venkat for Europe/Middle East expansion
items.quote: First of all we do have a team in place. So, we h ave two full time people in place for packaging. And these two people have been led by our President Mr. Rajashekar

items.statement: Aspiration of 18-20% medium-term growth unchanged but 'trumped like everybody else'; US tariff challenges considered transient
items.quote: The aspiration has not changed. But to some extent we have been trumped like everybody else.

items.statement: VFFS machine has 3 brand owner customers; expecting a few more orders soon
items.quote: Now we have about three customers who are using or three brand owners who are using this machine from Mamata. And we do expect a few more orders in the near future.

items.statement: Aftermarket spares/services 5-7% of top line; not tracked or pushed actively
items.quote: We do not really track aftermarket sales for us. T hat is not important because it i s not a significant part of our top line. It happens to be between 5% and 7

items.statement: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 FY26 due to strong order book
items.quote: It will be definitely improving as Q3, Q4 looks good. We have got enough orders. But then right now we can't comment on what will be it, but definitely it will improve.

items.statement: International markets face challenges; UK economy sluggish; US tariff impact minimal at 0.2% of gross margin decline
items.quote: The international market where we operate currently has its own challenges which we are all aware of and we have been sailing through it quite okay up to now.

items.statement: Gross margin fell from 39.27% in Q1 to 36.18% in Q2 due to customer mix change and a one-time INR3.3 crore raw material sale
items.quote: Our gross margin has declined from quarter 1 to quarter 2 from 39.27% to 36.18%. So, the reason for that 3% down is mainly due to the customer mix change.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined due to fixed costs from new Manekpur and Guwahati plants before sales ramp-up; expected to recover at optimal utilization
items.quote: As for EBITDA, the EBITDA has gone down as the fixed expenses has started incurring in Manekpur and Guwahati. But the sales as demand was less so the sales was not as expected.

items.statement: New orders secured from US and Australian customers; Australian market opportunity described as very huge; Japanese retailer order also closed
items.quote: We added one client last quarter and also if you look at Target, they awarded us with the award for the best diversification supplier, where we are engaging them very well for the next two quarters also.

items.statement: Bamboo pilot samples approved by large customer; trial order to ship in Q3 FY26 from pilot facility; commercial plant under planning
items.quote: Our bamboo samples have now been approved by one of our large customers and we have received our trial order which will be shipped in terms of the last quarter of this month from our pilot facility currently of this year.

items.statement: Khatalwada factory building expansion to complete by December end or January first week; administrative block expansion also on track
items.quote: The expansion of the factory building is on track and we are closing the factory building expansion by December end, January first week. The expansion will be completed.

items.statement: Capacity reached 37,000 metric tons at September end; 4,000 metric tons added in last week of September; FY26 exit capacity target 46,500 metric tons; FY27 target 52,500 metric tons
items.quote: By FY '26, it will be 46,500. And remaining 6,000 will be in '27. So it will be 52,500.

items.statement: Realisation per kg declined from 225-228 to 213 range due to lower raw material costs passed to customers and higher share of large customers
items.quote: The material is also, because we are passing on the material, if the material cost has also gone down, then we are passing that to the customers. So, that is one of the reasons.

items.statement: B2C margins better than B2B; B2C realisation example 250-270 vs 200 for B2B; domestic share target 25% from current 17%
items.quote: B2C, it is a little better as compared to B2B. Previous to this. Yes. So, previous quarter, you are talking about Q2 of last year and Q2 of this year or Q1 to Q2

items.statement: UK FTA no impact as products already duty-free; EU FTA eagerly awaited and expected to give significant landed cost advantage vs China
items.quote: UA FTA, we are eagerly looking forward and we definitely feel we will have a great advantage with the EU FTA happening because our business does drive by European Union market today.

items.statement: US share currently 9%-10%; internal target to grow to 15%-20%; domestic target 25%; focus on nearer geographies to reduce supply chain risk
items.quote: Internally, we would like to have that between the all like USA is right now at 9%-10%. Even if it's close up to 15%-20%, it is fine.

items.statement: 95% of IPO debt repaid; remaining to be paid in Q3 FY26; debt-equity ratio now 0.2
items.quote: On the utilization of IPO funds, we have paid 95% of the debt as per the object. So, out of that, 95% we have paid and remaining will be paying in this Q3. So, debt equity now stands at 0.2.

items.statement: Revenue Q2 FY26 INR147 crores, up 12.5% YoY; H1 FY26 INR305 crores, up 17% YoY
items.quote: Our Q2 numbers were closed at INR147 crores. It was a 12.5% on Q2 to Q2. The H1 number closed at INR305 crores. From H1 to H1 comparison, we have a growth of 17%.

items.statement: US tariff impact minimal at 0.2% of gross margin decline; US share small; no significant discounts passed on for tariffs
items.quote: So, as for the impact of US tariff on the margins, I will answer that question. So, it is very minimum, around 0.2% out of that 3% as the US share is lesser.

items.statement: Order book exceeds INR 4,000 crore as of the call date, with 82% Power T&D, 17% Water, balance Railway
items.quote: As of today, 2025, our total order book is more than INR 4000 crores, providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters. The Power Transmission & Distribution segment continues to be our key growth driver , accounting to about 82% of the order book , followed by the Water segment with 17%.

items.statement: Two large solar EPC orders won: INR 355 crore from Ellume Energy and INR 1,642 crore from Carbonminus Maharashtra One
items.quote: I am happy to share that recently we have awarded 2 prestigious turnkey EPC contracts in the Solar segment, a INR 355 crore project from Ellume Energy MH Solar One Private Limited. for a 100 MW solar power project in Maharashtra , and subsequently a very big leap to our growth journey, another big order of INR 1,642 crore single project from Carbonminus Maharashtra One Project Limited.

items.statement: With current working capital, company can reach ~INR 2,500 crore turnover without additional working capital
items.quote: previously we were using about INR 300 to INR 400 crores of working capital for the INR 900 crores of business. items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margins expected to remain in line with last 3 financial years
items.quote: And the margins, what you are saying for the full year as we discussed, we are expecting it to remain in the similar line as it was in last 3 financial years.

items.statement: Solar EPC margins on new orders are better than industry 10-12% range due to non-DCR modules, hurdle-free land, and supplier tie-ups
items.quote: And this is non -DCR, the modules, and the pricing is better, and the margins are much more better from the industry now, today. So, this is what we can see , because we always believe in bringing the highest margin orders.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin lower due to seasonality (25-30% of annual revenue in H1) and fixed cost absorption; H2 margins improve
items.quote: So, generally our H1 is about 25% to 30% of the total turnover of the year, as per the past trend. And the margins, what you are saying for the full year as we discussed, we are expecting it to remain in the similar line as it was in last 3 financial years.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR 541 crore deployed for working capital and project execution as envisaged
items.quote: The proceeds from our IPO are being effectively utilized to support working capital needs and the execution of the ongoing as well as newly secured projects, exactly as envisaged at the time of listing.

items.statement: Current order book executable in 18 months; new T&D orders 18-24 months execution timeline
items.quote: So, the current order book what we are having, that has to be executed in 18 months. And whatever the new order comes now in the T&D, that also ranges from 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Order book split approximately 60% private, 40% government (corrected from earlier 50-50)
items.quote: And finally, what I just wanted to ensure my investors, see we have just began now. items.statement: Management acknowledges Africa tender market is cutthroat on pricing; chooses private market (20% share) with niche portfolio for higher margins over tender volume

items.statement: MD personally travels ~180 days/year for market due diligence; spent 7-8 days in Algeria recently assessing market, distributors, regulations

items.quote: We are working with Safran also in the automation, which is one project is going on, will be delivered, I think in another 15 days to the Singapore Safran, it's an export order.

items.quote: One more order is there already in our hand, but unfortunately, it is getting hold for our geopolitical situation, but we are optimistic and let us see.

items.quote: That electricity act amendment proposal has come and they had asked for comments. We have given our comments.
