We are importing more than 50 different types of aluminium scrap, the scrap complexity

items.statement: SGF voluntary contribution policy: 5% of transaction revenue monthly, capped at 150% of minimum requirement
items.quote: BSE has decided to make voluntary core SGF contributions in line with the revenue as long as overall SGF is not exceeding 150% of the minimum requirement.

items.statement: Q2 FY26: 97 new equity listings raised Rs 53,548 crores; October 2025: 45 IPOs raised Rs 41,856 crores
items.quote: In Q2 FY'26, BSE welcomed 97 new equity listings across both the main and SME boards, raising a total of Rs. 53,548 crores.

items.statement: SME platform: 657 listed companies as of October 2025, collectively raised over Rs 13,083 crores since launch
items.quote: As of October 2025, the platform hosts 657 listed companies which have collectively raised over Rs. 13,083 crores since launch.

items.statement: Passive products tracking BSE indices AUM reached Rs 2.54 lakh crores as of September 2025
items.quote: As of September 2025, passive products tracking our indices have accumulated Rs. 2.54 lakh crores in asset under management.

items.statement: BSE StAR MF transactions grew 24% YoY to 20.1 crore in Q2 FY26; October 2025 hit 7.13 crore transactions
items.quote: The total number of transactions processed by BSE StAR MF grew by 24% to reach 20.1 crore transactions in Q2 FY'26 from 16.2 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin expanded to 64% from 52% YoY in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The operating EBITDA including contribution to core SGF has increased to Rs. 680 crores as compared to Rs. 388 crores with margins expanding to 64% from 52%.

items.statement: Consolidated operational revenue grew 44% YoY to Rs 1,068 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: BSE's operational revenues have grown by 44% to Rs. 1,068 crores from Rs. 740 crores.

items.statement: Transaction charges revenue increased 57% YoY to Rs 794 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Transaction charges, which include equity cash, equity derivatives, mutual fund and clearing house income has increased by 57% to Rs. 794 crores from Rs. 507 crores.

items.statement: Co-location revenue rose to Rs 46 crores in Q2 FY26 from Rs 27 crores previous quarter
items.quote: During the quarter under review, revenue from co-location rose to Rs. 46 crores compared to Rs. 27 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Capital work in progress of Rs 313 crores in H1 FY26 for physical and technology infrastructure
items.quote: Rs. 313 crores is not a small number. It is a big number. It is a mix of multiple things, including the physical and technology infrastructure.

items.statement: Clearing capacity scaled from 3,000 to 27,000 trades per second per broker per client; expecting 70-90 more co-location racks by FY26 end
items.quote: We took it up to around 27,000 trades per second per broker per client, which if you benchmark, is much ahead of what one of the largest trading members in this country could be generating.

items.statement: Total investor accounts crossed 23 crores in Q2 FY26 with 10 states having over 1 crore investors each
items.quote: The total number of investor accounts registered with BSE crossed 23 crores in Q2 FY2026, with 10 states registering more than 1 crore investors.

items.statement: Market share gains in derivatives driven by deeper liquidity and institutional participation; not tracking market share numbers directly
items.quote: Our intention and our work cont inues to be in deepening and broadening of markets. We have been taking multiple steps in including more number of participants, more number of members, and more FPIs

items.statement: Common contract note implemented effective June 27, 2025; smart order routing adoption underway
items.quote: We are pleased to share that the common contract note was successfully implemented in India effective 27th June 2025, addressing a long-standing request from BSE and marking a significant market reform.

items.statement: Core SGF corpus stood at Rs 1,159 crores as of October 2025 with Rs 10.6 crores contributed in Q2
items.quote: As of October 2025, BSE's core SGF stood at Rs. 1,159 crores with an additional Rs. 10.6 crores contributed during the quarter which is due to the new policy.

items.statement: Index derivatives average daily premium turnover over Rs 15,000 crores; focusing on longer-dated contracts and monthly options
items.quote: The BSE index derivative segment sustained its growth trajectory in the quarter with average daily premium turnover of over Rs. 15,000 crores.

items.statement: EbiX insurance platform underperforming vs StAR MF; management initiating deep rethink on strategy
items.quote: EbiX has not taken off and I think if we look at the entire country, the mutual fund performance levels are very different as compared to the insurance scheme's performance levels.

items.statement: SGF contribution policy designed to prevent sudden earnings volatility from unpredictable SGF requirement spikes
items.quote: Basically, in simple English, it is to ensure that no single quarter suddenly has jerks in the earning because of new emergence of additional requirement of core SGF to be contributed by BSE.

items.statement: Retail participation strong: SIP inflows hit all-time high of Rs 29,529 crores in October 2025; equity MF inflows Rs 24,691 crores
items.quote: SIP inflows through mutual funds reached an all-time high of Rs. 29,529 crores in October 2025, while equity mutual fund inflows for October 2025 stood at Rs. 24,691 crores.

items.statement: Treasury income from clearing and settlement funds decreased 32% YoY to Rs 42 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Treasury income from clearing and settlement funds has decreased by 32% to Rs. 42 crores from Rs. 63 crores.

items.statement: ICCL clearing charges income around Rs 32 crores in Q2 FY26; full impact of new members to be realized in coming quarters
items.quote: The clearing charges income of ICCL is around Rs. 32 crores this quarter and on an ongoing basis, we have to wait and watch because all these implementations and all these new members are happening one behind the other.

items.statement: Plan to add 60 screens in FY26 (17 added in H1, targeting 41 in H2) and 60-75 screens in FY27
items.quote: We'll be introducing around 50 to 60 screens by this financial year end, and we'll be adding another 60 to 75 screens by next financial year end, which is FY27.

items.statement: Long-term target of 1,000 screens by 2030
items.quote: Looking further ahead, by 2030, we aim to operate around 1,000 screens—our ambitious, long-term goal for the company.

items.statement: Added 17 screens in H1 FY26; total portfolio at 31 cinemas, 83 screens, 6,831 seats across 9 states
items.quote: Connplex delivered strong momentum in H1FY26, adding 17 new screens, 2 CAGR growth of 66% with several more in advanced stages and expected to open in the second half of the financial year once unit occupancy certificates are received.

items.statement: H2 FY26 target of 41 screens; 16 screens ready awaiting licensing, 2 in Mundra, several in Bihar pending post-election licenses
items.quote: So, for H2, our target is around 41 screens. Out of these, more than 16 screens are in our licensing process, and two more are in Mundra. So, roughly 18 screens are ready and can start operations at any time.

items.statement: Order book for next two years; LoIs completed and franchisee fee of ₹5 lakh per screen (₹15 lakh per cinema) received for almost all
items.quote: We have order book ready for about next two years. We'll be introducing around 50 to 60 screens by this financial year end, and we'll be adding another 60 to 75 screens by next financial year end, which is FY27.

items.statement: H1 FY26 footfall 12.16 lakh viewers, up 69% YoY; occupancy improved to 32% from 30%
items.quote: During H1FY26, we welcomed 12.16 lakh viewers, representing a growth of 69% YoY. Occupancy levels improved to 32% from 30% last year, reflecting both robust content performance and our focused footfall-enhancing initiatives.

items.statement: ATP grew 6% YoY to ₹243 from ₹229; F&B spend per head ₹94; ATP expected to continue increasing YoY with inflation
items.quote: Our Average Ticket Price grew 6% YoY to ₹243 from ₹229, while Food & Beverage Spend Per Head stood at ₹94.

items.statement: ATP in line with multiplex industry average (~₹250); no strategy to reduce prices, focus on service and experience
items.quote: There isn't much difference compared to other cinema chains. Their average ticket price is around ₹250, while ours is approximately ₹243. So, we are more or less in line with the multiplex industry average.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 27.87%, down 366 bps YoY due to higher operational and expansion costs; margin fluctuation within 3-4% based on revenue mix
items.quote: EBITDA Margin stood at 27.87%, a decline of 366 bps YoY, primarily due to higher operational and expansion-related costs.

items.statement: Royalty model: 80:20 revenue share (80% franchisee, 20% Connplex) on ticket, F&B, advertising; VPF and convenience fees 100% Connplex
items.quote: Sir, we follow an 80:20 revenue-sharing model, where 80% goes to the franchisee and 20% is retained by us as royalty from ticket sales, F&B sales, and advertising revenue.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue breakup: ₹29.86 cr cinema construction, ₹25 cr ticket sales, ₹3 cr F&B royalty, ₹1.12 cr advertising, ₹1.12 cr other revenue share, ₹1.7 cr VPF
items.quote: We have generated revenue of INR 29.85 crores from the income from setting up a cinema, INR 25 crore of income from selling of a ticket, INR 3 crore of income from revenue share from F&B and INR 1.12 crore from advertisement income, INR 1.12 crore from other revenue sharing income and INR 1.7 crore from VPF income.

items.statement: Operating cash flow lower than profit due to expansion-phase working capital investment: bulk procurement, construction debtor days 45-60 days
items.quote: Yes sir, this is because the company is in an expansion phase and is now aggressively focusing on developing new cinemas. We have also started bulk purchasing materials at more cost-effective prices. These efforts will reflect as a benefit in the next half year

items.statement: Receivable days increased to ~60 days (from 25 in FY24) due to construction receivables; operational settlements weekly (10-15 days)
items.quote: In the case of cinema construction, when our team is working at a site, the payments from franchisees may sometimes vary. For instance, if an installment is due on the 15th but the franchisee pays on the 20th or 30th, we still need to continue the work.

items.statement: IPO funds ₹24 cr for LEDs/projectors; ₹1.4 cr utilized in ~30 days post-August 14; remaining ₹23 cr to be deployed progressively with screen rollout
items.quote: As you may have seen, the IPO funds were received around August 14, and after that, it took us about 25 to 30 days to effectively begin utilizing those funds. Within those 30 days, we utilized approximately INR 1.40 crores for purchasing our technological assets.

items.statement: Centralized procurement of chairs, ACs, carpets, sound systems, curtains with Connplex branding; bulk ordering reduces cost despite logistics
items.quote: In inventory, we include the complete setup that we do for a franchise — for example, the chairs we order, the air conditioners, carpets, sound systems, and curtains we procure. All of these are properly stored in one place.

items.statement: Renegotiated projector prices: DCI 2K from ₹27.5L to ₹27L; non-DCI from ~₹5L to ~₹4L; Spectra model ~₹17-18L per auditorium
items.quote: The projector that originally cost INR 27.5 lakhs, we managed to bring down to INR 27 lakhs we've reduced the price again. On top of that, for the projector that cost around INR 5 lakhs, we also renegotiated about INR 1 lakh lower.

items.statement: Three cinema models: Express (8 screens added H1), Signature (3), Luxuriance (6); expanding across Tier 1-4 cities
items.quote: In H1FY26, the company added 8 Screens in Express Model, 3 Screens in Signature Model and 6 Screens in Luxuriance Model.

items.statement: Focus on untapped/underserved Tier 2/3 towns (e.g., Siwan, Bhagalpur, Ahmednagar); 25% franchisee repeat rate (23-24 of 88 screens)
items.quote: The fastest growth is definitely coming from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. While we do have cinemas in Tier 1 cities and metros, the most attractive markets currently are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations.

items.statement: Franchise agreements include penalties, control over real estate, finance, technology; LoI with ₹5L/screen non-refundable upfront fee
items.quote: So, we have a process of first doing an LoI (Letter of Intent) with the franchisee. That LoI is more or less an outline of the franchise agreement. But, more or less, almost everyone's LoI has been completed, and everyone's franchisee fee is INR 5 lakhs per screen.

items.statement: No cannibalization with PVR/INOX; operate in separate markets (towns with no/old cinema); compete on service/experience not price
items.quote: Connplex operates in a separate market rather than engaging in cannibalization. Many of our cinemas are located in towns that either had only an old single-screen theatre or had no cinema at all.

items.statement: Advertising revenue up 107% YoY to ₹112.38 lakh; VPF income ₹1.7 cr in H1, expected to reach ₹3-4 cr with scale
items.quote: Advertising revenue also maintained strong traction, up 107% YoY to ₹112.38 lakhs.

items.statement: Content pipeline strong: 20+ films crossed ₹100 cr in H1; upcoming multi-language blockbusters (De De Pyaar De 2, Avatar: Fire and Ash, Border 2, etc.)
items.quote: Looking ahead, the pipeline for upcoming releases remains very encouraging, with an exciting mix of multi-language blockbusters such as De De Pyaar De 2, 120 Bahadur, Tere Ishq Mein, Avatar: Fire and Ash, Border 2, Mardaani 3, Love & War, and many more.

items.statement: Seasonality depends on content; festive season usually strong but no significant H2 vs H1 difference
items.quote: It all depends upon content. If the move goes well, automatically it will start happening. The festival season usually goes well, sir

items.statement: Bihar cinema licenses delayed due to elections; construction revenue recognition lags signing by 6-12 months for possession + 3-4 months build
items.quote: In Bihar, several cinema licenses are pending due to elections. Once the elections are over, these screens will start operating.

items.statement: No diversification into gaming/other entertainment; focus solely on cinemas; small gaming zone inside cinema conceived 2 years ago but not pursued
items.quote: No, sir. We are focusing only on cinema

items.statement: FY27 net profit target Rs 18-20 crore
items.quote: In FY'27 we expect make it up around Rs. 18 crores to Rs. 20 crores of net profit in FY'27?

items.statement: FY26 AUM target Rs 250 crore
items.quote: Around 250 crore in FY'26.

items.statement: FY26 branch count target 42 branches
items.quote: FY'26, we have 36 branches. 42 branches, can happen, not more than that.

items.statement: BC portfolio target Rs 30-40 crore by end FY26 and Rs 80 crore by FY27
items.value: 30-40 crore by FY26; 80 crore by FY27
items.quote: Presently we expect to have our VC portfolio by end of FY'26 around Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 40 crore and by '27 it may touch around Rs. 80 crores.

items.statement: Kaleidofin BC disbursement run-rate Rs 1 crore/month in Q3, Rs 2 crore/month from Q4
items.quote: Q3 we may touch an average of Rs. 1 crore and Q4 we are expecting to touch on average of Rs. 2 crore per month.

items.statement: Kisan Dhan BC disbursement run-rate Rs 50 lakh/month in Q3, Rs 1-1.5 crore/month from Q4
items.quote: We expect to do a business of say around 50 lakhs per month in Q3 and then 1 to 1.5 crores per month disbursement from Q4.

items.statement: GNPA 1.29% as of September 2025; target to maintain GNPA 1-1.5% and NNPA within 1%
items.quote: As far as our gross NPA is concerned, it is roughly 1.29% as of September 2025.

items.statement: GNPA target 1-1.5% range; NNPA within 1% for next 12 months
items.quote: Historically my gross NPA is within 1 % to 1.5%, historically and we will maintain within this range. And net NPA will be maintaining within 1%.

items.statement: Net profit margin 20.75% in Q2 FY26, up 456 bps YoY; 19.66% in H1 FY26, up 360 bps YoY
items.quote: The net profit margin was 20.75% which is 456 basis point higher year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by Rs 22-23 crore IPO proceeds with zero cost of funds
items.quote: The Rs. 22 crores-Rs. 23 crores which came via IPO, I don't need to give interest. So my profit increased.

items.statement: Expect margins to be maintained at current levels; cost of funds trending down
items.quote: We hope to maintain it, sir. This quarter, we have the advantage of IPO proceeds being utilized against which there was no cost of fund. But still, we hope to maintain the margins as projected.

items.statement: Average yield 21.23%; cost of borrowing ~13% from banks, 14-15% from investors
items.quote: Our basically average term loan is 21.23%. That is the yield, cost of borrowing is roughly 13%.

items.statement: Expect cost of funds to decline by 0.5-1% as balance sheet improves and bond market tapped
items.quote: I can see by cost of going by 1.5 % to 1%. I need to also pay arrangement fees along with coupon rate. But it will be between 14 to 15%.

items.statement: Issued Rs 10 crore listed rated debentures in September; plan Rs 25-30 crore more NCDs in H2
items.quote: In September we already issued listed and rated debentures of Rs. 10 crore and we will be tapping more and more the bond markets, listed bond markets.

items.statement: Raised Rs 65 crore in H1 including Rs 10 crore from ICICI Bank and Bandhan Bank; IPO proceeds Rs 22-23 crore deployed
items.quote: We have been able to do better business in Q2 as because we had received good amount of money from the IPO and IPO possibly was put into the system.

items.statement: Maintain liquidity buffer equal to 2 months of repayment obligations as permanent protocol
items.quote: We always maintain equal to 2 months of repayment obligations, cash in hand and that is permanent protocol of the Company.

items.statement: Declared first interim dividend of 5% for FY26; paid dividends regularly for last 6 years
items.quote: This is the first time the board has declared interim divid end of 5% for the financial year 2025 -26

items.statement: No new product categories planned; no gold loan plans
items.quote: Not at the moment, really.

items.statement: Focus on safai karamcharis (municipal Grade IV staff) as unique niche; repeat customers contribute 10-15% of growth
items.quote: Repeat customer is confused, 10%-15% growth comes from repeat customer.

items.statement: No significant competition from larger NBFCs or digital lenders in core municipal employee segment
items.quote: We don't have any big problem from the NBFC competition.

items.statement: Collection efficiency improved in last two quarters after RBI risk-weight impact subsided
items.quote: Definitely for last two quarters, collection efficiency is better. What we see, RBI restriction on extra weightage on unsecured loan or microfinance industry and all that had some impact on the cash flow into the system but now that has improved.

items.statement: Built strong NPA management team; 250+ employees across 36 branches in 7 states
items.quote: We have developed a better management team for collecting NPA. We employ a few persons to look after bed debts or NPA as I would say. And we have built a very strong team for NPA management.

items.statement: Operating in semi-urban markets; physical sourcing model (touch banking); digital onboarding fully implemented
items.quote: We are operating entire 3-4-5 cities where the digital knowledge of the borrower is not there. They are not equipped and confident enough as of now at this stage to tap and go for digital loan. So we are sourcing our loan through physical touch with the borrower.

items.statement: Collection mix: municipal loans via RTGS, secured MSME 100% E-NACH, unsecured MSME 20-30% cash collection
items.quote: My personal loan to safaikaramchari happens via RTGS from the municipality. And in secured loan it is 100% E-NACH. So there is 20% to 30% rejection. So we have to follow up personally. So balance around 20% to 25% is cash collection.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR320 crores and PAT of INR22-24 crores
items.quote: So, this financial year, we'll be ending up in a positive note to expected turnover of around INR320 crores. And that would also help us to increase our PAT margin to the range of INR22 crores to INR24 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target of INR380-390 crores, internal target INR400 crores
items.quote: We are looking somewhere around INR380 crores, INR390 crores of revenue minimum in the next financial year. So that could be treated as a peak for this existing capacity. I mean, with the addition that we are doing this year.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance of 14-15%
items.quote: Ma'am, we are looking somewhere around 14% to 15%.

items.statement: FY26 PAT margin guidance of 9.7-10%
items.quote: I am looking somewhere around -- this financial year, we are looking somewhere around 10%, 9.7% to 10%.

items.statement: FY27-28 PAT margin target of 11-12%
items.quote: Sir, in FY '27-'28, we are definitely looking at a PAT margin of say about 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Current confirmed order book of INR101.89 crores
items.quote: Our current confirmed order book stands at INR101.89 crores, supported by long-standing repeat clients and new strategic relationships.

items.statement: USA orders up 25%, Japan orders up >55%, first orders from Latin America
items.quote: The orders from USA have currently jumped up by 25%. Orders from Japan are more than 55% up, and we have recently got first-time orders from Latin American countries.

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 45M units (FY25) to 65.5M (FY26) to 105M (FY28)
items.quote: With these additions, our in-house capacity is projected to scale from 45 million units in financial year '25, to 65.5 million units in financial year '26, and further to 105 million units in financial year '28.

items.statement: Factory 4 (Badu, WB): 40,000 sq ft, +12M units annually, operational Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are coming up with our Factory 4, situated at Badu, Madhyamgram, West Bengal, with a new 40,000 square feet of area, and a 20,000 square feet of corporate office, adding 12 million units annually, which will become operational in the last quarter of this financial year, '25 '26.

items.statement: Factory 5 (Bagodara, Ahmedabad): 20,000 m/day weaving, 40M units bags, trial production Jan 2027
items.quote: Factory 5, which will be coming up in Bagodara, Ahmedabad, the ground-breaking ceremony has been done, and construction will begin in December, with in-house weaving capacity of about 20,000 meters a day, and 40 million units of capacity of bag, with the trial production commencing in January 27.

items.statement: Calcutta workshop: 25,000 sq ft, +8M units, operational Dec 2025
items.quote: We are also taking up a new workshop in Calcutta, with about 25,000 square feet, which will be adding 8 million units, and will be operational from December 25.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization >95%
items.quote: Ma'am, it is more than 95%.

items.statement: Ahmedabad Factory 5 capex estimated at INR65-70 crores
items.quote: Ma'am that the Ahmedabad factory 5 that we are talking about, the estimated capex is roughly about INR65 crores to INR70 crores.

items.statement: Calcutta plant capex ~INR10 crores (rented facility)
items.quote: Ma'am, the capex in the Calcutta plant would not be of a greater extent because that area we are taking on rent. So, that we expect something around maximum to the tune of INR10 crores.

items.statement: Capex funded via internal accruals and IPO proceeds, no debt planned
items.quote: Ma'am, we do not plan to take any debt as of now and we will be utilizing our internal accruals as well as the IPO proceeds for the same.

items.statement: Company effectively debt-free; only export credit limits from banks
items.quote: We remain effectively debt-free, and with improved working capital management, our operating cash flow has also increased to INR56.17 lakh, compared to a negative position in the previous period.

items.statement: Working capital cycle increased to ~60 days due to shipping delays
items.quote: Ma'am, the working capital has grown up about 60 days because of the shipping delays. Now the shipping time is increased. So that has increased our working capital.

items.statement: Order conversion period 3-3.5 months
items.quote: Yeah. So we looking at around three, three and a half months. The order book stands for about three, three and a half months.

items.statement: FX hedging policy covers 40-45% of exposure
items.quote: Sir, we have a certain hedging policy where we hedge our foreign exchange to protect us. Now, that is not a 100% hedge, but it is to the tune of 40-45%.

items.statement: Raw material 54% of revenue; 96-97% sourced domestically; cotton 80%, jute 20% of RM
items.quote: Raw material formed around 54% of our revenue, and we continue to optimize procurement through vendor diversification, strategic stocking, and backward integration by the upcoming weaving capacity in Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Long-term agreements with 10-15 key suppliers for 6-9 month price locks
items.quote: Sir, that we have 80% of our purchase is from around only 10 or 15 key suppliers. So, and our contracts with them are for long-term. So we are able to manage that volatility with our long-term agreements with them.

items.statement: No customer or country concentration risk; US 7.5%, Japan ~4% of FY25 revenue
items.quote: Ma'am, in the last financial year, the total revenue was just 7.5%. We are very well diversified into multi-countries and multi-clients. We do not depend on certain country and a certain client.

items.statement: Polyester bags, hand towels, backpacks, caps as new high-potential segments
items.quote: Our portfolio today spans; cotton bags, organic, recycled, Fairtrade bags, jute bags, aprons, and the new high-potential segments, such as polyester bags, backpacks, hand towels, and caps.

items.statement: Key risks: currency volatility and quality control (<0.5% annual claims)
items.quote: Sir, there is a -- we are looking at the risk of currency could be a risk. And also sometimes quality could be a risk, which we are very much focused on.

items.statement: Market share ~4.5% (latest available); claims to be India's largest cotton bag manufacturer
items.quote: Ma'am, I would not be having the updated figure, but yes, that was the latest we have, 4.5%. And supposedly, we are India's largest for at least the cotton-bag segment.

items.statement: Management targets 30-40% year-on-year revenue growth going forward
items.quote: I would like to say that we will grow anywhere between 30% to 40% year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 10.6% in H1 FY26, up 72.3% year-on-year
items.quote: EBITDA margin has been, it's up by 72.3%.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to improve by 5-10% on current base due to women/kids wear and quick commerce scale
items.quote: I believe, it should increase by at least 5% to 10% again.

items.statement: Quick commerce expected to contribute 5-10% of total revenue going forward
items.quote: I believe going forward, quick commerce should be at least, between 5% to 10% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Warehouse holding capacity increased from 6 lakh to 2 million units across 9 states
items.quote: we have increased our warehouse capacity from 6 lakh pieces holding capacities it has got to 2 million units holding capacity.

items.statement: Launched women's and kids' wear under FTX brand generating Rs 5.5 crore; added 7 new categories in quick commerce
items.quote: We have also added women wear and kids wear categories under our brand name FTX through which we have generated ₹5.5 crores business till date.

items.statement: Winter wear selling well on quick commerce with 10-minute delivery; kurtas driving strong traction in Hyderabad, UP, South India
items.quote: we are seeing very good traction in our winter wear products, including jackets, sweatshirt, sweatpants, through Zepto and we are delivering it within 10 minutes.

items.statement: Inventory up 30-40 days due to 50% revenue growth, seasonal winter stocking, and Kolkata production shutdown during Durga Puja
items.quote: the inventory has gone up hardly by 30 to 40 days, and that is because of several reasons. Number one, we are growing by almost 50% top line.

items.statement: Payables days reduced to 13 days from 47 days due to strategic early payment to suppliers during Durga Puja and Punjab raw material crisis
items.quote: we went all in, in the month of August and September and bought a lot of winter wear from there. So today's situation that only 50% to 60% supply is happening through Punjab this time.

items.statement: Marketplace commissions average 30-33% of sales value, ranging from 22% to 40% across platforms
items.quote: It is around 30% to 33%.

items.statement: Added ~1 million customers in H1 FY26; delivered to >1 million customers via B2C platforms
items.quote: We have, added around a million customers in last six months. We have delivered to more than a million customers through B2C platforms.

items.statement: Return rates among lowest in industry: men's top wear <7% vs industry 18-19%, bottom wear 14-15% vs industry 30%, average <12%
items.quote: For the top wear in men's wear, our return is below 7%, which is I think the industry standard is around 18% - 19%. And bottom wear, our return is around 14% to 15%. The industry standard is around 30%. So our average return is still below 12%.

items.statement: Brand revenue grew 47% YoY from Rs 48.68 cr to Rs 71.79 cr; overall revenue up 50.6% YoY
items.quote: our brand revenue has rose from ₹48.68 crores to ₹71.79 crores, year-on-year. Also, our overall revenue has gone up by 50% comparing last H1 to this H1.

items.statement: No plans for D2C with FTX brand due to high CAC at Rs 400 ASP; will only consider D2C for higher price point segments
items.quote: So we have taken this, I believe smarter route by selling through online where we pay commission only when the product is sold. We are not paying anything before that.

items.statement: Promoters subscribed 70-80% of warrant issue to increase ownership, signaling conviction in growth
items.quote: This warrant issued is 70% - 80% subscribed by me and my brother. So this is one. So we have increased our holding there.

items.statement: Algorithm-driven marketplace visibility depends on CTR, conversion, returns, reviews, availability, delivery speed, and brand tenure
items.quote: So the algo works like the first thing is, they check every new listing, which is live on any marketplace, get some minimum count of view.

items.statement: Secured winter fabric inventory early from Punjab ahead of 50-60% supply disruption due to natural calamity
items.quote: today's situation that only 50% to 60% supply is happening through Punjab this time. And there is a huge crisis of the raw material.

items.quote: INR 950 crores Ritwik Sheth: From the ongoing projects? Sajal Gupta: From the ongoing projects like the soft cost will go and INR 950 crores. These will be the 2 things that will go out

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve gradually in Q4 FY26 as SOC setup costs taper and services-led revenues scale up
items.quote: Margin should gradually improve in the Q4 as set-up costs taper and services-led revenues scale up.

items.quote: For tools and other equipment that we have built over a period of time, it is approximately Rs. 2.5 crores, which we have used for our SOC setup and now we are all geared up to start monetizing this thing.

items.quote: Our new soft center is at Turbhe, Navi Mumbai and it has been already now geared up for the operational purpose. We are all ready. Now, we are just waiting for few of the challenges that we are facing for second and third shift perspective.

items.quote: We remain fully on track to begin commercializing the SOC and generating revenues from latter half of Q3, but early stages of Q4, you can see that we will start generating the revenue.

items.statement: Significant EBITDA contribution from SOC and new services expected from Q4 FY26 or early Q1 FY27
items.quote: But yes, we are expecting from Q4 or early Q1 of the next year, it should start seeing in the P&L significantly.

items.statement: Won Rs 30.81 crore multi-year order from New India Assurance for network, backup and storage solutions
items.quote: Additionally, a leading insurance company, New India Assurance, placed a multi-year order worth Rs. 30.81 crores with us for network, backup and storage solutions across its data centers.

items.statement: Won Rs 30 crore technology refresher order from a Big Four consulting firm
items.quote: One of the Big Four consulting firms selected Orient Technologies for the technology refresher program with an order of around Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Completed phase one of VAT automation solution for Maharashtra Government valued at Rs 18.69 crores over five years
items.quote: In application development, we successfully completed phase one of the VAT automation solution for the VAT-CST-PT department of the Government of Maharashtra, valued at Rs.18.69 crores over a period of five years.

items.statement: Won Rs 3.75 crore order from global pharmaceutical company for high-availability infrastructure via Dell Azure Stack
items.quote: A large global pharmaceutical company entrusted Orient Technologies to implement its high-availability technology infrastructure through the Dell's Azure Stack, valued at Rs. 3.75 crores.

items.statement: Partnered with prominent foreign bank for regulatory reporting module on cloud in a Rs 25 crore multi-year deal
items.quote: the 25 crores cloud services deal with the foreign bank involves end-to-end cloud modernization, migration, and managed operations over a multi-year period

items.statement: Business 100% domestic in India; foreign bank deal serves as reference for future MNC cross-border opportunities
items.quote: Currently, we do not go internationally. Our majority of business is happening domestically in India. But yes, this will give an opportunity as a reference customer for many more MNC customers.

items.statement: Revenue grew 22.25% YoY to Rs 272.80 crores in Q2 FY26; H1 FY26 revenue grew 30.48% YoY to Rs 485.37 crores
items.quote: during Q2 of FY'26, our company delivered a strong performance with revenue from operations at Rs. 272.80 crores from last year's revenue of Rs. 223.14 crores, which is up by around 22.25% year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA at Rs 21.96 crores in Q2 FY26; H1 FY26 EBITDA at Rs 39.29 crores

items.statement: Segmental revenue mix Q2 FY26: Mid-market & others 47.40%, Government/PSU 19.65%, BFSI 14.90%, Telecom 13.11%, ITES 4.94%
items.quote: In terms of segmental revenue, mix of Q2 of FY'26, telecommunication contributed to 13.11%, BFSI contributed 14.90% and Government / PSU contributed 19.65%, ITES contributed 4.94% and Mid-market and others contributed to 47.40%.

items.statement: AI adoption still in early POC stage; customers not ready for production deployment due to budget and unclear ROI
items.quote: Most of the customers are not ready for AI only because AI needs a huge budget, number one, and there is no definite ROI on that. So, everybody is flirting with AI, okay? They are trying to do a lot of POCs on AI, but it is not getting into the actual production environment.

items.statement: Does not provide forward-looking revenue or EBITDA numbers as company policy; expects good EBITDA improvement in near future
items.quote: Generally, we do not, you know, give any forward-looking numbers. That's a strategy that Orient has adopted from day one. Okay. But to answer your question, yes, we are looking forward for good EBITDA improvement in the near future.

items.statement: Provides complete IT infrastructure and management for data centers; does not build data centers but supports hyperscale data center customers
items.quote: We don't build data centers, but we provide the complete IT infrastructure for the data centers. Plus, we manage the data centers. That means we give the complete support to the data centers.

items.statement: No major capex plans decided for FY27 as of now
items.quote: As of now, there are no major capex plans that we have decided for FY27. If anything changes, we will communicate that appropriately.

items.statement: Plan to have own service centres in all Tier I cities within next two years
items.quote: Our plan is to have our own service centres in all Tier I cities of India within the next two years. That is a realistic timeline we are working with.

items.quote: It is close to half of our sales at present that comes from our own brands.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to move back towards mid-teens over time as investments generate returns
items.quote: We believe that over time, EBITDA margins should move back towards the mid-teens as these investments start generating returns.

items.statement: Short-term inventory days expected to stabilise around 120-150 days; long-term target below 100 days

items.quote: That said, we believe we are already capable of handling 3x the current order volume from a tech standpoint. On warehousing, we have made significant fixed-cost investments in H1. These costs will not grow linearly with orders.

items.statement: Repeat order behaviour remains strong; delivery time reducing; product depth and availability improving; organisational capability stronger than one year ago
items.quote: Our repeat order behaviour remains strong. Our delivery time continues to reduce. Our product depth and availability are improving. Our organisational capability is much stronger than it was one year ago.

items.quote: Currently, with all humility, I'm a small company. First, we are benchmarking against ourselves, whether we have done better than the last quarter, whether we will do better in the next year. So first, we are benchmarking against ourselves.

items.statement: Real estate value appreciation at Hosur mine (3x investment); potential monetization if land values reach INR5 crores/acre
items.quote: But that probably will not be captured on a balance sheet at the moment because our core activity is in the production of construction aggregate in the M-sand. So that value may be typically not reflect on the balance sheet, but however, on an realistic value, if you ask me, we have already multiplied our investment at least by three times of it.

items.statement: EBITDA margins for legacy business expected to improve to 7-9% range in December and March quarters
items.quote: Backed by firm sale prices and healthy order inflows, we anticipate an improvement in EBITDA margins to the 7–9% range during the December and March quarters in our legacy business.

items.statement: No consolidated margin or top-line guidance for FY26; will update after Q3 results
items.quote: Yes. So basically, margins and -- we are not giving any margin and top line guidance this time. Better -- we would be better in providing the same after the Q3 numbers.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR1,500 crores not intact; will be updated after Q3
items.quote: So I just answered this question in the last question on this. So it is not very much clear the top line numbers for the Q3. Basically it depends on the deliveries for B2B for this month.

items.statement: Legacy business back on track with strong order flows and rising demand for rPSF and Yarn segments
items.quote: Our legacy business, which had seen a very dismal performance over the last couple of quarters, is now almost back on track with strong order flows and rising demand for both rPSF as well as Yarn segments.

items.statement: B2B segment sales and deliveries expected to remain below expectations in December quarter due to pending MOEF notification and seasonal beverage slowdown
items.quote: In the B2B segment, sales and deliveries are expected to remain below expectations in the December quarter as well, pending release of the final MOEF notification. Additionally, bottling plants are also operating at reduced capacities right now, due to the typical seasonal slowdown in beverage demand during the last quarter of the calendar year.

items.statement: Recovery in B2B demand and deliveries anticipated from January 2026 as regulatory uncertainty resolves
items.quote: However, based on our recent industry interactions and government interactions, we anticipate a recovery in demand and deliveries beginning January 2026, as the uncertainty surrounding the draft notification is confined to the current year only.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margins compressed to 6.1% and net profits turned slightly negative
items.quote: The second quarter of FY26 continued to be a challenging period for us. Despite our best efforts and strong sales performance, the quarter concluded overall on an adverse note, with EBITDA margins compressed to 6.1% and net profits turning slightly negative.

items.statement: Inventory loss of INR10-11 crores incurred in Q2 due to raw material price drop from INR55 to INR43-44 per kg
items.quote: So sir, it is roughly to the tune of INR10 crores to INR11 crores.

items.statement: Legacy business long-term gross margin range normally 62-66%
items.quote: So it is -- normally, it is in the range of 62% to 65%, 66%.

items.statement: Legacy business EBITDA margins expected to return to 7-9% from December quarter, potentially exceeding 10% by March quarter
items.quote: Presently, we are looking for 7% to 9%, and we are trying to get it improve further. May be over next quarter and March quarter, we will be more than 10%.

items.statement: Customer commitments for recycled PET deliveries received starting January 2026
items.quote: In response, we have begun receiving customer commitments for recycled PET deliveries starting January 2026, enabling us to optimize capacity utilization from the last quarter onwards.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at Warangal adding 22,500 MTPA rPET capacity at INR130 crores, operational by end-March 2026
items.quote: So for this brownfield expansion is about 22,500 tons per annum. And we spent about INR130 crores for this expansion.

items.statement: Greenfield expansion capex of INR500 crores, expected operational by end of next financial year (FY27)
items.quote: So expected capex is about INR500 crores for that project.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at Warangal on track to be operational by end-March 2026, adding 22,500 MTPA rPET capacity

items.statement: Industry FSSAI-approved rPET capacity increased from 70,000 tons to 210,000 tons in last 6 months
items.quote: So 6 months ago, it was 70,000 tons. And right now, it is about 210,000 tons available FSSAI approved capacity.

items.statement: rPET capacity utilization expected to reach 90%+ from March quarter onwards
items.quote: But from March onwards, we are expecting we would reach to 90% plus capacity utilization in our rPET business.

items.quote: On a console basis, the average capacity utilization was about 80%...

items.statement: Average selling prices dropped about 4% across businesses in Q2
items.quote: The average selling prices have also dropped by about 4% across the businesses contributing further to lower margins.

items.statement: Raw material prices surged from INR43-45/kg to INR55-56/kg then retreated sharply to INR43-44/kg between March and June 2025
items.quote: The Prices surged from ₹43-45 per kg to around ₹55-56, before retreating very sharply back to ₹43-44 levels between March and June 2025.

items.statement: No hedging mechanism available for plastic scrap raw material
items.quote: So basically, it is not -- Bhavya, it is not a very organized collection system or organized suppliers are there. So there is no hedging mechanism available like it was -- it is a -- I think it is in metal scrap or I think there is some hedging mechanism, it's not there in plastic scrap.

items.statement: Current product mix: 65% PSF, 20% chips, rest yarn; expected to shift to 65% chips, 35% rest after expansions
items.quote: So currently, we are -- our product mix is about 65% is from the PSF side, 20% from the chips side and rest is from the yarn side. But going forward, after this greenfield expansion and brownfield expansion, the product mix will change to 65% from the chips and 35% from the rest of the businesses.

items.statement: Legacy business client base scattered with no single customer >5%; B2B segment concentrated with Coke and Pepsi as primary customers
items.quote: So in our legacy business, the client base is very, very scattered and we are not getting more than 5% from a single customer. But in the case of B2B, yes, of course, client concentration is more because we are presently supplying to the big bottlers Coke and Pepsi only.

items.statement: MOEF draft notification in June 2025 proposed carryover of FY26 recycled content shortfall over 3 years; final notification pending
items.quote: The MOEF issued a draft notification on 3rd of June in 2025 which proposed a relaxation for the usage of recycled materials. According to the draft, any shortfall in meeting the requirements of mandatory recycled plastic usage during the year could be offset over the following three years.

items.statement: Mandatory recycled content usage increases to 40% in FY27 from 30% in FY26; carryover only for FY26 shortfall
items.quote: And from next year onwards, the mandatory use will increase to 40% from 30%. So the good demand is visible, and we are also getting the commitment from the buyers from January onwards lately.

items.statement: Exports contributed around 11% of revenue in Q2 FY26
items.quote: For this quarter, we made around 11% of our exports.

items.statement: High-cost inventory fully consumed by end of Q2; inventory value and market price at par as of 30th September
items.quote: No, no, we have consumed the entire inventory, which was high cost. Now as on the 30th September, the value of our inventory as well as the market price is almost at par.

items.statement: Regulatory delay of 4-5 months in finalizing MOEF notification was unexpected and caused demand shock in B2B segment
items.quote: And so it was expected that in August, anyways, the regulation should have been done finally, but it was just getting delayed. So even we did not expect that this kind of huge delay of about 4 to 5 months would happen from the government side and -- which led to even like a lot of miss or I would say, a shock for us also on the B2B side.

items.quote: In air coolers segment, if you talk of air coolers, we wil l see margin improvement of close to 5%-7%. And for television cabinets, it will be close to 5%.

items.quote: Optimal utilization, we can go up to Rs. 1,000-Rs. 1,200 crores, approximately in that range.

items.quote: We expect the approval over the next 30, 40 days. And once we are in approved, AMISP, then it also allows us to create another revenue stream to the tune of ₹300 crores to ₹400 crores.

items.statement: Exploring export opportunities for gas meters and other products; in discussions with organisations
items.quote: exports and domestic sales are concerned, we are looking at opportunities for exports also. We're also in talking terms with a few organi sations

items.statement: Railway underslung charger (4.5 kW) approved; orders from Railways or their contractors via tender process

items.quote: We have not repaid our borrowings. We have used that money to buy material from the vendors.

items.quote: we expect that cumulatively we will process around 38,000 to 40,000 metric tons of waste tire, compared to last year's 24,000 metric tons. So, we expect that revenue could be around ₹130 to ₹140 crores.

items.statement: H2 FY26 revenue target of ~₹80 crore

items.statement: Target to return to 20% operating margin for full year

items.statement: Radhe Renewables business expected to have higher margins than Hi-Green due to technology monopoly

items.statement: TPO demand improving post-monsoon; winter season and road construction ramp-up supporting demand

items.statement: TPO prices fell from ₹44-45 to ₹34, now settled at ₹36-38; ~₹10/kg decline YoY

items.statement: Rajasthan plant 8,000/8,300 MT utilization (96%); Maharashtra plant 9,000 MT utilization; combined 75-76% utilization
items.quote: In the last half year, we almost achieved 8,000 metric tons of processing in our Rajasthan plant. It has a capacity of 8,300 metric tons. And 9,000 metric tons in the Dhule plant. So, we achieved better utilization at our new plant.

items.quote: 75% we achieved for pyrolysis, 30% for rCB, and 0% for syngas. Syngas will be utilized once we install the DG set next month. And for rCB, we are makin g maximum efforts to promote our rCB

items.statement: Maharashtra plant onboarded 6-7 new rCB customers in last 6 months; total rCB customer base 10-12
items.quote: For rCB, I think in our system plant also, we hardly had 10 to 12 customers. And for the Maharashtra plant also, we have already started supplying to 6—6 to 7 customers already. So, the demand will increase, and side by side, we are adding new customers also.

items.statement: rCB export discussions ongoing with Sri Lanka, Thailand, Malaysia, Middle East; ISCC EU certification obtained
items.quote: There is good demand, and we are in talks with a few customers in nearby countries like Sri Lanka, Thailand, Malaysia, and even the Middle East. So hopefully, we will crack that.

items.statement: Applied for waste tyre import license from MOEF; CPCB/State Pollution Board committee formed for site visit
items.quote: one meeting was already conducted, and in that meeting, they… they ordered for a physical visit of our premises by people from CPCB, from MOEF, from State Pollution Board. So that committee is already formed, and they are supposed to come and visit, and then submit report to MOEF here

items.statement: Syngas bottling approval sought for MP plant; first-of-kind globally, PESO queries ongoing
items.quote: For our third plant in Madhya Pradesh, we are trying to get this approval, but there are a lot of queries because this would be the first time in the world that syngas is converted into a bottled fuel. items.statement: EPR credits not material; price ₹1-1.25 vs earlier ₹7-8 expectations; credits passed to suppliers/customers

items.statement: Future plant funding via internal accruals, bank support, state incentives; external capital only for larger opportunities
items.quote: After ramping up our third plant, we will have enough internal accruals, and our bankers are there to support us. items.statement: No Indian competitor at current scale; global players targeting 100k+ MT but in early stages

items.statement: IzmoMicro next year gross margin 30-40% and EBITDA margin at least 25%
