items.statement: IzmoMicro to reach 50-50 revenue contribution with legacy business in 3 years
items.quote: In the next 3 years, we expect 50-50 contribution of Izmo Micro and the rest of the business.

items.statement: Legacy automotive business normalized growth 10-15% once tariff issues resolve
items.quote: I would expect a 10% to 15% steady growth at least for next year and maybe more in the following year once things get stabilized.

items.statement: Current izmoMicro packaging capacity supports INR 80-100 crore revenue; post-expansion INR 1,000 crore
items.quote: See with the current capacity, I can do INR100 crores, maybe INR80 crores to INR100 crores. After the expansion, I can do INR1,000 crores turnover.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 23.4% excluding other income
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding other income for the 6 months increased 23.4% Y-o-Y to INR 18.79 crores and corresponding EBITDA margin is 23.4%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 22.5% excluding other income
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding other income for the quarter grew 42.4% Y-o-Y to INR13.51 crores, while corresponding EBITDA margin is 22.5%.

items.statement: Strong international and domestic demand for silicon photonics packaging; clients ramping up volumes
items.quote: The demand frankly, has surprised us. We had never expected such a hard -- but actually, we realized all this work was being done outside, which is now moving here.

items.statement: FrogData added 78 clients last quarter and launched two new products
items.quote: FrogData business is growing steadily. We added 78 clients last quarter. We also added two more products, like I said earlier.

items.statement: AI Factory leveraging India cost advantage for enterprise AI solutions
items.quote: AI Factory delivers enterprise-grade AI solutions at a fraction of Western pricing, a huge competitive moat.

items.statement: FrogData launched FixedOps Mojo and FixedOps Velocity targeting service marketing
items.quote: This quarter, we launched two new offerings, FixedOps Mojo and FixedOps Velocity, targeting the untapped service marketing opportunity.

items.statement: Engaging with 3 US OEMs; already have 2 US OEM clients
items.quote: We are working with three OEMs right now. We are talking to three OEMs. We already have two OEMs in US who are already our client.

items.statement: IzmoAuto acquired 22 new clients in Europe this quarter; completing major OEM rollout for 900 dealer sites
items.quote: This quarter alone, we acquired 22 new clients in Europe, proof of our multilingual platform, which resonates global ly. We are completing a major OEM contract for rollout of our digital marketing web platform for 900 dealer sites in Europe

items.statement: DSIR recognition driving inquiries from defence PSUs for indigenization projects
items.quote: We are getting a lot of inquiries coming in from most of the DPSUs after we received this that can we work on some projects for them?

items.statement: Government-driven fab initiative under Indian Semiconductor Mission with 50% central subsidy and state incentives
items.quote: the fab initiative has actually been driven by the government. They have told us that they would like us to be the leader in silicon photonics and also move towards the fab. So it's something which is being driven by the IS M Indian Semiconductor Mission

items.statement: Silicon photonics packaging market $2-3B today, projected $10B+ by 2030 at 25-30% CAGR
items.quote: Silicon photonics packaging is a $2 billion to $3 billion market today, projected to hit $10 billion plus by 2030, 25% to 30% CAGR, driven by explosive AI and data center demand.

items.statement: US/Europe auto market sluggish due to tariff confusion; dealers and OEMs cautious on spending
items.quote: The market in the U.S. and Europe has been subdued overall because with so much of confusion created by tariffs and all that mess, there has been a slow uptake of cars, slow -- I mean, less stocking of vehicles.

items.statement: Order book over ₹3,300 crore, 99% smart meters, AMISP-driven
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, we carried an order book of over ₹3, 300 crore, of which roughly 99% is smart meters.

items.statement: Expect Q3 better than Q2, Q4 much stronger; full-year revenue around ₹1,900-2,000 crore
items.quote: Whether it's ₹1, 900 crore or ₹2, 000 crore, we should be looking at somewhere in that zip code.

items.statement: Smart meter uptake improved over 12% sequentially in Q2; further step-up expected Nov-Mar FY26
items.quote: Smart meter uptake improved by over 12% sequentially in Q2. Going forward, we expect a further step-up in deliveries from November to March FY26 as on-ground inspections accelerate and AMISP roll-outs gather pace.

items.statement: Metering segment EBIT margins improved to ~17.5% in Q2 despite softer revenues
items.quote: Even in a quarter of softer metering revenues, segment EBIT margins improved to around 17.5%, thanks to pricing discipline, procurement efficiency and a richer mix of smart meters.

items.statement: C&I segment EBIT margins around 11%; expect similar margins until volumes scale significantly
items.quote: Right now, as I just said, we are seeing good movement, we are probably around 11% on EBIT basis. As volumes go up, maybe by FY27 or FY28, if the same momentum continues and we are able to make that happen, then we can work towards better margins.

items.statement: Most metering capex done; FY27 onwards mainly maintenance capex
items.quote: Right now, if you look at the medium-term capacities that we are expecting, I would say that most of the capex on the metering front is more or less done.

items.statement: C&I revenue mix: ~40% switchgear, ~40% wires & cables, ~20% lighting
items.quote: Roughly 40% is switchgear, 40% is cables, and about 20% is lighting. Fans are still small and can be clubbed within lighting for now.

items.statement: C&I segment targeting double-digit growth; aim to double C&I business in 3 years
items.quote: In three years' time, the ideal would be to double our C&I business. That is how we are looking at it. It's a strong vertical for us and a strong focus area.

items.statement: C&I revenue share expected to settle around 45% in H2 FY26
items.quote: Overall, metering could grow at a much faster pace because the uptake could be higher. But I think anywhere between 45–50% is where C&I should be.

items.statement: Debtor days ~125 including GST, improved 50-60 days vs March; inventory to reduce ₹50-60 crore in H2
items.quote: If you look at it including GST, it's about 125 days overall on debtor days, which is about 50–60 days better than March.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings up ~₹60 crore in H1 for capex; operating cash flows to reduce working capital borrowings
items.quote: There has been capex in the first six months and long-term borrowings have increased by about ₹60 crore. On working-capital borrowings, any additional realisations will go towards bringing short-term debt down.

items.statement: Strong manufacturing capacity; added automated machines for switchgear; wires & cables capacity expansion planned
items.quote: We have also added a lot of automated machines, especially on the switch side, over the last one–two years. That enhances quality, consistency and reduces human intervention, even in final testing.

items.statement: Supplying to almost all AMISPs; added 2 new AMISPs; order pipeline healthy with breakthroughs expected
items.quote: If you see my opening remarks, I did say that we are covering almost everybody now in the AMISP universe as a customer. Anybody who is there, big or small, we are somehow connected with them and we are supplying to them.

items.statement: Industry cumulative smart meter installations ~4.5 crore; run-rate 60-70 lakh/month
items.quote: The last figures in the public domain are about 4.5 crore smart meters already installed. So now at least some meaningful numbers are coming in, because we are already talking about double-digit implementation rates.

items.statement: Government extended 25-crore smart meter target to March 2028; ministry pushing AMISPs to speed implementation
items.quote: The government had earlier Transcribed by ElevEase 23 extended the deadline and this time I think there will be a much bigger push to adhere to it

items.statement: Execution challenges: skilled labour shortage for installations causing delays; some AMISP schedule postponements of 30-45 days
items.quote: My understanding is that, at times, meters and data are available but the requisite skilled manpower for installation is missing. That is my view; there could be other issues too.

items.statement: Copper prices volatile with 3 hikes in Sep-Oct; recently stabilising; global sourcing for electronic components
items.quote: Wires and cables still contribute a good chunk of the business and remain commoditised. There is a lot of play on copper prices. Only in the last two–three weeks we've seen some stabilisation; otherwise they've been volatile, with almost three price increases in September–October.

items.statement: Fans launched in exports (14 countries, international approvals); India launch from Dec, target 70-80% market coverage by June FY26
items.quote: In India, we have all the mandatory approvals, including for star rating. For the Indian market, we are looking at starting in December and then building up into June–July of FY26, which will be the first full season where we will participate.

items.statement: Havells settlement positive; no change to operating freedoms; consideration received by HPL group including promoter entities
items.quote: Overall, I think it's been very positive for both groups to set aside the dispute and move forward. I would say it has been positive for both sides.

items.statement: C&I growth above reported industry growth (EMA); market share still low with headroom
items.quote: Our growth in most segments is above reported industry growth (EMA figures etc.). If H2 comes in strong, we will put longer-term strategies in place to make this sustainable.

items.statement: Global sourcing for ICs, active/passive components, polycarbonate; procurement efficiencies in metering
items.quote: We are doing global sourcing for many items, ICs, active and passive electronic components, polycarbonate, etc. Wherever we get the best pricing and quality, we source from there.

items.statement: Metering orders structured over 2.5-3 years; bulk of ₹3,300 crore order book scheduled for FY27-FY28
items.quote: On the order book of about ₹3, 300 crore, normally any order we get is to be supplied over about 2.5–3 years. Many of the orders currently in our order book are actually scheduled for the end of this year, FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 better than Q2; Q4 FY26 very strong based on confirmed AMISP delivery schedules
items.quote: Q3 is definitely going to be better than Q2, and Q4 should see much stronger growth. From our point of view, our teams are working to make sure that we are able to cover up the shortfall and then have growth as expected in the metering part.

items.statement: Consolidated margins healthy with room for efficiency-driven improvements; metering supply chain stable
items.quote: So, consolidated margins should remain healthy, with room for efficiency-driven improvements.

items.statement: No single state materially impacts order book; business aligned to AMISP customers not state-wise
items.quote: No particular state has such a large share that it can significantly impact our overall order book. Since ours is mainly a supply business to AMISPs, it is the AMISP that matters more than any single state.

items.statement: C&I strategy mainly traditional offline retail; builder projects strong; online focus for fans from Q4, then lighting/accessories
items.quote: Right now, our strategy is mainly traditional and offline. We address the market through the traditional retail channel. We have seen growth in terms of outlets or points of sale we are addressing, across all product lines.

items.statement: Brand investment ~2% of C&I sales in H1 FY26; stepping up in H2 FY26
items.quote: In the first half of FY26, we invested about 2% of C&I sales in advertising and promotion. We intend to step this up further in the second half of FY26, as we clearly see evidence that brand salience and distribution depth are translating into better-quality growth and pricing power over time.

items.statement: FY26 pump volume target 70,000-75,000 units
items.quote: Aditya Vora: Roughly 70,000 to 75,000 you are looking at? Gopal Rajaram Kabra: Yes.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to remain same or improve positively in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: And our EBITDA margin will remain same, or it is going to improve more positively. We are not looking towards any downside on the margins as well.

items.statement: Total order book INR 863.98 crores as of 30 Sep 2025 including 36,444 solar pumps worth INR 846.15 crores and 4 MW rooftop worth INR 17.83 crores
items.quote: Total order book, we are standing with 863.98 crores as on 30, September 2025.

items.statement: Magel Tyala-III empanelment tender for 1 lakh pumps submitted 13 Nov 2025; expect orders in Q3 FY26
items.quote: It is an empanelment for the 1 lakh pump.

items.statement: No slowdown expected in decentralized solar pump segment; demand remains aggressive
items.quote: But on the decentralized area where we are working, it is going more aggressive now. We are not looking towards any slowdown in the coming time.

items.statement: Current installation capacity 8,000-10,000 pumps per month; targeting 25-30% increase by April 2026
items.quote: We are targeting to increase around 25% to 30% capacity without stretch in comfort zone.

items.statement: 1 GW solar module line facility land acquired in Solapur, Maharashtra; work started; operational by Sep 2026 or earlier
items.quote: Yes. So, land acquisition is already done and the other things is in process. And it is a 1 gigawatt line definitely will be operational by the September 2026 or it will be before.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 20.20% vs 18.96% YoY; Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 20.57% vs 19.83% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 from business was INR 132.04 crores; it is basically 65.07% increase over INR 79.99 crores last year, with EBITDA margin expanding to 20.20% compared to 18.96% in H1 FY 2025.

items.statement: Input raw material prices decreased alongside selling prices; margins intact due to volume-based vendor negotiation
items.quote: See, definitely, I would not say pressure, price has been decreased, but input raw material price also has been decreased. So, price decreased and input raw material price also got decreased. So, ultimately, we GK Energy as the EPC player standing 100% with the intact margin what we have.

items.statement: Receivable days increased from 135 to 192 days (Sep 2024 to Sep 2025) due to monsoon delays, software integration, IPO work; expect normalization in Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have looked towards a little bit delay into the receivable from the previous time; it was 135 to 192 days in September 2024 to September 2025.

items.statement: Inventory turnover days increased from 31 to 55 days in H1 FY26 aligned with Q3 execution plan
items.quote: Our inventory turnover day increased from 31-days to 55-days in H1 FY26, and this increase was aligned with our execution plan as we are preparing to deliver and install significantly higher volume of the pump in Q3 2026.

items.statement: Debt primarily for working capital; interest rate 9% +/- 1%; net debt may increase in FY27 due to higher volumes
items.quote: See, debt is what we have, it is majorly for the working capital only. And the interest rates vary from the banker-to-banker, but in the range of 9% plus/minus 1% it will be there.

items.statement: Definitive agreement for procurement of 875 MW solar DCR cells for next financial year
items.quote: Furthermore, we are entering the definitive agreement procurement of 875 megawatt of solar DCR cell for the next financial year.

items.statement: Realization per pump varies by HP mix (3, 5, 7.5 HP); 3 HP volume increased lowering average realization
items.quote: It is about the mix of the 3, 5 and 7.5 HP. So, the little bit volume of 3 HP has been increased. So, 3 HP have the less price, 5 HP is more price and 7.5 HP is more price, right.

items.statement: Revenue share outside Maharashtra 10-15%; expanded presence in MP, UP, Rajasthan, Haryana
items.quote: It will be in the range of 10% to 15% outside Maharashtra.

items.statement: Asset-light pure-play EPC model protects margins vs integrated manufacturers; historic market share 15-18% per CRISIL
items.quote: See, number one thing, we are the asset light company. Number two, we are pure play EPC player.

items.statement: PM-KUSUM 2.0 opportunity expected not less than 3x previous scheme; industry belief based on government endorsement at ISA
items.quote: So, we are expecting a very good number and it is not less than 3x of the last PM-KUSUM what we have, this is what the industry believe I am having it.

items.statement: H1 FY26 installed 24,502 solar agri-pumps (+50.77% YoY); Q2 FY26 installed 13,675 pumps (+26.32% YoY)
items.quote: We have installed 24,502 solar Agri-pumps in H1 of '26. It is a 50.77% increase over the 16,251 pumps in the last year FY 2025 H1.

items.statement: H1 FY26 rooftop solar installed 1.24 MW; order book 4 MW (INR 17.83 crores)
items.quote: During the first half of FY2026, we have installed 1.24 megawatt of the rooftop capacity.

items.statement: Receivable delay risks from monsoon, software integration, IPO workload; AIIB USD 1.1bn funding to MSEDCL disbursement pending
items.quote: Basic delay got due to the extensive monsoon. We do the groundwork where the field-based inspection has to be carried out after installation. That has been got delayed because the monsoon was very aggressive this year.

items.statement: Capacity expansion driven by local manpower hiring and training; new resources output from Feb 2026, fully ready by Apr 2026
items.quote: So, next year, what is the target, we want to increase the number of the manpower. So, that training and the whole process has been started and we will be starting getting the output of the resources, manpower availability from the month of February onwards.

items.statement: FY26 revenue projected at Rs 260-275 crore
items.quote: FY ' 26, we are p rojecting somewhere between 260 and 275. Let us see how because generally, in the first half and the second half, we always see it has been 40 -60, 45-55 kind.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at minimum 20% over FY26
items.quote: Growth wise, FY '27, we are expecting to close maybe at 20% growth over and above FY '26, minimum. So it should be more also.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 15-20 crore running orders plus Rs 15 crore B2C orders
items.quote: See, currently our order book, we have running orders. Because we have a distribution , we sell through B2B as well as B2C. So as far as order goes we always have running orders. And apart from that when we talk about, say, B2C, so there we have orders, currently we are having orders of close to Rs. 15 odd crores.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 70-75%
items.quote: Our current capacity utilization is 70%-75%.

items.statement: Flux-Cored wire capacity 150 tons/month (1,800 MT/year) at 15-20% utilization
items.quote: It is 150 tons per month. Archit Agrawal: And utilization rate? Niraj Jindal: Utilization will improve because we have recently started. So with time, this is going to improve. Currently, it should be at 15%-20% odd

items.statement: Rs 1.5 crore from IPO proceeds for de-bottlenecking and automation at Unit 1
items.quote: During the period, we also outlined a growth plan focused on de -bottlenecking and automation initiatives at Unit 1, supported by Rs. 1.5 crores from the IPO proceeds.

items.statement: Plan to establish new manufacturing facility in South India (Nagpur or Chennai) in FY27
items.quote: So in FY '27, we are focusing on establishing a new manufacturing facility. The thought is in pipeline. We are planning right now. So we are planning to set up a new business in South India, somewhere near Nagpur or Chennai.

items.statement: EBITDA margins: electrodes 8-10%, general MIG wires ~10%, specialized MIG wires 18-22%, Flux-Cored wire expected 20-25%
items.quote: So the margins for electrodes range between 8 %-10%. And for MIG wires, we had special grades, which very few companies are doing in India. So the general MIG wires gives around 10% and the specialized gives around 18 %-22% EBITDA margin. And for Flux-Cored wire, we are expecting around 20%-25%.

items.statement: Manufacturing share improved to ~70% in H1 FY26 from 66-67% in FY25; trading dropped to ~30%
items.quote: If I talk about last year, the manufacturing contribution was approximately 66%-67% and trading was 32%-33% odd percent. However, in the first half of the year, the trading has dropped close to 30%. So the manufacturing business is improving vis-a-vis the trading.

items.statement: Strong demand expected for H2 FY26 and Q1 FY27 driven by government project completions
items.quote: So we expect a good demand for at least the next 2 quarters, which is the H2 of this year. As in general trends, we have seen that the government projects have to be completed by the year-end. So we expect a huge demand as compared to the coming 2 quarters. And it should continue for the 3rd quarter that is April to May.

items.statement: Raw material prices lower than last year; stable outlook for H2
items.quote: the raw material prices for this year, compared to last year, it has gone down. And the market has slowed down in the segment of raw materials. And for the H2 also, we do not see an increase of any prices. So we expect the same stable prices for the H2 itself.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 90-110 days; debtor days will increase with higher sales
items.quote: Our working capital cycle generally ranges between 90 to say 105-110 days. So that is what the trend had been and this is how it is going to continue. So somewhere between 3-4 months is the complete working capital cycle.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used for debt repayment reducing interest cost
items.quote: Financial benefit in terms of, we did not get it . So financial benefits, we are repaying our debt. So since we are repaying our debt, so obviously there will be a benefit in terms of the interest, what we were foregoing.

items.statement: Key risk: dependence on government infrastructure spending and policies
items.quote: See, challenges could be the government policies. Because everything depends on how the government policies are, the infrastructure development, because we are directly related to the development of infrastructure.

items.statement: Flux-Cored wire at full capacity to contribute Rs 25-30 crore revenue
items.quote: In 100% capacity, it should contribute between Rs. 25-Rs. 30 crores with the current capacity.

items.statement: Flux-Cored wire at 70-80% utilization expected to add Rs 30 crore revenue
items.quote: If we run around 70%-80%, we expect Rs. 30 crores extra revenue from that.

items.statement: Ongoing R&D for specialty products and complex electrodes
items.quote: See, this is a continuous or you can say, this is an ongoing R&D, which you keep doing it. So where you keep upgrading yourself as well as you try to make more complex electrodes.

items.statement: Trading division deals in wire rods (key raw material) with 2-3% margins; opportunistic trading to save costs
items.quote: So generally, we have MoUs from Steel Authority of India. So we trade wire rods. So it is not our main focus. It is just that sometimes we have a supply or we have an extra supply of wire rods. And if the market supports it, if there is any inquiry, we trade the wire rods to customers for a minimum margin. So the margin there is approximately 2 %-3%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue Rs 123.03 crore (+16.4% YoY); PAT Rs 6.48 crore (+5.9% YoY); EPS Rs 3.61
items.quote: Total revenue grew 16.4% to Rs. 123.0 3 crores. Profit before tax increased 11.7% to Rs. 8.46 crores. Profit after tax grew 5.9% to Rs. 6.48 crores and EPS stood at Rs. 3.61.

items.statement: Revenue target Rs 450-500 crore in 3-4 years
items.quote: See from here, in next 3 years' time, we expect our revenues to cross or touch close to say 450-500 in between.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 2,262 crore as of 30 September 2025
items.quote: Our order book remains robust at Rs. 2,262 crores as of 30 th September 2025, providing a strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters

items.statement: Order book mix: civil infra 39%, water infra 23%, mining 30%, civic utilities 8%
items.quote: Our business mix has diversified meaningfully, with civil infra contributing to 39%, water infra at 23%, mining at 30% and civic utilities at 8%.

items.statement: Secured Rs 708 crore mining O&M order from Kandoi Transport for Nigahi coal field
items.quote: We secured a landmark order of Rs. 708 crores from Kandoi Transport for the operation and maintenance of heavy mining equipments at the Niga hi coal field in the Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Won two sewerage treatment projects worth Rs 105.77 crore in Jammu and Kashmir
items.quote: These include two sew erage treatment projects worth Rs. 105.77 crores in Jammu and Kashmir, a Rs. 280 crore civil infra projects for the school in the Northeast and a Rs. 62.12 crore EPC order in railway communication infrastructure through our newly formed JV, Ganesh Netsoft JV Networks.

items.statement: Added Rs 203.83 crore sewerage treatment infrastructure package in Mumbai
items.quote: We also added notable new contracts including the Rs. 203.83 crore sew erage treatment infrastructure package at Mumbai, which further consolidates our position as a preferred partner for complex water projects.

items.statement: H2 FY26 expected to contribute ~60% of full-year revenue; margins to improve as projects mature
items.quote: H1 contributes to somewhere around 40% of the total revenue and H2 is 60%. So, nothing as such has happened. Moreover, after the public listing which happened in December, we have quite bumped up our team in the month of January and February. So, joining has also happened from February onwards and Company machinery strength has also grown up and we have also engaged big subcontractors also for the

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 12.3%, up 230 bps YoY; H1 EBITDA margin 11.9%, up 230 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 25.7 crores, a growth of 171% year -on-year. EBITDA margins improved by 230 basis points to 12.3%. Profit after tax for the quarter was Rs. 18.1 crores, up 156% year -on-year, with the PAT margin improving to 8.6%.

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by shift from subcontracting to direct JV execution, saving contractor margins
items.quote: No, margins, I think it should improve a little bit more because previously we were majorly a contractor. So, a good amount of margin was directly going to the contractor just for the name lending. And nowadays we have started forming JVs and we are doing the projects directly. So, the change in margin is majorly because of that reason, not for any other reason, because we are not, we are saving t

items.statement: Mining segment EBITDA margin similar to current levels; may improve with own fleet
items.quote: It will be similar only. EBITDA margins will be similar to what we have performed, what we have been achieving in the last quarter. And the margin profile should improve a little bit once we have our own fleet of machineries, which we have plans to do it in the future.

items.statement: Mining sector projected CAGR ~19% through 2030; early entry gives first-mover advantage
items.quote: Mining as a sector is also expected to grow at a rapid pace with projected CAGR of approximately 19% through 2030, driven by policy reforms and increased demands for critical minerals as well as coal. Our early entry gives us a first -mover advantage and a diversification opportunity in the space that will continue to expand meaningfully.

items.statement: Water infra focus on WTP, STP, pipelines under AMRUT/Namami Gange; not pursuing Jal Jeevan Mission
items.quote: Nowadays, we are not at all a participant in the remaining 15%. Because in Har-Ghar Jal, it has become, the project is around seven years old. So, now it has become everyone's cup of tea. And since we have gained experience for more than four years in the same project, so right now we are not aiming anything in Jal Jeevan Mission. We are aiming only in WTP, water pipelines, and STP and SN, sewerag

items.statement: Plan to purchase machinery for mining PQ requirements; funded via sanctioned NBFC/PSU bank loans
items.quote: But going forward, for the PQ requirement also, a few machineries need to be purchased. But right now the debt to equity ratio of the Company is quite good. And so we have already, we have sanctions from many of the private lenders, NBFC as well as PSU banks for this machinery. And the effect of all those things will not be much because already we are paying the higher charges which will get repla

items.statement: Preferential issue of ~Rs 100 crore sufficient for working capital needs until FY27
items.quote: And for the future projects which we are bidding or which we are planning to bid, so for that definitely some amou nt of working capital will be required for which we have already gone ahead for the fundraising through the preferential issue of shares. So that will suffice the requirement for at least FY '27. And then profits are getting plot back and the net worth of the Company is increasing. So

items.statement: Mining projects have working capital cycle of 45-50 days, half of typical infra projects
items.quote: Like in mining project, the working capital days will be somewhere around 45 to 50 days. Which is half the size of what working capital days is required in an infra project. So all these things were supporting. So we entered into mining segment.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations expected to turn positive in H2 FY27 as projects mature
items.quote: No, as of now, I think the cash flow from operations shall get positive from H2 FY '27 because no new fund raise or any big event is planned in the books. And all the projects which we have right now in hand are profitable. So, I think this thing will improve in H2 FY'27 only.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio 0.35x; credit rating upgraded to BBB+/A2 by Infomerics
items.quote: We continue to maintain a healthy financial profile with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.35x, which positions us well for sustainable future growth.

items.statement: Credit rating upgrade helps secure higher non-fund based limits (bank guarantees) for bidding
items.quote: One particular thing we need is bank guarantee for every project. For bidding we need guarantee, then performance guarantee and during the project we need retention bank guarantee, advanced bank guarantee and after the project also we need retention bank guarantee. So we don't expect any more funds from the banks. But we have to keep a proper mix, because we can get from PSU bank also. So whenever

items.statement: Mining order is OpEx for Coal India, ensuring timely payments; no Jal Jeevan Mission exposure
items.quote: So, once the project is, the nature of the project is in OpEx, then in that case, the chances of money getting stuck becomes very, very thin because it is an operating expense. Every month they are paying us like you are refueling your car, like you have to drive your car, you refuel your car and then you are driving it. So, that way we are quite safe in the biggest order which we have booked.

items.statement: No projects under Jal Jeevan Mission; all water projects under Namami Gange with no major payment delays
items.quote: Moreover, all these projects are coming up in, we don't have any projects from Jal Jeevan Mission. All the projects which we are taking up is Namami Gange scheme. items.statement: Medical automation product in oncology patient care management under development with AI partner trials ongoing
items.quote: So, the conversations are on. So, we are yet to finalize the AI partner for this technology for our product. So, currently, I think the conversations are on, the trials are on, work is in progress.

items.statement: Manufacturing sector adopting AI for smart factories; BFSI continues to lead digital transformation demand
items.quote: So digital transformation we are seeing in manufacturing. Yes, BFSI always leads. Their requirements are completely different. But what we are seeing is manufacturing adopting AI.

items.statement: Exploring partnerships with Israeli cyber security vendors for niche areas like drone and campus aerial security
items.quote: Yes. We are talking to a few cyber security vendors from Israel and these kind of areas. Well, that's what I said. You can expect some announcements very soon in niche areas.

items.statement: Plan to migrate from SME to main board listing within 18-24 months upon reaching Rs. 250 crore revenue
items.quote: Yes, that's the plan for the next 18 months to 24 months. That's what our pursuit is. So, once we reach the Rs. 250 crore mark, I think, yes.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense dropped from Rs. 8.41 crore to Rs. 3.12 crore due to reduced external consultant costs and in-house capability building
items.quote: And moreover, I think, as Sukanya well said, our execution costs have come down big time because we have built a framework within ourselves.

items.statement: Stock in trade/work in progress of Rs. 14.71 crore expected to close in H2 FY26 through milestone-based projects
items.quote: We hope to complete it this half year. There are multiple milestone-based projects that are in pipeline. And we expect it to close down in the H2, hopefully.

items.statement: Key operational challenge in international expansion is sourcing quality manpower requiring 18-24 months training investment
items.quote: See, operational challenge is getting quality manpower. That is for sure. With that reason, we are hiring and training people. Yes, those youngsters will get ready in 18 months, 24 months kind of a training.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY26 performance to be as good as H1 or slightly better
items.quote: We are at the end of the second month of the third quarter. Okay? So, we are doing equally good and we hope to perform as good as the first half or even a little better.

items.statement: Total capex for YEIDA facility is Rs.184.16 crores; Rs.53.64 crores deployed in H1 FY26 (Rs.7.07 crores from IPO, Rs.46.57 crores from internal accruals)
items.quote: The total facility is approximately Rs.184.16 crores and we are going on the track and we are making the good progress. And we have incurred already Rs.46.57 crores through internal accruals and Rs.7.07 crores from IPO proceeds.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 26.98% in H1 FY26 from 20.22% in H1 FY25; management says expansion is sustainable due to high-margin product mix, operational efficiency, cost control and pricing strategy
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 26.98% from 20.22% in the same period last year, reflecting improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Strong demand across all categories; domestic market contributed Rs.25.52 crores of incremental revenue; growth driven by new customers, new products and organic growth from existing customers
items.quote: Domestic market continue to be the key growth engine, contributing Rs.25.52 crores of the overall increase. Our growth was supported by the addition of new customers, addition of more products, and organic growth from existing customers.

items.statement: Business is sticky with no customer losses in decades; customers provide quarterly, half-yearly or annual schedules; new facility built under customer pressure for capacity
items.quote: Ours is a very sticky business. We are in the business of fragrances and flavors which are not the commodities. Our product becomes the identity of the end product and we are dealing with the best of the companies. In the last many decades of my business experience, touchwood, we have not lost any business.

items.statement: Raw material cost fluctuations managed through strategic sourcing and inventory management; benefits passed to customers to keep them competitive
items.quote: We at Sacheerome mitigate this through strategic sourcing and inventory management as I mentioned you earlier, and we will continue to do so effectively.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue split: fragrances Rs.75 crores, flavors Rs.1.46 crores; flavors expected to catch up in H2; dedicated flavor tower in new facility
items.quote: From the fragrances, we have generated around Rs.75 crores and the flavors we have generated Rs.1.46 crores. And the flavors segment which is a little sometimes seasonal and sometimes there is a demand, but we will be doing better than the previous year in the flavors also.

items.statement: Working capital cycle optimized to ~23 days from ~45 days previously
items.quote: One of the examples could be how we were able to optimize our working capital cycle as well which we have been able to operate at about 23-days compared to 45-days which we were doing in previous year.

items.statement: Term loan of Rs.60 crores from HDFC Bank secured for YEIDA facility; will be drawn after IPO proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: We have the term loan from HDFC Bank and we are fully covered. And, as per need base, we will withdraw... we will utilize the term loan. We will use the internal accruals and IPO first, then we will start using as and when required.

items.statement: Export market giving huge acceptance; Indian companies gaining global confidence; not taking share from global players but creating own space
items.quote: We will not say that we are taking away the business from our able competitors. We are creating our own space. Okay? And there is a much scope. Every day there are new launches of the new products, Indian products are doing so well, as well as we are looking at the export market also, which is also giving us a huge acceptance.

items.statement: Revenue grew 51.75% YoY to Rs.76.56 crores in H1 FY26; PAT Rs.14.94 crores
items.quote: We delivered robust revenue growth of 51.75%, with revenue from operations increasing to Rs.76.56 crores compared to Rs.50.45 crores in the same period last year, leading to an overall quantum increase of Rs.26.11 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization over 100% (above 95-97%); operational efficiency improvements and debottlenecking enabled volume growth despite constraints
items.quote: 760,000 is our current capacity. And, as you say, necessity is the mother of invention, we were under pressure and with our operational efficiency, we are able to produce all of our customer requirements.

items.statement: New facility revenue contribution expected from Q1 FY27; Q4 FY26 production start will be very small
items.quote: The last quarter will be the start of the production at our new facility. But let me tell you, they will start from there maybe, but it is very small, it will take some time, but at the same time, we will continue to maintain from our existing facility and there will be no loss of any business. From the first quarter of the next financial year, the revenue will start coming from the new facility a

items.statement: Management confident EBITDA margin of ~25% sustainable despite new capacity ramp-up; cites top-line growth, product mix, efficiency, cost control and pricing strategy
items.quote: As our top line grows, as our turnover grows, and which we are sure, I do not think it is a forward-looking statement, but I will say we are confident and we will be able to maintain our EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Margins higher than listed peers due to R&D innovation, qualified talent, quality products, regulatory compliance, deep customer relationships and proprietary technologies like Sach Veda
items.quote: Our competitive edge comes from a combination of R&D innovation, highly qualified human resources, high-quality standard products, regulatory compliance, and deep customer relationships. We provide tailor-made solutions aligned with consumer preferences, which help us to maintain the better profit margins.

items.statement: Multi-generational team with 40-45 years promoter experience; 54 R&D personnel; R&D is backbone of business
items.quote: I am in this industry myself for over 40-years, 45-years and I belong to third generation, Dhruv belongs to fourth generation, many people in our company are from second generation, their father was working, their son is working, their mother was working, their daughter is working. And it is like a family.

items.statement: Raw material supply risks (fire at BSF, COVID, China supply, climatic scarcity) managed through advance inventory planning and supplier relationships
items.quote: There are three turbulences we have faced, everybody in the industry, not only we. First of all, there was a fire in BSF, then there was COVID, then, China products, and sometimes, due to the climatic conditions, due to some reasons, there is scarcity. But, we plan our inventory very well and we plan in advance.

items.statement: Targets 25% CAGR revenue growth over next 3-4 years, aiming to double business size
items.quote: So, we have already given a guideline. So, we see the next 3 to 4 years, we are looking for double the size of the current business. So, with a 25% CAGR year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets 100 bps EBITDA margin improvement in short term
items.quote: So, madam, we are looking for a short term 100 basis point improvements in EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.62%, standalone at 9%
items.quote: EBITDA increased to 19.92 crores, it's up 13% H-on-H, so with the margin at 8.62%.

items.statement: IFM margins around 2-2.5%, hard services higher than soft services
items.quote: and other verticals also. So, if we compare the facility management business, the margins are thin in the facility business. And if we compare with the competitors, the margins come to around 2% to 2.5

items.statement: Converting clients from soft to hard services to improve margins
items.quote: Our plan is that only. And we have already initiated that step. And we have also converted few clients from soft services to hard services.

items.statement: Business pipeline over 1,200 crores provides strong visibility
items.quote: And our business pipeline of over 1,200 crores provides strong visibility for the upcoming quarter.

items.statement: Outsourcing penetration increasing across manufacturing, IT, ITES, retail sectors
items.quote: So, there are immense opportunity for the IFM services because in India, whether it is a manufacturing sector or maybe IT, ITES or maybe the retail sector, basically, they want to focus on their core activities.

items.statement: Entered pharmaceutical sector with good opportunity and expertise
items.quote: Apart from that, we have started in the pharmaceutical sector. So, there is a very good opportunity and we have the expertise to deliver as well.

items.statement: IFM contributes ~60% revenue, employee transportation and production support have better EBITDA margins
items.quote: So, if you see the mainly IFM business have a major revenue side that is the top line which contribute almost 60% of the business. And if we see the margin wise, it's employee transportation contributes better, that has contributed.

items.statement: Cross-selling adds revenue but margins remain same per service line
items.quote: So, margin enhancement for the cross-selling, it's like, definitely it will add, the margin will remain the same for the services we are offering, but revenue, definitely it will help on the top line.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute 50% revenue, but serve 140+ clients with pan-India multi-location contracts
items.quote: Yes, these clients are contributing first top 10 clients are contributing 50%. But apart from that, also, we have a clientele of almost 140 clients, like 50% contribution is from those clients.

items.statement: Key multi-service clients include Tata Motors, Volkswagen, JCB, Thermax across IFM, transport, food solutions
items.quote: Yes. So, for Tata Motors, we are giving the PAN India services for IFM and the employee transportation as well. Similarly, for Volkswagen facility management and the employee transportation services, these are the top clients.

items.statement: Employee transport capex only for 5-year exclusive contracts with back-to-back vehicle financing
items.quote: So, whenever there is a contract which has a 5 year duration and exclusivity with the clients, then only we invest in the vehicles and that will be have a back-to-back locking agreement for 5 years.

items.statement: Expanding geographic presence in North (Delhi NCR) and South (Chennai, Karnataka) manufacturing hubs
items.quote: So, if you see that in South region, so almost all the manufacturing industry is located in Chennai region. So, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, there we are focusing a lot of industry bases over there. And in the North region, the Delhi NCR, there we are focusing.

items.statement: New regions expected to contribute minimum 30% of future growth
items.quote: New region if you see that minimum 30% growth will come from the new region.

items.statement: Receivable days stable at 85-95 days due to MNC payment terms of 60-75 days post-invoice
items.quote: So, if you see, madam, the receivable days, it comes around 90 to 95 days, even in FY25 and current also. So, the receivables are coming into the 3 months, that is a cycle.

items.statement: Debt levels to remain at current levels even at 800-1,000 crore revenue scale
items.quote: So, when we close that business of 800 to 1,000 crores, the margins will improve and the debt levels will remain the same levels what we have at currently.

items.statement: Signed MoU for acquisition in South, acquisition not yet closed; evaluating more targets selectively
items.quote: So, no, Amit, we have just signed a MoU with them for acquisition. It's, acquisition has not been closed.

items.statement: Inorganic growth selective for geographic expansion or similar business segments
items.quote: So, the main expansion or improvements in business comes from organic. In that we are targeting the inorganic at a selective basis on the specific geographical expansion.

items.statement: Set up training division for skilled manpower sourcing and placement across pan-India network
items.quote: So, we have also set up a training division from where we are training people and placing them to our clients to give the quality of services.

items.statement: Client retention rate 85%, average client tenure 25 years with contract renewals
items.quote: I should say that we have an impressive 85% client retention rate. So, can I know, what initiatives are helping you to deepen the relationship and increase the wallet share within?

items.statement: Manpower cost 62-63% of revenue, rises proportionally with revenue in IFM business
items.quote: The manpower cost is directly related to our business because we are like in IFM business, which is mainly a manpower-oriented business. So, when the revenues increase, the manpower cost proportionately will get increased. So, it will rise into the similar percent of 62% to 63% of the total revenues.

items.statement: Long-term contracts enable year-on-year margin improvements
items.quote: So, if we have a contract constant for long-term, we definitely margin get year-on-year improvements.

items.statement: Clients shifting to single-vendor integrated contracts for admin and support services
items.quote: Yes, that was the trend like currently the market are shifting to single service provider for all the services. So, if you see the portfolio of services which we have, that is all related to the admin services and support services.

items.statement: Adopted Pazo technology platform for digital checklists, SAP workflows, automation and data-driven processes
items.quote: So, we have the Pazo technology which we have opted so far.

items.statement: Corporate food solutions expanding via in-house kitchen model (no capex) starting in West zone
items.quote: So, nowadays, like company has their in-house kitchen. So, we don't have to invest or set up a kitchen for them. So, they have their in-house kitchen. So, those opportunities we are trying to tap and wherever means we can expand that into the various regions in India. So, our focus basically first for this food solution is the west zone because that way our revenue is hardly 1.5 crores and all mon

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance INR2,600-2,700 crore with PAT margin 11-12%
items.quote: FY ‘26, we keep a guidance of about INR2,600 crores to INR2,700 crores as a top-line guidance with a PAT margin of about 11% to 12

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR3,100-3,200 crore with PAT margin 11-12%
items.quote: For FY ‘27, which is next financial year, we keep a top-line target of about INR3,100 crores to INR3,200 crores with a PAT margin of again 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Total order book INR9,135 crore split energy INR5,869 crore and telecom INR3,266 crore
items.quote: So, as Rajeev was explaining, we have a total order book of INR9,135 crores, with the bifurcation of energy and telecom.

items.statement: Energy order book expected to increase by INR8,000-10,000 crore by end of FY26
items.quote: Going forward, we see our energy projects order book to increase by INR8,000 to INR10,000 crores before end of this financial year.

items.statement: Full year FY26 PAT margin expected to stabilize at 11.5%
items.quote: So, the current number of 13.61% will get stabilized at 11.5% for the complete financial year.

items.statement: Telecom product EBITDA margin 15-18%, EPC 13-14%; Energy product 15%, EPC 10-12%
items.quote: The telecom products has a n EBITDA margin of about 15% to 18%. The EPC has a margin of about 13% to 14%. And on the energy side, as we have started recently, the product margin is about 15%. EPC margin is about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Annuity O&M business EBITDA margin 80-85%
items.quote: So, these annuity business, the revenue, the EBITDA margin is about 85%, 80 to 85%.

items.statement: BESS facility expansion from 5 to 10 GWh requires additional INR100 crore capex
items.quote: Plus, for expansion of another 5 gigawatt hour, we need to spend another, say, INR100 crores more, because the fixed installations like the factory building is all common.

items.statement: IPO funds INR630 crore allocated for developer project, INR150 crore already spent from internal sources
items.quote: And we have already spent about INR150 crores, say, either from the debt sources or from the internal accruals for the project. The IPO funds, as it is, as it is received only in October, we are yet to spend from the IPO funds for this project.

items.statement: Current BESS orders 4.0-4.3 GWh, expected to cross 6-7 GWh by end FY26 and 10 GWh by facility commissioning
items.quote: So, at this point, we have orders for more than 4.0 to 4.3 gigawatt. And by end of this financial year, we are expecting orders to cross beyond 6 to 7 gigawatt.

items.statement: Strong demand for BESS from state discoms and central PSUs for EPC projects, private customers for product supply
items.quote: The projects that we're executing, which are EPC and developer projects, are usually state discoms or the public sector companies like the SECI or the NTPC, whereas we also have private customers where we only manufacture and supply our equipment.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: Energy INR500-550 crore, Telecom INR200-250 crore ICT, rest pure telecom
items.quote: And this year, we expect this energy segment to touch about INR500 to INR550 crores for this financial year, against a target of INR2,600 crores

items.statement: Won SECI BESS EPC INR1,159 crore, TTL O&M INR185 crore, MAHAGENCO solar EPC INR920 crore
items.quote: We have won three major projects, that include one project from SECI for battery energy storage system for INR1,159 crores for 600 /1,200 megawatt-hour battery energy storage system supply and installation, EPC project. We have also won a O&M contract with the telecom company TTL, Tata Teleservices, for INR185 crores for a period of three years. We have also recently won an EPC project for solar w

items.statement: Net working capital INR970 crore as of Sep 2025, expected to reduce by March 2026 as EPC projects complete and retention money releases
items.quote: So, the net current asset, we have about INR970 crores for this as on 30th September. So, which is expected to go down because of the project nature that we have, the EPC projects, which is at the verge of completion.

items.statement: Total debt INR150 crore, debt-equity 0.11x, net worth INR1,331 crore, cash/FD INR213 crore as of Sep 2025
items.quote: The debt, that is the company's debt, overall debt stands at about INR150 crores, and we have a debt equity ratio of about 0.11x. Again, the company has a net worth of about INR1,331 crores with a cash and FD balances of about INR213 crores.

items.statement: IPO proceeds received October 2025, INR630 crore for developer project equity, INR120 crore for two more projects
items.quote: So out of the INR820 crores of the IPO issue, INR630 crores goes for one specific project. So, beyond this, there are two more projects which are already signed off. There, we would be putting balance of IPO funds, which is about INR120 crores net of the issue expenses.

items.statement: Developer model 4 projects INR3,300 crore to yield INR420 crore annual revenue at 85% EBITDA from FY28, INR150 crore in FY27
items.quote: Four projects which we have as on date is about INR3,300 crores. This is expected to give an annual revenue of about INR420 crores without GST and EBITDA margin of a round 85%. So, with this, the next financial year, this particular number is going to come from FY28. But from FY27, we'll have a portion of it coming to the P&L.

items.statement: Annuity O&M order book INR3,300 crore yielding INR412 crore annual revenue, expected to grow to INR1,000 crore
items.quote: Yes. So, standing today, the order book that we have for this annuity business is about INR3,300 crores, which will give an overall top line of about INR412 crores every year. And this is expected to grow up to, say, INR1,000 crores in the upcoming years.

items.statement: Lithium-ion cells 50-60% of BESS cost, imported from China with back-to-back price locking; 5% customs duty vs 20% on finished goods
items.quote: So, the import content is the cell alone, which would – the battery cell alone will come to about 50% to 60% of the total cost. The remaining ancillaries are all manufactured in India, and we do the manufacturing and assembly here.

items.statement: MSEDCL project includes VGF of INR27 lakh per MWh paid in installments: 10% advance, 45% on commissioning, 45% over 3 years
items.quote: The developer model of this comes with a VGF of about 27 lakhs per megawatt hour, again. So, these are the components, I would say, if you want. I think I have answered your question. So, the VGF is like, say, it would be paid in different installments, like, say, 10% is paid on advance, 45% is paid on commissioning of the plant and the balance 45 % is paid over a period of three, next to three ye

items.statement: BESS competition increasing with infra companies bidding aggressively; PACE has cost advantage from in-house manufacturing and backward integration
items.quote: There is huge demand and huge competition that has started coming in over the last two, three months now. And there is a lot of infra and other types of companies coming in to bid for such projects. But as PACE, we have an advantage where we have the control of the product.

items.statement: Recent BESS tenders bidding below INR2 lakh/MW/month seen as unsustainable, expected to correct in coming months
items.quote: But we see that that numbers are closer to impossible and because of which this will go through a correction over the next few months.

items.statement: Kenya and Africa expansion driven by telecom infrastructure growth, supplying power equipment and hybrid solutions
items.quote: Kenya and Africa in the last few years have invested a lot in the telecom industry and have expanded a lot in the telecom industry. So, we see a big need and we've been working in the past few years, in expanding the telecom side, providing our power equipments, doing the supply and installation of our power equipment and the hybrid solutions.

items.statement: Workforce 1,500+ on-roll and 1,500+ off-roll employees across India
items.quote: We have a strong workforce of 1,500 -plus people across India on roll and more than 1,500 off roll.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of minimum 15% year-on-year; FY27 revenue target around INR300 crores
items.quote: So, FY '27, probably, we have -- as we have already given some targets, like 15% year-on-year growth minimum. And CAGR, it was. So, we will be probably around 300 or around that line.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 10% for full FY26; expects further improvement in FY27
items.quote: Yes, yes. We would be able to. This was just lowered down due to we have been shifting our pultrusion process from rented to the new premises. So, it affected our operational efficiency somewhat and the revenue also. Also, the US part somewhat was affected. So, ultimately, H2 would be much more better than the H1.

items.statement: Carbon fiber project machinery investment between INR8-10 crores; rebar five lines capex approximately INR7.5 crores including bend machines
items.quote: So, on the carbon fiber side, probably our i nvestment is going to be between INR8 crores to INR10 crores This is only machineries and then there are other ancillaries and all that

items.statement: New Mehsana facility 51,671 sq m operational end of Sep 2025; full 22,000 metric tons capacity over next few quarters; targeting over 70% utilization by FY27
items.quote: The unit has become operational at the end of September 25 and is currently in the scale-up phase with full 22,000 metrics and capacity expected to be achieved over the next few quarters.

items.statement: FRP rebar: 2 lines installed, scaling to 5 lines by end FY26; each line ~300 MT/year generating INR5-7 crores
items.quote: So, each machine has a capacity of approximately 300 metric tons a year and that would generate approximately anywhere between, depends on the diameter, but it will generate probably around INR5 to INR6 crores. Between INR5 to INR7 crores, I would say, depends on the diameter per machine.

items.statement: Carbon fiber pilot plant expected installed capacity by end FY26; approvals 8-12 months; full scale-up FY28
items.quote: We are hoping that by end FY26, we have the installed capacity for carbon fiber product. And going forward, all these carbon fiber is more technical product and the approval is also there. So, we will start approval process and as we go forward with approvals, we can add on capacities in carbon fiber as well.

items.statement: Current order book INR45 crores, executable in FY26
items.quote: So, there is no bifurcation right now with respect to customized or not, but our current order book is INR45 crores.

items.statement: FRP rebar and carbon fiber margins projected at least 4% higher than existing business; carbon fiber higher than rebar
items.quote: I think the margins are higher, at least by -- this is what our projected are, by 4% than our existing line of business, at least by 4%.

items.statement: Pricing flattish in H1; some specialty chemical raw material volatility; potential domestic price increase if anti-dumping duty on glass fiber imposed
items.quote: So, the pricing is more of a flattish right now. There are certain raw materials which are specialty chemicals has been little bit volatile. But overall, the international global scenario has been flattish with respect to price of FRP products and with respect to the raw material of the major raw materials.

items.statement: FRP rebar market acceptance growing fast; government promotion by MoRTH/NHAI; customers adopt gradually per project
items.quote: Market has been receptive with respect to FRP rebar. It's been almost just two years since the government has started promoting this product and started accepting this product. And the feedback from the market is also very positive.

items.statement: Key rebar clients: Shaligram (Ahmedabad developers), IRB (highways), L&T; optic fiber rods to Apar Industries, KEC, OFS/Furukawa; EPC contractors and end-users across sectors
items.quote: In Ahmedabad, there are a few developers. One of the big names is Shaligram. And then, on highways, IRB, we are already supplying in IRB. I think that is a good, big enough name to address the highway developers. We are also supplying to L&T.

items.statement: FRP rebar competitors: Jindal Advanced Materials (JSW group) and Rathi Steel (Delhi) with ~10+ machines combined; Aeron to be among few large manufacturers with 5 lines
items.quote: One is Jindal Advanced Material, which is a JSW group company. then there is Rathi Steel, they are based in Delhi. I t hink these two have good enough capabilities right now at this point. There are other manufacturers as well with one machines or two machines, but these two are having good capabilities. And probably with our five lines, we will be among the few large manufacturers

items.statement: MoRTH/NHAI promoting FRP rebar adoption; guidelines issued encouraging use; anti-dumping duty hearing on glass fiber products may raise domestic raw material prices
items.quote: This is further supported by growing regulatory momentum, most notably the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways under Mr. Nitin Gadkari and NHAI, which has actively promoted the adoption of FRP rebar and issued guidelines encouraging its use.

items.statement: Exports 55% of H1 revenue (down from 61% due to plant shift); supplying to 39 countries; Western countries stronger demand; USD/INR at 89
items.quote: Export revenue contributed 55% of the total revenue during the first half, underscoring the strength of our international presence and brand acceptance.

items.statement: Receivables typically 60-90 days; >6 months receivables increased FY24 to FY25 but improving in H2 FY26
items.quote: Generally, it is between 60 to 90 days in general.

items.statement: Long-term debt for buildings; short-term working capital ~INR25 crores; cash ~INR40 crores from IPO proceeds; no plan to prepay long-term debt with IPO cash
items.quote: Long term, which is our debt for the term loans we have taken from the bank, which is for current buildings, which we have achieved right now for pultrusion and molded. And short terms will be around INR25 crores, which is plus minus according to the utilization of the working capital.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR53 crores; total gross block after full implementation ~INR110-120 crores including term loans and internal accruals
items.quote: So overall, if we talk about our gross block in total with whole implementation, let's say total term loan plus our internal accruals would be INR33 crores, our gross block till '25, it was INR35 crore s and INR53 crore s of total of IPO proceedings. So overall, it would go around INR110 crores or INR20 crores total gross block after complete implementation

items.statement: FRP rebar NSR assumption INR140/kg; each rebar line ~300 MT/year at INR5-7 crores revenue
items.quote: Right now, we are taking INR140 a kg.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty affecting exports; mitigation via new non-US customers if deal fails; carbon fiber approvals 8-12 months delay revenue
items.quote: Meanwhile, if the tariff, the deal does not get through, then we are, of course, we have already started to talk to outside US customers to improve their offtake from us, basically. And we are -- we will be adding new customers to offset that loss of revenue in that case, in the tariff deal…

items.statement: Integrated 360-degree FRP provider: pultruded profiles, molded grating, UV-cured FRP rods, CFRP rebars; adding carbon fiber pultrusion (wind blades, HTLS core rods) and autoclave (auto, rail, defense)
items.quote: These high -performance, high -margin composites aimed at sectors such as wind energy, railways and automo tive represent the next step in broadening our advanced material portfolio

items.statement: Dev Accelerator (DevX) public issue of Rs. 143.35 crore strengthened balance sheet; DevIT stake diluted from 23% to 17%; exceptional gain of Rs. 93.55 crore recognized
items.quote: The public issue of our subsidiary, Dev Accelerator Limited, worth Rs. 143.35 crore, was also an important milestone.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty in US (tariffs), Canada (trade treaty), driving focus on India market sustainability and high-value asset creation
items.quote: We don't know what is going on with North America. We don't know what are our tariff implications on IT services business, as far as the U.S. is concerned. We don't know about our trade treaty with Canada.

items.statement: Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra offering data center incentives; in final talks with data center creator for management services
items.quote: in GIFT. In Gujarat, government has started providing incentives to data centers. Similarly, in states like Chhattisgarh, states like Maharashtra, they are also offering more incentives to data centers

items.statement: GIFT City ecosystem play: DevX center positioned to provide end-to-end solutions (real estate, IT, compliance) for GCCs entering GIFT City
items.quote: we are creating an ecosystem where we will be providing end-to-end solutions to those companies entering in GIFT City, starting from real estate to IT to compliance, everything that will be under one banner.

items.statement: Revenue will increase in FY26; second half revenue will be high and more than expected
items.quote: Revenue will increase. Second half revenue will be high. Revenue will be more than expected.

items.statement: EBITDA margin will remain intact for FY26
items.quote: Yes, margin will be intact.

items.statement: Competition will reduce in the livestock feed sector
items.quote: Competition will reduce.

items.statement: Overall margin is good; value-added products carry superior high margin potential
items.quote: Overall margin is good.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility managed through buffer stock policy and daily averaging; no impact over 12 months
items.quote: Overall, ma'am, there is no impact from around the year. And we already keep concentrating on it. And there is daily average of it. And there is no effect in the period of 12 months.

items.statement: Working capital cycle will reduce; working capital has increased compared to last year
items.quote: Working capital cycle will reduce. Working capital has increased compared to last year.

items.statement: Borrowings increased due to inventory buildup; some leverage must be borne
items.quote: Concentration is like that. Some things we have to bear.

items.statement: Farmer education and advisory programs will be launched to increase scientific adoption
items.quote: Farmer education. We will launch farmer education. We will bring that into effect.

items.statement: H1 FY26 total income Rs 2,369.51 lakhs; EBITDA Rs 327.48 lakhs at 13.82% margin; PAT Rs 204.56 lakhs at 8.63% net margin
items.quote: For the half year financial '26, total income was Rs. 2,369.51 lakhs. EBITDA stood at Rs. 327.48 lakhs with a margin of 13.82% and PAT increased to Rs. 204.56 lakhs with a net margin of 8.63%.

items.statement: Non-GMO compliance maintained; no GMO material used
items.quote: We do not use GMO material.
